items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · अन्तरक्रियात्मक प्रयोग The ER visualiser — what a cardinality actually means What you will learn: the difference between one-to-many and many-to-many, shown in rows rather than in notation — and why only one of them needs a third table. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: एक–धेरै र धेरै–धेरैको फरक, चिन्हमा होइन पङ्क्तिमा देखेर — र किन तीमध्ये एउटालाई मात्र तेस्रो तालिका चाहिन्छ। What to notice The notation at the top barely changes between the three buttons — one letter. The rows underneath change completely, and that is the real difference. On 1:M, read the note under the list: every course points back at exactly one student. Now press M:N. The same note changes — Maths is now reached from two students. Both directions are "many", and that is the whole definition. Only M:N produces a junction table. Watch it appear, and notice it holds nothing but two foreign keys — one row per link, which is exactly what the relationship is. माथिको चिन्ह तीन बटनबीच झन्डै बदलिँदैन — एउटा अक्षर मात्र। तलका पङ्क्ति भने पूरै बदलिन्छन्, र वास्तविक फरक त्यही हो। 1:M मा सूचीमुनिको टिप्पणी पढ्नुहोस्: हरेक विषयले ठ्याक्कै एउटा विद्यार्थी देखाउँछ। अब M:N थिच्नुहोस् — Maths अब दुई विद्यार्थीबाट जोडिन्छ। दुवैतर्फ "धेरै", र पूरा परिभाषा यही हो। M:N ले मात्र junction तालिका बनाउँछ; त्यसमा दुई foreign key बाहेक केही हुँदैन। Practise the judgement
items.ne: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Read the sentence, name the cardinality What you will learn: to test both directions every time, which is the one habit that separates a right answer from a guess. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: सधैं दुवै दिशा जाँच्ने बानी — सही उत्तर र अनुमानबीचको फरक यही एउटा बानीले पार्छ। How to use this For each case, read the two sentences as two separate questions: how many on the right for one on the left? and then how many on the left for one on the right? Only after both do you have a cardinality. The last two cases are the ones worth slowing down for. One uses softer wording — "may be treated by several" is still "many". The other describes a relationship between entities that also relate in other ways: judge the relationship that is named, not the entities. हरेक केसमा दुई वाक्यलाई दुई छुट्टै प्रश्न मानेर पढ्नुहोस्: बायाँको एउटालाई दायाँ कति? अनि दायाँको एउटालाई बायाँ कति? दुवैपछि मात्र cardinality थाहा हुन्छ। अन्तिम दुई केसमा बिस्तारै जानुहोस् — एउटामा शब्द नरम छ, अर्कोमा नाम दिइएको सम्बन्ध हेर्नुपर्छ, इन्टिटी होइन। Example 1 Choosing the cardinality from a sentence Question: decide the mapping cardinality for each, and give the reason. Working "Each citizen has one citizenship number, and each number belongs to one citizen." → 1:1 both directions are "one" "A class contains many students, but each student is in only one class." → 1:M many one way, one the other way "A student takes many courses, and a course is taken by many students." → M:N many BOTH ways Always test both directions. A sentence that only tells you one direction has not told you the cardinality. "A class has many students" alone could be 1:M or M:N — you have to ask whether a student can be in two classes. सधैं दुवै दिशा जाँच्नुहोस्। एउटा दिशा मात्र बताउने वाक्यले cardinality बताएकै हुँदैन। "एउटा कक्षामा धेरै विद्यार्थी" भन्ने मात्रले 1:M कि M:N भन्न मिल्दैन — एउटा विद्यार्थी दुई कक्षामा हुन सक्छ कि भनी सोध्नुपर्छ। 2.6 Keys in DBMS {{dia:keyTypes}} Each key is a narrowing of the one above it. Every primary key is a candidate key, and every candidate key is a super key — but not the reverse. हरेक कुञ्जी माथिकोभन्दा साँघुरो हुँदै जान्छ। हरेक primary key एउटा candidate key हो, र हरेक candidate key एउटा super key — तर उल्टो होइन। The two rules a primary key must obey A primary key must be unique — no two rows may share its value — and it must be NOT NULL — it can never be left empty. Those two rules are what allow a row to be found reliably. A foreign key is different in kind. It is not about identifying a row in its own table; it is a column whose value must already exist as a primary key in another table. That rule is what links two tables together, and it is called referential integrity. A foreign key may be NULL — Gita has no class yet — and it may repeat, since many students share one class. A primary key may do neither. Primary key ले पालना गर्नुपर्ने दुई नियम Primary key अद्वितीय हुनुपर्छ — दुई पङ्क्तिको मान उही हुन नहुने — र NOT NULL हुनुपर्छ — कहिल्यै खाली छाड्न नहुने। यी दुई नियमले नै पङ्क्ति भरपर्दो रूपमा खोज्न दिन्छन्। Foreign key फरक किसिमको हो। यसले आफ्नै तालिकाको पङ्क्ति चिनाउँदैन; यो त्यस्तो स्तम्भ हो जसको मान अर्को तालिकाको primary key मा पहिले नै हुनैपर्छ। यही नियमले दुई तालिका जोड्छ, र यसलाई referential integrity भनिन्छ। Foreign key NULL हुन सक्छ — गीताको कक्षा अझै छैन — र दोहोरिन पनि सक्छ, किनभने धेरै विद्यार्थीको कक्षा एउटै हुन्छ। Primary key ले यी दुवै गर्न पाउँदैन। Example 2 Identifying every key in a table Question: a Student table holds roll, reg_no, name, class_id. Both roll and reg_no are unique. class_id exists in the Class table. Name every key. Four kinds of key are being asked for. Before you open this, commit to one number: how many candidate keys does this table have? If your answer is 1, look at the question again. चार किसिमका key सोधिएका छन्। खोल्नुअघि एउटा सङ्ख्या भन्नुहोस्: यो तालिकामा कति वटा candidate key छन्? जवाफ १ आयो भने प्रश्न फेरि हेर्नुहोस्। Step 1 — find everything that identifies a row uniquely. These are the super keys, and there are many, because adding spare columns to a unique column keeps it unique: Working {roll} unique ✓ {reg_no} unique ✓ {roll, name} unique ✓ (roll alone was enough) {reg_no, class_id} unique ✓ (reg_no alone was enough) {name} NOT unique — two students may share a name Step 2 — strip out the spare columns. A super key with nothing unnecessary left in it is a candidate key: {roll} and {reg_no}. Step 3 — choose one. The school uses roll, so that is the primary key. The candidate key not chosen becomes the alternate key. Answer Super keys {roll}, {reg_no}, {roll, name}, … many Candidate keys {roll}, {reg_no} Primary key {roll} (chosen) Alternate key {reg_no} (the one not chosen) Foreign key {class_id} → Class.class_id The examiner is checking that you know these are nested, not five unrelated things. Every primary key is a candidate key, and every candidate key is a super key. Saying so in one line is often worth a mark by itself. परीक्षकले यी पाँच असम्बन्धित कुरा होइनन्, एकभित्र अर्को हुन् भन्ने जान्नुभएको छ कि छैन हेर्छन्। हरेक primary key एउटा candidate key हो, र हरेक candidate key एउटा super key। यही एक हरफले प्रायः एक अंक दिन्छ। Mistakes that cost marks here Calling a weak entity "unimportant". It means the entity has no key of its own and must borrow its owner's. Draw it with a double rectangle. कमजोर इन्टिटीलाई "महत्त्वहीन" भन्नु। यसको अर्थ आफ्नो कुञ्जी नभएको र मालिकको कुञ्जी लिनुपर्ने भन्ने हो। दोहोरो आयतले कोर्नुहोस्। Answering "many students in a class" as M:N. Check the other direction: a student is in one class, so it is 1:M. "एउटा कक्षामा धेरै विद्यार्थी" लाई M:N भन्नु। अर्को दिशा जाँच्नुहोस्: विद्यार्थी एउटै कक्षामा हुन्छ, त्यसैले 1:M। Confusing degree with cardinality. Degree counts the entities in a relationship; cardinality counts how many rows link to how many. Degree र cardinality मिसाउनु। Degree ले सम्बन्धका इन्टिटी गन्छ; cardinality ले कति पङ्क्ति कतिसँग जोडिन्छ भन्छ। Underlining nothing in an ER diagram. The key attribute must be underlined — that is the notation for a primary key, and a marker looks for it. ER चित्रमा कुनै पनि नाममुनि रेखा नकोर्नु। कुञ्जी एट्रिब्युटमुनि रेखा हुनैपर्छ — primary key को चिन्ह त्यही हो। Writing a relationship as a noun. A diamond holds a verb: ENROLS, TEACHES, CONTAINS — not "enrolment". सम्बन्धलाई नामपदमा लेख्नु। चतुर्भुजभित्र क्रियापद हुन्छ: ENROLS, TEACHES, CONTAINS — "enrolment" होइन। Weak means no key of its own, not unimportant. Double rectangle, double diamond. Weak भनेको आफ्नो कुञ्जी नभएको, महत्त्वहीन होइन। दोहोरो आयत, दोहोरो हीरा। Exam focus — what is asked from this unit This unit is examined mostly by drawing. The commonest question gives you two or three sentences describing a small system and asks for an ER diagram — entities, attributes with the key underlined, a relationship named as a verb, and the cardinality marked on both lines. Marks are given for each of those four things separately, so a diagram missing its cardinalities still earns most of them. Draw it big, and label everything. यो युनिट प्रायः कोरेर जाँचिन्छ। सामान्य प्रश्नले दुई–तीन वाक्यमा सानो प्रणाली वर्णन गरेर ER चित्र माग्छ — इन्टिटी, कुञ्जीमुनि रेखासहितका एट्रिब्युट, क्रियापदमा नाम दिइएको सम्बन्ध, र दुवै रेखामा cardinality। यी चार कुरालाई छुट्टाछुट्टै अंक हुन्छ, त्यसैले cardinality छुटे पनि धेरैजसो अंक आउँछ। ठूलो कोर्नुहोस् र सबैमा नाम लेख्नुहोस्। 2 marks Practice question Define entity and attribute with one example of each. इन्टिटी र एट्रिब्युटको परिभाषा एक–एक उदाहरणसहित दिनुहोस्। Show the answer An entity is a real-world object or concept about which data is stored, and which can be identified distinctly. Example: a STUDENT. It is drawn as a rectangle and becomes a table. An attribute is a property or characteristic of an entity. Example: the student's name. It is drawn as an ellipse and becomes a column. दुवैको परिभाषा, एक–एक उदाहरण, र चाहेमा कुन आकारले कोरिन्छ भन्ने पनि। 4 marks Practice question Explain the three mapping cardinalities with a suitable example of each. तीनै mapping cardinality लाई उपयुक्त उदाहरणसहित व्याख्या गर्नुहोस्। Show the answer ONE-TO-ONE (1:1) Each A relates to at most one B, and each B to at most one A. Example: a citizen and a citizenship number. ONE-TO-MANY (1:M) One A relates to many B, but each B to only one A. Example: a class contains many students; each student is in one class. MANY-TO-MANY (M:N) Many A relate to many B, in both directions. Example: a student takes many courses, and a course is taken by many students. → needs a third (junction) table. One mark per cardinality with its example, and the fourth for stating that M:N requires an extra table. हरेक cardinality र उदाहरणलाई एक–एक अंक, र M:N लाई थप तालिका चाहिन्छ भनेकोमा चौथो अंक। 4 marks Practice question A library keeps books and members. A member may borrow many books, and a book may be borrowed by many members over time. Draw an ER diagram for this. एउटा पुस्तकालयले पुस्तक र सदस्यको अभिलेख राख्छ। एक सदस्यले धेरै पुस्तक लिन सक्छन्, र एउटै पुस्तक समयक्रममा धेरै सदस्यले लिन सक्छन्। यसको ER चित्र कोर्नुहोस्। Show the answer (member_id) (name) (book_id) (title) \ / \ / ┌──────────┐ M ◇ BORROWS ◇ N ┌────────┐ │ MEMBER │──────────────────────│ BOOK │ └──────────┘ └────────┘ member_id and book_id are UNDERLINED (key attributes) BORROWS is written in a diamond, as a verb M and N are marked on the two lines One mark for the two entities as rectangles, one for the attributes as ellipses with the keys underlined, one for the relationship in a diamond named as a verb, and one for the M:N cardinality marked on both lines. आयतमा दुई इन्टिटीलाई एक अंक, कुञ्जीमुनि रेखासहित दीर्घवृत्तका एट्रिब्युटलाई एक, चतुर्भुजमा क्रियापद रूपको सम्बन्धलाई एक, र दुवै रेखामा M:N लेखेकोमा एक। Key points to revise
items.ne: — दोहोर्‍याउनुपर्ने मुख्य बुँदा

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: contains
items.ne: समावेश गर्छ

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: enrols in
items.ne: भर्ना हुन्छ

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: One-to-one
items.ne: एक–एक

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Each row on the left is joined to at most ONE row on the right, and the other way round too. Both directions are "one".
items.ne: बायाँको हरेक पङ्क्ति दायाँको बढीमा एउटासँग जोडिन्छ, र उल्टो पनि त्यस्तै। दुवैतर्फ "एक"।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Two tables. The foreign key can sit in either one.
items.ne: दुई तालिका। Foreign key जुनसुकैमा राख्न सकिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: One-to-many
items.ne: एक–धेरै

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: One row on the left joins to MANY on the right — but each right row goes back to only ONE left row. The "many" side is one direction only.
items.ne: बायाँको एउटा पङ्क्ति दायाँका धेरैसँग जोडिन्छ — तर दायाँको हरेक पङ्क्ति बायाँको एउटैसँग फर्किन्छ। "धेरै" एकतर्फी मात्र हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Two tables. The foreign key goes in the MANY side. This is the most common relationship in real databases.
items.ne: दुई तालिका। Foreign key "धेरै" तर्फ जान्छ। वास्तविक डाटाबेसमा सबैभन्दा धेरै आउने सम्बन्ध यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Many-to-many
items.ne: धेरै–धेरै

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Many on the left join to many on the right, BOTH ways. Look at the lines: they cross. No single foreign key can record that.
items.ne: बायाँका धेरै दायाँका धेरैसँग, दुवैतर्फ। रेखाहरू हेर्नुहोस् — काटिन्छन्। यसलाई एउटै foreign key ले राख्न सक्दैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: THREE tables. A third — a junction table — is needed, holding one row per link. This is the consequence you must be able to state.
items.ne: तीन तालिका। बीचमा एउटा junction तालिका चाहिन्छ, हरेक जोडका लागि एक पङ्क्ति। परीक्षामा भन्न सक्नुपर्ने नतिजा यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Entity
items.ne: इन्टिटी

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A rectangle. A real thing the database stores — a student, a course, a book. It becomes a TABLE.
items.ne: आयत। डाटाबेसले राख्ने वास्तविक वस्तु — विद्यार्थी, विषय, पुस्तक। यो तालिका बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Weak entity
items.ne: कमजोर इन्टिटी

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A double rectangle. It cannot be identified on its own — it needs its owner's key. Not "unimportant": it has no key of its own.
items.ne: दोहोरो आयत। यो आफैंले चिनिन सक्दैन — मालिकको कुञ्जी चाहिन्छ। "महत्त्वहीन" होइन: आफ्नै कुञ्जी नभएको।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Attribute
items.ne: एट्रिब्युट

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: An ellipse. A property of an entity — name, marks. It becomes a COLUMN.
items.ne: दीर्घवृत्त। इन्टिटीको गुण — नाम, अंक। यो स्तम्भ बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Key attribute
items.ne: कुञ्जी एट्रिब्युट

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: An ellipse with the name UNDERLINED. It identifies each occurrence uniquely and becomes the PRIMARY KEY.
items.ne: नाममुनि रेखा भएको दीर्घवृत्त। हरेकलाई अद्वितीय चिनाउँछ र प्राथमिक कुञ्जी बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Multivalued attribute
items.ne: बहुमान एट्रिब्युट

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A double ellipse. One occurrence can hold several values — a student with two phone numbers.
items.ne: दोहोरो दीर्घवृत्त। एउटैले धेरै मान राख्न सक्छ — दुई फोन नम्बर भएको विद्यार्थी।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Derived attribute
items.ne: व्युत्पन्न एट्रिब्युट

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A dashed ellipse. Not stored — worked out from something that is. Age is derived from date of birth.
items.ne: धर्के दीर्घवृत्त। भण्डारण गरिँदैन — अरूबाट निकालिन्छ। उमेर जन्ममितिबाट निस्कन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Relationship
items.ne: सम्बन्ध

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A diamond. How two entities are connected — a student ENROLS IN a course. Written as a verb.
items.ne: चतुर्भुज। दुई इन्टिटी कसरी जोडिन्छन् — विद्यार्थी विषयमा भर्ना हुन्छ। क्रियापदमा लेखिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: ER model visualiser
items.ne: ER मोडेल भिजुअलाइजर

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Show {…}
items.ne: {…} देखाउनुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: What that means row by row
items.ne: पङ्क्ति–पङ्क्तिमा त्यसको अर्थ

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Now look back the other way: {…} is linked from {…} rows of {…}. Both directions are "many" — that is what makes this M:N.
items.ne: अब उल्टो हेर्नुहोस्: {…} लाई {…} का {…} पङ्क्तिले जोडेका छन्। दुवैतर्फ "धेरै" — यसैले यो M:N हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Look back the other way: every {…} row points at exactly one {…} row. That is why this is not many-to-many.
items.ne: उल्टो हेर्नुहोस्: {…} को हरेक पङ्क्तिले {…} को ठ्याक्कै एउटा पङ्क्ति देखाउँछ। त्यसैले यो धेरै–धेरै होइन।

items.ne: कार्डिनालिटी भनेको पङ्क्तिको सङ्ख्या। ठाडो गरी गन्नुहोस्। विद्यार्थीले डिग्रीसँग साट्ने ठाउँ यही हो।

items.ne: डोमेन भनेको कुनै स्तम्भले लिन पाउने मानहरूको समूह। marks मा "Ram" राख्न मिल्दैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language
items.en: The primary key identifies each row uniquely. No two rows may share it, and it can never be empty.
items.ne: प्राथमिक कुञ्जीले हरेक पङ्क्तिलाई अद्वितीय रूपमा चिनाउँछ। दुई पङ्क्तिको उही हुन सक्दैन, र खाली हुन पाउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language
items.en: Relational schema
items.ne: रिलेसनल स्किमा

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language
items.en: The schema is the STRUCTURE — the table name and its columns. It does not change when rows are added.
items.ne: स्किमा भनेको संरचना — तालिकाको नाम र स्तम्भहरू। पङ्क्ति थप्दा यो बदलिँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language
items.en: Relational instance
items.ne: रिलेसनल इन्स्ट्यान्स

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language
items.en: The instance is the DATA in the table right now. It changes every time a row is inserted or deleted.
items.ne: इन्स्ट्यान्स भनेको अहिले तालिकामा भएको डाटा। पङ्क्ति थपिँदा वा हट्दा यो बदलिन्छ।

items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language

items.ne: रिलेसनल तालिका भिजुअलाइजर

items.ne: कुनै पङ्क्ति छैन

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language
items.en: columns — degree
items.ne: स्तम्भ — डिग्री

items.subject: grade10/dbms

items.ne: पङ्क्ति — कार्डिनालिटी

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language
items.en: {…}.{…} identifies each row of {…} uniquely.
items.ne: {…}.{…} ले {…} का हरेक पङ्क्तिलाई अद्वितीय चिनाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.unitTitle: Entity Relationship Model (ER-Model) / Relational Model / SQL — Structured Query Language
items.en: {…}.{…} must already exist in {…}.{…} . That rule is what links the two tables.
items.ne: {…}.{…} को मान {…}.{…} मा पहिले नै हुनुपर्छ। यही नियमले दुई तालिका जोड्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Degree is the number of columns; cardinality is the number of rows. Here the degree is 5 and the cardinality is 200. Swapping these two is the commonest error in this unit.
items.ne: Degree भनेको स्तम्भ सङ्ख्या; cardinality भनेको पङ्क्ति सङ्ख्या। यहाँ degree ५ र cardinality २००। यी दुई साट्नु यस युनिटको सबैभन्दा सामान्य गल्ती हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A relation is a set of tuples, so no two rows may be identical — the primary key guarantees it. Order is not significant for rows or columns, and NULLs are permitted in non-key columns.
items.ne: रिलेसन ट्युपलहरूको सेट हो, त्यसैले दुई पङ्क्ति उस्तै हुन पाउँदैनन् — primary key ले सुनिश्चित गर्छ। पङ्क्ति र स्तम्भको क्रमको महत्त्व हुँदैन, र कुञ्जी नभएका स्तम्भमा NULL मिल्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A domain constrains what may appear in a column. The domain of "marks" might be whole numbers from 0 to 100, so the text "Ram" could never be stored there.
items.ne: Domain ले स्तम्भमा के आउन सक्छ भन्ने सीमित गर्छ। "marks" को domain ० देखि १०० सम्मका पूर्ण सङ्ख्या होला, त्यसैले त्यहाँ "Ram" राख्न मिल्दैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Referential integrity says a foreign key may only hold a value that already exists as a primary key in the table it points at. It may be NULL — meaning "not assigned" — but it may not be wrong.
items.ne: Referential integrity अनुसार foreign key ले देखाइएको तालिकाको primary key मा पहिले नै भएको मान मात्र राख्न पाउँछ। NULL हुन सक्छ — "तोकिएको छैन" भन्ने अर्थमा — तर गलत हुन पाउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The primary key of the "one" side is copied into the "many" side. Each student stores the one class_id they belong to. Doing it the other way round cannot work — a column holds one value, and a class has many students.
items.ne: "एक" तर्फको primary key "धेरै" तर्फ सारिन्छ। हरेक विद्यार्थीले आफू भएको एउटा class_id राख्छ। उल्टो गर्दा हुँदैन — स्तम्भले एउटै मान राख्छ, र कक्षामा धेरै विद्यार्थी हुन्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The relational model links tables by matching values — a foreign key holding a value that exists as a primary key elsewhere. It deliberately avoids pointers, which is what made it simpler than the models before it.
items.ne: रिलेसनल मोडेलले मान मिलाएर तालिका जोड्छ — foreign key सँग अन्यत्र primary key भएको मान। यसले जानाजान pointer प्रयोग गर्दैन, र यही कारण यो अघिल्ला मोडेलभन्दा सरल भयो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: 3.3 — The properties of a relation. Every cell holds a single, atomic value — never a list. No two rows are identical — the primary key guarantees it. The order of rows does not matter, and neither does the order of columns — a table is a set, not a list. Every value in a column comes from the same domain.
items.ne: रिलेसनका गुण: हरेक कक्षमा एउटै अविभाज्य मान हुन्छ — सूची कहिल्यै होइन। दुई पङ्क्ति उस्तै हुँदैनन् — primary key ले सुनिश्चित गर्छ। पङ्क्तिको क्रमले फरक पार्दैन, स्तम्भको क्रमले पनि — तालिका सेट हो, सूची होइन। एउटै स्तम्भका सबै मान उही domain बाट आउँछन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Swapping degree and cardinality. Degree counts columns; cardinality counts rows. Check your answer against the table — the two numbers are almost never the same.
items.ne: Degree र cardinality साट्नु। Degree ले स्तम्भ, cardinality ले पङ्क्ति गन्छ। तालिकासँग मिलाएर जाँच्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Turning an ER diagram into tables, one rule at a time.
items.ne: ER चित्रलाई तालिकामा बदल्ने — एक पटकमा एउटा नियम।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Start from the ER diagram: two entities and one relationship, many-to-many.
items.ne: ER चित्रबाट सुरु: दुई इन्टिटी र एउटा सम्बन्ध, धेरै–धेरै।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Rule 1: every entity becomes a table. STUDENT becomes Student, and its key attribute becomes the primary key.
items.ne: नियम १: हरेक इन्टिटी तालिका बन्छ। STUDENT बाट Student, र यसको कुञ्जी एट्रिब्युट प्राथमिक कुञ्जी बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The same rule again for COURSE. Every attribute becomes a column.
items.ne: COURSE लाई पनि उही नियम। हरेक एट्रिब्युट स्तम्भ बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Rule 2: a MANY-TO-MANY relationship becomes a table of its own, holding the primary key of each side as a foreign key. This third table is the one students forget.
items.ne: नियम २: धेरै–धेरै सम्बन्ध आफैं एउटा तालिका बन्छ, जसमा दुवैतर्फको प्राथमिक कुञ्जी foreign key भएर बस्छ। विद्यार्थीले बिर्सने तेस्रो तालिका यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Convert an ER diagram into a set of tables, including the junction table an M:N relationship forces.
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा: रिलेसनल मोडेल के हो र किन प्रायः सबै डाटाबेसले यही प्रयोग गर्छन् भन्न, दिइएको तालिकाका हरेक भागलाई सही नाम दिन, degree र cardinality नअलमलिई छुट्याउन, domain–instance–schema परिभाषित गर्न, रिलेसनका गुण भन्न, र ER चित्रलाई तालिकामा बदल्न सक्नुहुनेछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Press the same button twice to clear it.
items.ne: Degree र Cardinality एकपछि अर्को थिच्नुहोस् — उज्यालो स्तम्भबाट पङ्क्तिमा सर्छ। दुवै गणना तालिकामुनि सधैं देखिन्छ। अब Relational schema र Relational instance थिच्नुहोस्। Schema ले शीर्ष भाग, instance ले मुख्य भाग बाल्छ — शीर्ष भनेको डिजाइन, मुख्य भाग भनेको आजको data। उही बटन दोहोर्‍याएर थिच्दा हट्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Two entities, related many-to-many. Commit to one number before you open this: how many tables will the finished answer have? The number itself tells you whether you have remembered the M:N rule.
items.ne: दुई entity, many-to-many सम्बन्ध। खोल्नुअघि एउटा सङ्ख्या भन्नुहोस्: पूरा उत्तरमा कति वटा तालिका हुनेछन्? त्यो सङ्ख्याले नै M:N को नियम सम्झनुभयो कि भएन भन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Three tables from two entities. Marks are lost here by producing only two and trying to squeeze the relationship into a single column — which cannot work, because a column holds one value and this doctor has many patients.
items.ne: दुई इन्टिटीबाट तीन तालिका। यहाँ अंक जाने ठाउँ: दुई मात्र बनाएर सम्बन्धलाई एउटै स्तम्भमा कोच्न खोज्नु — जुन सम्भव छैन, किनभने स्तम्भले एउटै मान राख्छ र यो डाक्टरका धेरै बिरामी छन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Gita's class_id is NULL, and that is allowed. A foreign key may be empty — it means "not assigned yet". It may not be wrong.
items.ne: दुई ब्याज पढ्नुहोस्। PK ले पङ्क्ति चिनाउने स्तम्भ, FK ले अर्को तालिका देखाउने स्तम्भ जनाउँछ। Student.class_id मा १०, १०, ११ छन् — सबै Class.class_id मा भएका मान। यही referential integrity हो। कक्षा १५ मा विद्यार्थी थप्न खोजे अस्वीकार हुन्छ। गीताको class_id NULL छ, र त्यो मिल्छ — foreign key खाली हुन पाउँछ, गलत हुन पाउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Write down all five answers now. Degree and cardinality are the pair that get swapped — one of them counts across, the other counts down, and deciding which before you look is the whole exercise.
items.ne: पाँचै उत्तर अहिल्यै लेख्नुहोस्। Degree र cardinality नै साटिने जोडी हो — एउटाले तेर्सो गन्छ, अर्कोले ठाडो, र हेर्नुअघि कुन हो भन्ने छुट्याउनु नै पूरा अभ्यास हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Write the two counts with the words "columns" and "rows" beside them, as above. A marker reading "Degree 4, Cardinality 3" cannot tell whether you knew which was which or guessed; "Degree 4 columns, Cardinality 3 rows" removes the doubt.
items.ne: दुई गणनासँगै "स्तम्भ" र "पङ्क्ति" शब्द लेख्नुहोस्। "Degree ४, Cardinality ३" मात्र लेखे परीक्षकले जानेर लेखेको कि अनुमान गरेको भन्न सक्दैनन्; शब्द थपे शङ्का हट्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Saying a relation may have duplicate rows. It may not — that is one of the defining properties.
items.ne: रिलेसनमा उही पङ्क्ति दोहोरिन सक्छ भन्नु। सक्दैन — यो परिभाषित गुण मध्येको एक हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Turning an M:N relationship into two tables. It needs three. The relationship itself becomes a table.
items.ne: M:N सम्बन्धलाई दुई तालिका बनाउनु। तीन चाहिन्छ — सम्बन्ध आफैं तालिका बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Confusing schema with instance. Inserting a row changes the instance. The schema is unchanged.
items.ne: Schema र instance मिसाउनु। पङ्क्ति थप्दा instance बदलिन्छ, schema होइन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Putting a list in a cell. "Maths, Science" in one cell breaks the atomic-value property — and it is exactly what 1NF exists to fix, in Unit 5.
items.ne: एउटै कक्षमा सूची राख्नु। "Maths, Science" ले अविभाज्य मानको गुण तोड्छ — र युनिट ५ को 1NF यही सुधार्न छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Two question shapes dominate here. The first gives you a small table and asks you to state its degree, its cardinality and its primary key — a few marks, quickly earned, provided you do not swap the first two. The second gives you an ER diagram and asks you to convert it to tables; the marks are for the right number of tables and for putting the foreign key on the correct side.
items.ne: यहाँ दुई किसिमका प्रश्न हावी छन्। पहिलोले सानो तालिका दिएर degree, cardinality र primary key सोध्छ — छिटो पाइने अंक, पहिला दुई नसाटे। दोस्रोले ER चित्र दिएर तालिकामा बदल्न भन्छ; अंक सही सङ्ख्या का तालिका र foreign key सही तर्फ राखेकोमा हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Any three, each named and explained in one line.
items.ne: कुनै तीन — नाम दिएर एक–एक हरफमा व्याख्या गर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: One mark per table, one for the primary keys, one for the foreign key on the correct side. Putting student_id into Class instead would be wrong — a class has many students, so that column could not hold them all.
items.ne: सम्बन्ध 1:M भएकाले नियम २ लाग्छ: तेस्रो तालिका चाहिँदैन। "एक" तर्फ (Class) को primary key "धेरै" तर्फ (Student) मा foreign key भएर जान्छ। उल्टो गर्दा गलत हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Degree = number of columns. Cardinality = number of rows. Do not swap them.
items.ne: Degree = स्तम्भ सङ्ख्या। Cardinality = पङ्क्ति सङ्ख्या। नसाट्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Schema is the structure; instance is the data in it right now.
items.ne: Schema संरचना हो; instance अहिलेको data।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: A relation holds atomic values, no duplicate rows, and no significant order.
items.ne: रिलेसनमा अविभाज्य मान हुन्छन्, उही पङ्क्ति दोहोरिँदैन, र क्रमको महत्त्व हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: ER → tables: every entity a table; 1:M puts a foreign key in the many side; M:N makes a third table; a multivalued attribute makes its own table.
items.ne: ER → तालिका: हरेक इन्टिटी एउटा तालिका; 1:M मा "धेरै" तर्फ foreign key; M:N ले तेस्रो तालिका; बहुमान एट्रिब्युटले आफ्नै तालिका।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Referential integrity: a foreign key may be NULL, but it may never hold a value that does not exist in the table it points at.
items.ne: Referential integrity: foreign key NULL हुन सक्छ, तर देखाइएको तालिकामा नभएको मान कहिल्यै राख्न पाउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: The relational model stores everything as tables and links them with keys, not pointers. Proposed by E. F. Codd, 1970.
items.ne: रिलेसनल मोडेलले सबै कुरा तालिकामा राख्छ र pointer होइन, कुञ्जीले जोड्छ। E. F. Codd, सन् १९७०।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Definition — learn this wording The relational model represents all data as relations — two-dimensional tables of rows and columns — and represents the connections between them using keys rather than pointers or links. That is the whole idea, and its power is that it needs only one shape. A student, a course, and the enrolment joining them are all the same kind of object: a table. Nothing else has to be learned. It was proposed by E. F. Codd in 1970 and is the model behind MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL and MS Access.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्दमा सम्झनुहोस् रिलेसनल मोडेल ले सबै data लाई रिलेसन — पङ्क्ति र स्तम्भ भएका दुई आयामिक तालिका — का रूपमा राख्छ, र तिनबीचको जोडाइ pointer वा link होइन, कुञ्जी ले देखाउँछ। पूरा विचार यत्ति हो, र यसको बल एउटै आकार चाहिनुमा छ। विद्यार्थी, विषय, र दुवैलाई जोड्ने भर्ना — तीनै उही किसिमका वस्तु हुन्: तालिका। अरू केही सिक्नु पर्दैन। यो E. F. Codd ले सन् १९७० मा प्रस्ताव गरेका हुन्, र MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL तथा MS Access यसैमा आधारित छन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Nine words, six things This topic is a list of terms, and lists of terms are what students confuse in the hall. The pair that goes wrong most is degree and cardinality: they sound interchangeable and they are not. Degree is the number of columns. Cardinality is the number of rows. A table with 4 columns and 100 rows has degree 4 and cardinality 100 — the numbers are usually nothing alike, so if you can remember which is which you can always check your own answer. Rather than memorising nine definitions, point at them. Use the tool below: choose a word and the part of the table it names lights up.
items.ne: नौ शब्द, छ वस्तु यो टपिक शब्दहरूको सूची हो, र परीक्षा हलमा विद्यार्थीले अलमल्ने ठाउँ यस्तै सूची हुन्। सबैभन्दा बढी बिग्रने जोडी degree र cardinality हो: सुन्दा उस्तै लाग्छ, तर होइन। Degree भनेको स्तम्भको सङ्ख्या। Cardinality भनेको पङ्क्तिको सङ्ख्या। ४ स्तम्भ र १०० पङ्क्ति भएको तालिकाको degree ४ र cardinality १०० हुन्छ — सङ्ख्या प्रायः निकै फरक हुने भएकाले कुन हो सम्झे आफ्नै उत्तर जाँच्न सकिन्छ। नौ परिभाषा घोक्नुभन्दा औंल्याएर हेर्नुहोस्। तलको औजारमा शब्द छान्नुहोस् — त्यसले जनाउने भाग तालिकामा बल्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Four rules, applied in order 1. Every entity becomes a table. Its key attribute becomes the primary key, and every other attribute becomes a column. 2. A 1:M relationship is recorded by putting the primary key of the "one" side into the "many" side as a foreign key. No extra table. 3. A M:N relationship becomes a table of its own, holding the primary key of each side as a foreign key. Together those two columns form its composite primary key. 4. A multivalued attribute becomes a separate table too — a column can hold only one value, so two phone numbers cannot live in one cell.
items.ne: चार नियम, यही क्रममा १. हरेक इन्टिटी तालिका बन्छ। यसको कुञ्जी एट्रिब्युट primary key बन्छ, र बाँकी हरेक एट्रिब्युट एउटा स्तम्भ। २. 1:M सम्बन्ध लाई "एक" तर्फको primary key लाई "धेरै" तर्फ foreign key बनाएर राखिन्छ। थप तालिका चाहिँदैन। ३. M:N सम्बन्ध आफैं एउटा तालिका बन्छ, जसमा दुवैतर्फको primary key foreign key भएर बस्छ। ती दुई स्तम्भ मिलेर composite primary key बन्छ। ४. बहुमान एट्रिब्युट पनि छुट्टै तालिका बन्छ — स्तम्भले एउटै मान राख्ने भएकाले दुई फोन नम्बर एउटै कक्षमा बस्न सक्दैनन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: Degree counts across (columns). Cardinality counts down (rows).
items.ne: Degree ले तेर्सो गन्छ (स्तम्भ)। Cardinality ले ठाडो गन्छ (पङ्क्ति)।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Example: a Student table with columns id, name, marks, class_id and 4 rows has degree 4 and cardinality 4.
items.ne: दुवैको परिभाषा र एउटा उदाहरण। स्तम्भ = degree, पङ्क्ति = cardinality।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Define degree and cardinality of a relation.
items.ne: रिलेसनको degree र cardinality परिभाषित गर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: State any three properties of a relation.
items.ne: रिलेसनका कुनै तीन गुण लेख्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: A school has CLASS (class_id, room) and STUDENT (student_id, name). A class contains many students, and each student belongs to one class. Convert this ER model to the relational model and mark the keys.
items.ne: एउटा विद्यालयमा CLASS (class_id, room) र STUDENT (student_id, name) छन्। एउटा कक्षामा धेरै विद्यार्थी हुन्छन्, र हरेक विद्यार्थी एउटै कक्षाको हुन्छ। यसलाई रिलेसनल मोडेलमा बदलेर कुञ्जी देखाउनुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Yes. A relation is a set of tuples, and a set has no order. This is why you must write ORDER BY when you want a particular order — the database is under no obligation to give you the rows in the order they were inserted, and without ORDER BY it may give a different order each time.
items.ne: हो। रिलेसन भनेको ट्युपलहरूको सेट हो, र सेटको क्रम हुँदैन। त्यसैले निश्चित क्रम चाहिँदा ORDER BY लेख्नैपर्छ — डाटाबेसले भर्ना गरेकै क्रममा दिनुपर्ने बाध्यता छैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Two tables hold exactly the same four rows, but one lists them in a different order. Are they the same relation?
items.ne: दुई तालिकामा ठ्याक्कै उही चार पङ्क्ति छन्, तर एउटामा क्रम फरक छ। के ती एउटै रिलेसन हुन्?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A table is what an entity becomes, and a foreign key is what a relationship becomes. Converting ER to relational is the whole of topic 3.4, and it is impossible without the ER half.
items.ne: Entity तालिका बन्छ, र relationship foreign key बन्छ। ER लाई relational मा बदल्नु नै टपिक ३.४ हो, र ER पक्ष नभई त्यो सम्भव छैन।

items.ne: पूरै उस्तै दुई पङ्क्ति

items.ne: कुनै निश्चित क्रम नभएका पङ्क्ति

items.ne: NULL राख्न दिने स्तम्भ

items.en: Columns listed in a different order
items.ne: फरक क्रममा राखिएका स्तम्भ

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The set of values an attribute is allowed to hold
items.ne: कुनै एट्रिब्युटले लिन पाउने मानहरूको समूह

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The number of rows in a table
items.ne: तालिकाका पङ्क्तिको सङ्ख्या

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The name of the database
items.ne: डाटाबेसको नाम

items.en: The primary key of a relation
items.ne: रिलेसनको primary key

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: It is refused — referential integrity is violated
items.ne: अस्वीकार हुन्छ — referential integrity उल्लङ्घन हुन्छ

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: It is accepted and class 15 is created automatically
items.ne: स्वीकार हुन्छ र कक्षा १५ आफैं बन्छ

items.en: It is accepted and the value becomes NULL
items.ne: स्वीकार हुन्छ र मान NULL बन्छ

items.en: It is accepted with a warning
items.ne: चेतावनीसहित स्वीकार हुन्छ

items.en: Into the table on the MANY side
items.ne: "धेरै" तर्फको तालिकामा

items.ne: नयाँ तेस्रो तालिकामा

items.ne: दुवै तालिकामा

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A table has 5 columns and 200 rows. What is its DEGREE?
items.ne: एउटा तालिकामा ५ स्तम्भ र २०० पङ्क्ति छन्। यसको DEGREE कति हो?

items.en: Which of these is NOT allowed in a relation?
items.ne: रिलेसनमा यीमध्ये कुन मिल्दैन?

items.ne: रिलेसनल मोडेलमा DOMAIN भनेको के हो?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: By the end of this unit you can…
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा तपाईं यी कुरा गर्न सक्नुहुनेछ

items.en: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.ne: परीक्षा केन्द्रबिन्दु — यो युनिटबाट के सोधिन्छ

items.ne: Relational तालिका भिजुअलाइजर

items.ne: Key हरू, र दुई तालिका जोड्ने नियम

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Interactive experiment
items.ne: · अन्तरक्रियात्मक प्रयोग

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · अन्तरक्रियात्मक प्रयोग The relational table visualiser What you will learn: which part of a table each term names, so the words attach to something you can see instead of to each other. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: हरेक शब्दले तालिकाको कुन भाग जनाउँछ — शब्दहरू एकआपसमा होइन, देखिने कुरामा टाँसिऊन् भनेर। What to notice Press Degree and then Cardinality one after the other, and watch the highlight turn from columns to rows. The two counts are printed under the table the whole time — 4 and 4 here, which is unhelpfully equal, so read the word, not the number. Now press Relational schema, then Relational instance. The schema highlights the heading; the instance highlights the body. That is the whole distinction: the heading is the design, the body is today's data. Press the same button twice to clear it. Degree र Cardinality एकपछि अर्को थिच्नुहोस् — उज्यालो स्तम्भबाट पङ्क्तिमा सर्छ। दुवै गणना तालिकामुनि सधैं देखिन्छ। अब Relational schema र Relational instance थिच्नुहोस्। Schema ले शीर्ष भाग, instance ले मुख्य भाग बाल्छ — शीर्ष भनेको डिजाइन, मुख्य भाग भनेको आजको data। उही बटन दोहोर्‍याएर थिच्दा हट्छ। 3.3 — The properties of a relation. Every cell holds a single, atomic value — never a list. No two rows are identical — the primary key guarantees it. The order of rows does not matter, and neither does the order of columns — a table is a set, not a list. Every value in a column comes from the same domain. रिलेसनका गुण: हरेक कक्षमा एउटै अविभाज्य मान हुन्छ — सूची कहिल्यै होइन। दुई पङ्क्ति उस्तै हुँदैनन् — primary key ले सुनिश्चित गर्छ। पङ्क्तिको क्रमले फरक पार्दैन, स्तम्भको क्रमले पनि — तालिका सेट हो, सूची होइन। एउटै स्तम्भका सबै मान उही domain बाट आउँछन्। Predict first
items.ne: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् Two tables hold exactly the same four rows, but one lists them in a different order. Are they the same relation? दुई तालिकामा ठ्याक्कै उही चार पङ्क्ति छन्, तर एउटामा क्रम फरक छ। के ती एउटै रिलेसन हुन्? Yes — order does not matter No — the order is part of the table Yes. A relation is a set of tuples, and a set has no order. This is why you must write ORDER BY when you want a particular order — the database is under no obligation to give you the rows in the order they were inserted, and without ORDER BY it may give a different order each time. हो। रिलेसन भनेको ट्युपलहरूको सेट हो, र सेटको क्रम हुँदैन। त्यसैले निश्चित क्रम चाहिँदा ORDER BY लेख्नैपर्छ — डाटाबेसले भर्ना गरेकै क्रममा दिनुपर्ने बाध्यता छैन। 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model Four rules, applied in order 1. Every entity becomes a table. Its key attribute becomes the primary key, and every other attribute becomes a column. 2. A 1:M relationship is recorded by putting the primary key of the "one" side into the "many" side as a foreign key. No extra table. 3. A M:N relationship becomes a table of its own, holding the primary key of each side as a foreign key. Together those two columns form its composite primary key. 4. A multivalued attribute becomes a separate table too — a column can hold only one value, so two phone numbers cannot live in one cell. चार नियम, यही क्रममा १. हरेक इन्टिटी तालिका बन्छ। यसको कुञ्जी एट्रिब्युट primary key बन्छ, र बाँकी हरेक एट्रिब्युट एउटा स्तम्भ। २. 1:M सम्बन्ध लाई "एक" तर्फको primary key लाई "धेरै" तर्फ foreign key बनाएर राखिन्छ। थप तालिका चाहिँदैन। ३. M:N सम्बन्ध आफैं एउटा तालिका बन्छ, जसमा दुवैतर्फको primary key foreign key भएर बस्छ। ती दुई स्तम्भ मिलेर composite primary key बन्छ। ४. बहुमान एट्रिब्युट पनि छुट्टै तालिका बन्छ — स्तम्भले एउटै मान राख्ने भएकाले दुई फोन नम्बर एउटै कक्षमा बस्न सक्दैनन्। {{dia:erToRelational}} Example 1 Converting an ER diagram to tables Question: a hospital records DOCTORs (doctor_id, name) and PATIENTs (patient_id, name). A doctor treats many patients, and a patient may be treated by many doctors. Convert this to the relational model. Two entities, related many-to-many. Commit to one number before you open this: how many tables will the finished answer have? The number itself tells you whether you have remembered the M:N rule. दुई entity, many-to-many सम्बन्ध। खोल्नुअघि एउटा सङ्ख्या भन्नुहोस्: पूरा उत्तरमा कति वटा तालिका हुनेछन्? त्यो सङ्ख्याले नै M:N को नियम सम्झनुभयो कि भएन भन्छ। Step 1 — apply rule 1 to each entity: Working Doctor ( doctor_id, name ) PK Patient ( patient_id, name ) PK Step 2 — decide the cardinality. Many doctors to many patients, in both directions, so it is M:N. Rule 3 applies: the relationship gets a table of its own. Answer Doctor ( doctor_id, name ) Patient ( patient_id, name ) Treats ( doctor_id, patient_id ) FK FK composite primary key = both columns together Three tables from two entities. Marks are lost here by producing only two and trying to squeeze the relationship into a single column — which cannot work, because a column holds one value and this doctor has many patients. दुई इन्टिटीबाट तीन तालिका। यहाँ अंक जाने ठाउँ: दुई मात्र बनाएर सम्बन्धलाई एउटै स्तम्भमा कोच्न खोज्नु — जुन सम्भव छैन, किनभने स्तम्भले एउटै मान राख्छ र यो डाक्टरका धेरै बिरामी छन्। Worked example — read it
items.ne: · तयार उदाहरण — पढ्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · तयार उदाहरण — पढ्नुहोस् Keys, and the rule that links two tables What you will learn: how a foreign key in one table points at a primary key in another, and what referential integrity actually forbids. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: एउटा तालिकाको foreign key ले अर्कोको primary key लाई कसरी देखाउँछ, र referential integrity ले साँच्चै के निषेध गर्छ। What to notice Read the two badges. PK marks the column that identifies a row; FK marks the column that points at another table. Student.class_id holds 10, 10 and 11 — values that all exist in Class.class_id. That is referential integrity: a foreign key may not hold a value that has no matching primary key. Inserting a student in class 15 would be refused, because no class 15 exists. Gita's class_id is NULL, and that is allowed. A foreign key may be empty — it means "not assigned yet". It may not be wrong. दुई ब्याज पढ्नुहोस्। PK ले पङ्क्ति चिनाउने स्तम्भ, FK ले अर्को तालिका देखाउने स्तम्भ जनाउँछ। Student.class_id मा १०, १०, ११ छन् — सबै Class.class_id मा भएका मान। यही referential integrity हो। कक्षा १५ मा विद्यार्थी थप्न खोजे अस्वीकार हुन्छ। गीताको class_id NULL छ, र त्यो मिल्छ — foreign key खाली हुन पाउँछ, गलत हुन पाउँदैन। Example 2 Labelling a table with the right term for every part Question: for the table below, state the relation name, the degree, the cardinality, the primary key, and the domain of marks. Given Student ┌────┬───────┬───────┬──────────┐ │ id │ name │ marks │ class_id │ ├────┼───────┼───────┼──────────┤ │ 1 │ Ram │ 78 │ 10 │ │ 2 │ Sita │ 91 │ 10 │ │ 3 │ Hari │ 55 │ 11 │ └────┴───────┴───────┴──────────┘ Write down all five answers now. Degree and cardinality are the pair that get swapped — one of them counts across, the other counts down, and deciding which before you look is the whole exercise. पाँचै उत्तर अहिल्यै लेख्नुहोस्। Degree र cardinality नै साटिने जोडी हो — एउटाले तेर्सो गन्छ, अर्कोले ठाडो, र हेर्नुअघि कुन हो भन्ने छुट्याउनु नै पूरा अभ्यास हो। Count sideways for degree, downwards for cardinality. That one sentence prevents the only mistake this question invites: Answer Relation name Student Degree 4 (id, name, marks, class_id — count COLUMNS) Cardinality 3 (three tuples — count ROWS) Primary key id (unique, and never NULL) Domain of marks whole numbers 0–100 Attribute one column, e.g. name Tuple one row, e.g. (2, Sita, 91, 10) Write the two counts with the words "columns" and "rows" beside them, as above. A marker reading "Degree 4, Cardinality 3" cannot tell whether you knew which was which or guessed; "Degree 4 columns, Cardinality 3 rows" removes the doubt. दुई गणनासँगै "स्तम्भ" र "पङ्क्ति" शब्द लेख्नुहोस्। "Degree ४, Cardinality ३" मात्र लेखे परीक्षकले जानेर लेखेको कि अनुमान गरेको भन्न सक्दैनन्; शब्द थपे शङ्का हट्छ। Mistakes that cost marks here Swapping degree and cardinality. Degree counts columns; cardinality counts rows. Check your answer against the table — the two numbers are almost never the same. Degree र cardinality साट्नु। Degree ले स्तम्भ, cardinality ले पङ्क्ति गन्छ। तालिकासँग मिलाएर जाँच्नुहोस्। Saying a relation may have duplicate rows. It may not — that is one of the defining properties. रिलेसनमा उही पङ्क्ति दोहोरिन सक्छ भन्नु। सक्दैन — यो परिभाषित गुण मध्येको एक हो। Turning an M:N relationship into two tables. It needs three. The relationship itself becomes a table. M:N सम्बन्धलाई दुई तालिका बनाउनु। तीन चाहिन्छ — सम्बन्ध आफैं तालिका बन्छ। Confusing schema with instance. Inserting a row changes the instance. The schema is unchanged. Schema र instance मिसाउनु। पङ्क्ति थप्दा instance बदलिन्छ, schema होइन। Putting a list in a cell. "Maths, Science" in one cell breaks the atomic-value property — and it is exactly what 1NF exists to fix, in Unit 5. एउटै कक्षमा सूची राख्नु। "Maths, Science" ले अविभाज्य मानको गुण तोड्छ — र युनिट ५ को 1NF यही सुधार्न छ। Degree counts across (columns). Cardinality counts down (rows). Degree ले तेर्सो गन्छ (स्तम्भ)। Cardinality ले ठाडो गन्छ (पङ्क्ति)। Exam focus — what is asked from this unit Two question shapes dominate here. The first gives you a small table and asks you to state its degree, its cardinality and its primary key — a few marks, quickly earned, provided you do not swap the first two. The second gives you an ER diagram and asks you to convert it to tables; the marks are for the right number of tables and for putting the foreign key on the correct side. यहाँ दुई किसिमका प्रश्न हावी छन्। पहिलोले सानो तालिका दिएर degree, cardinality र primary key सोध्छ — छिटो पाइने अंक, पहिला दुई नसाटे। दोस्रोले ER चित्र दिएर तालिकामा बदल्न भन्छ; अंक सही सङ्ख्या का तालिका र foreign key सही तर्फ राखेकोमा हुन्छ। 2 marks Practice question Define degree and cardinality of a relation. रिलेसनको degree र cardinality परिभाषित गर्नुहोस्। Show the answer The degree of a relation is the number of attributes (columns) in it. The cardinality of a relation is the number of tuples (rows) in it. Example: a Student table with columns id, name, marks, class_id and 4 rows has degree 4 and cardinality 4. दुवैको परिभाषा र एउटा उदाहरण। स्तम्भ = degree, पङ्क्ति = cardinality। 3 marks Practice question State any three properties of a relation. रिलेसनका कुनै तीन गुण लेख्नुहोस्। Show the answer Atomic values — every cell holds a single indivisible value, never a list. No duplicate tuples — no two rows are identical, which the primary key guarantees. Order is not significant — the rows and the columns may be listed in any order. Values come from a domain — every value in a column is drawn from the same allowed set. Each attribute has a distinct name. Any three, each named and explained in one line. कुनै तीन — नाम दिएर एक–एक हरफमा व्याख्या गर्नुहोस्। 4 marks Practice question A school has CLASS (class_id, room) and STUDENT (student_id, name). A class contains many students, and each student belongs to one class. Convert this ER model to the relational model and mark the keys. एउटा विद्यालयमा CLASS (class_id, room) र STUDENT (student_id, name) छन्। एउटा कक्षामा धेरै विद्यार्थी हुन्छन्, र हरेक विद्यार्थी एउटै कक्षाको हुन्छ। यसलाई रिलेसनल मोडेलमा बदलेर कुञ्जी देखाउनुहोस्। Show the answer Class ( class_id, room ) PK Student ( student_id, name, class_id ) PK FK → Class.class_id The relationship is 1:M, so rule 2 applies: no third table. The primary key of the "one" side (Class) goes into the "many" side (Student) as a foreign key. One mark per table, one for the primary keys, one for the foreign key on the correct side. Putting student_id into Class instead would be wrong — a class has many students, so that column could not hold them all. सम्बन्ध 1:M भएकाले नियम २ लाग्छ: तेस्रो तालिका चाहिँदैन। "एक" तर्फ (Class) को primary key "धेरै" तर्फ (Student) मा foreign key भएर जान्छ। उल्टो गर्दा गलत हुन्छ। Key points to revise
items.ne: — दोहोर्‍याउनुपर्ने मुख्य बुँदा

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Relational Model
items.ne: रिलेसनल मोडेल

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: What you will learn: which part of a table each term names, so the words attach to something you can see instead of to each other.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: हरेक शब्दले तालिकाको कुन भाग जनाउँछ — शब्दहरू एकआपसमा होइन, देखिने कुरामा टाँसिऊन् भनेर।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 3.4 Mapping the ER model to the relational model
items.en: What you will learn: how a foreign key in one table points at a primary key in another, and what referential integrity actually forbids.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: एउटा तालिकाको foreign key ले अर्कोको primary key लाई कसरी देखाउँछ, र referential integrity ले साँच्चै के निषेध गर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Sort a statement by what it changes. CREATE TABLE changes the structure, so it is DDL. DML changes the data inside; DCL changes who is allowed to use it.
items.ne: कथनले के बदल्छ त्यसैअनुसार छुट्याउनुहोस्। CREATE TABLE ले संरचना बदल्छ, त्यसैले DDL। DML ले भित्रको data, DCL ले प्रयोग गर्न पाउने अधिकार बदल्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: DELETE removes rows; the table and its columns remain, and you can insert into it again tomorrow. DROP TABLE removes the table itself. This is the difference examiners ask for most often.
items.ne: DELETE ले पङ्क्ति हटाउँछ; तालिका र यसका स्तम्भ रहन्छन्, र भोलि फेरि पङ्क्ति थप्न सकिन्छ। DROP TABLE ले तालिका नै हटाउँछ। परीक्षकले सबैभन्दा धेरै सोध्ने फरक यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Two independent cuts. WHERE chooses rows: 4 becomes 3. SELECT chooses columns: 4 becomes 1, because only "name" is listed. Neither clause does the other one's job.
items.ne: दुई छुट्टै कटाइ। WHERE ले पङ्क्ति छान्छ: ४ बाट ३। SELECT ले स्तम्भ छान्छ: ४ बाट १, किनभने "name" मात्र लेखिएको छ। एउटाले अर्कोको काम गर्दैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: ORDER BY only rearranges. Filtering is WHERE's job. The result still has 5 rows, now in a different order.
items.ne: ORDER BY ले क्रम मात्र मिलाउँछ। छान्ने काम WHERE को हो। नतिजामा अझै ५ पङ्क्ति छन्, क्रम मात्र फरक।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Work backwards from where the NULL is. Every left row survived and the missing value is on the right, so it is a left join. An inner join would have dropped that student entirely.
items.ne: NULL कता छ भन्नेबाट उल्टो सोच्नुहोस्। बायाँका सबै पङ्क्ति बाँचे र नभएको मान दायाँ छ, त्यसैले left join। Inner join ले त्यो विद्यार्थीलाई पूरै हटाइदिन्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: All five joins share the same matching test; they differ only in what they do with rows that did not match. Inner throws them away; the outer joins keep one side or both.
items.ne: पाँचै join को मिलान जाँच उही हो; फरक केवल नमिलेका पङ्क्तिको के गर्ने भन्नेमा। Inner ले फालिदिन्छ; outer join हरूले एक वा दुवैतर्फ राख्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The statement is perfectly legal, so nothing warns you — the WHERE clause is optional, and without it the change applies to every row. This is why the WHERE clause should be written before the SET.
items.ne: कथन पूर्णतः वैध हुने भएकाले चेतावनी आउँदैन — WHERE ऐच्छिक हो, र नभए परिवर्तन हरेक पङ्क्तिमा लाग्छ। त्यसैले SET भन्दा पहिले WHERE लेख्ने बानी राख्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A view reads from the real tables every time it is used, so it is always current. Views hide complexity — a long join becomes one name — and restrict access, since a user can be granted the view without the whole table.
items.ne: View ले प्रयोग हुँदा हरेक पटक वास्तविक तालिकाबाटै पढ्छ, त्यसैले सधैं ताजा हुन्छ। यसले जटिलता लुकाउँछ र पहुँच सीमित गर्छ — पूरै तालिका नदिई view दिन सकिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: GRANT gives a privilege and REVOKE takes it back; both are DCL. DELETE removes rows and DROP removes a table — those change data and structure, not permission.
items.ne: GRANT ले अधिकार दिन्छ र REVOKE ले फिर्ता लिन्छ; दुवै DCL हुन्। DELETE ले पङ्क्ति र DROP ले तालिका हटाउँछ — ती data र संरचना बदल्छन्, अधिकार होइन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Text values need single quotes. Without them the database looks for a COLUMN called Ram and reports that no such column exists. SQL uses a single = for comparison, not ==.
items.ne: पाठ मानलाई एकल उद्धरण चिन्ह चाहिन्छ। नभए डाटाबेसले Ram नामको स्तम्भ खोज्छ र त्यस्तो स्तम्भ छैन भन्छ। SQL मा तुलनाका लागि एउटै = हुन्छ, == होइन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The quickest way to classify a statement. Ask what would be lost if it ran. Structure gone → DDL. Rows changed → DML. Somebody's permission changed → DCL.
items.ne: छुट्याउने छिटो तरिका: यो चल्यो भने के हराउँछ भनी सोध्नुहोस्। संरचना गयो → DDL। पङ्क्ति बदलियो → DML। कसैको अधिकार बदलियो → DCL।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Using DELETE when the question says DROP. DELETE FROM Student; empties the table but leaves it standing — you can still insert into it tomorrow. DROP TABLE Student; removes the table itself. One is DML, the other is DDL.
items.ne: DROP भनेको ठाउँमा DELETE लेख्नु। DELETE FROM Student; ले तालिका खाली गर्छ तर तालिका रहन्छ। DROP TABLE Student; ले तालिका नै हटाउँछ। एउटा DML, अर्को DDL।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Sort by what a statement CHANGES, not by how it looks. This one classification answers a whole family of exam questions.
items.ne: कथनले के बदल्छ त्यसैअनुसार छुट्याउनुहोस्, हेराइअनुसार होइन। यही एउटा वर्गीकरणले परीक्षाका धेरै प्रश्नको उत्तर दिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.3 & 4.5 SELECT — asking the database a question
items.en: The order matters. WHERE runs before SELECT, which is why a query can filter on a column it never displays.
items.ne: क्रमको महत्त्व छ। WHERE, SELECT भन्दा पहिले चल्छ — त्यसैले क्वेरीले नदेखाउने स्तम्भमा पनि छान्न सक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.6 Joins — reading two tables as one
items.en: Learn the picture, not five separate definitions. The shaded area is the answer to "which rows survive".
items.ne: पाँच फरक परिभाषा होइन, यही चित्र सम्झनुहोस्। छायाँ परेको भाग नै "कुन पङ्क्ति बाँच्छ" भन्ने उत्तर हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Define a view and say why one is useful.
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा: SQL के हो भन्न र कुनै पनि कथनलाई DDL, DML वा DCL मा छुट्याउन, CREATE TABLE लेख्न, WHERE–AND–OR–ORDER BY सहितको SELECT लेखेर नतिजा अनुमान गर्न, INSERT–UPDATE–DELETE लेख्न र DELETE कसरी DROP भन्दा फरक छ भन्न, GRANT–REVOKE को उद्देश्य भन्न, पाँच join मध्ये कसले कुन पङ्क्ति राख्छ भन्न, र view को परिभाषा दिन सक्नुहुनेछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.3 & 4.5 SELECT — asking the database a question
items.en: Finally, add ORDER BY marks DESC. Watch the last number: it does not change. Sorting never removes a row.
items.ne: जस्ताको तस्तै चलाएर pipeline पढ्नुहोस्। FROM ४ → WHERE ३: एक जना हटे। अब > 60 लाई > 90 बनाएर फेरि चलाउनुहोस् — WHERE ले ४ मध्ये ३ हटेको भन्छ, नतिजामा एक पङ्क्ति आउँछ। अब पूरै WHERE मेटाउनुहोस्: सङ्ख्या घट्न छाड्छ — छान्ने काम WHERE ले मात्र गर्छ भन्ने प्रमाण यही हो। अन्त्यमा ORDER BY marks DESC थप्नुहोस्: अन्तिम सङ्ख्या बदलिँदैन। क्रम मिलाउँदा पङ्क्ति कहिल्यै हट्दैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.3 & 4.5 SELECT — asking the database a question
items.en: Four students, and the query is on screen. Write down exactly which names come back, in the order they come back. The database does not read this query top to bottom, and the ORDER BY is what gives that away.
items.ne: चार विद्यार्थी छन्, query सामुन्ने छ। कुन-कुन नाम, कुन क्रममा फर्किन्छन् ठ्याक्कै लेख्नुहोस्। डाटाबेसले यो query माथिबाट तलसम्म पढ्दैन, र ORDER BY ले नै त्यो देखाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.3 & 4.5 SELECT — asking the database a question
items.en: Gita is dropped for a reason worth remembering: her class_id is NULL, and NULL is not equal to anything — not even to 10. A comparison against NULL is never true.
items.ne: गीता हट्नुको कारण सम्झनलायक छ: उनको class_id NULL छ, र NULL कुनै पनि कुरासँग बराबर हुँदैन — १० सँग पनि होइन। NULL सँगको तुलना कहिल्यै सत्य हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.2 DDL — building and removing the structure
items.en: Three marks are usually available here and they are usually lost in the same three places: forgetting the data types, forgetting PRIMARY KEY, and forgetting the brackets round the whole column list. Write it in that order every time — name, type, key — and you cannot leave one out.
items.ne: यहाँ प्रायः तीन अंक हुन्छन्, र प्रायः उही तीन ठाउँमा जान्छन्: डाटा टाइप छुट्नु, PRIMARY KEY छुट्नु, र पूरै स्तम्भ सूचीको कोष्ठक छुट्नु। सधैं यही क्रममा लेख्नुहोस् — नाम, टाइप, कुञ्जी — अनि केही छुट्दैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.2 DDL — building and removing the structure
items.en: Press Reset, then run UPDATE Student SET marks = 80 with no WHERE. Every row changes, and the step turns red to tell you so. In a real school database that single missing WHERE would give every student the same mark.
items.ne: DELETE FROM Student WHERE marks < 60 चलाउनुहोस्। एउटा पङ्क्ति गयो; तालिका भने चारै स्तम्भसहित रहन्छ। अब DROP TABLE Student चलाउनुहोस्। तालिका नै हरायो — अब केहीबाट select गर्न सकिँदैन। Reset थिचेर WHERE नराखी UPDATE Student SET marks = 80 चलाउनुहोस्। सबै पङ्क्ति बदलिन्छन्, र चरण रातो हुन्छ। वास्तविक विद्यालय डाटाबेसमा त्यही एउटा छुटेको WHERE ले सबै विद्यार्थीलाई उही अंक दिन्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.6 Joins — reading two tables as one
items.en: If your data has no unmatched rows, all five joins return the same answer and you learn nothing from them. That is why this table was built with holes in it.
items.ne: पढाइका लागि दुई ठाउँ जानाजान खाली छन्: गीताको कक्षा छैन, र कोठा C-3 मा विद्यार्थी छैनन्। यी दुई खाली ठाउँ नै पूरा पाठ हुन्। उदाहरण क्रमैसँग थिच्नुहोस्। Inner ले ३ पङ्क्ति — दुवै खाली ठाउँ हराउँछन्। Left ले ४ — गीता कोठाको ठाउँमा NULL लिएर फर्किन्छिन्। Right ले ४ — C-3 नामको ठाउँमा NULL लिएर आउँछ। Full outer ले ५ — दुवै। नमिल्ने पङ्क्ति नै नभए पाँचै join ले उही उत्तर दिन्छन् र केही सिकिँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.6 Joins — reading two tables as one
items.en: Four joins are possible and only one fits. Name it before you open this, then check whether your reason was the NULL's position or only its presence — the position is what decides it.
items.ne: चार वटा join सम्भव छन्, मिल्ने एउटै हो। खोल्नुअघि नाम भन्नुहोस्, अनि जाँच्नुहोस् — तपाईंको कारण NULL को ठाउँ थियो कि खाली NULL भएकै? निर्णय गर्ने ठाउँले हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.6 Joins — reading two tables as one
items.en: Work backwards from where the NULL is. NULL on the right → left join. NULL on the left → right join. NULLs on both sides → full outer. No NULLs and fewer rows than either table → inner.
items.ne: NULL कता छ भन्नेबाट उल्टो सोच्नुहोस्। दायाँ NULL → left join। बायाँ NULL → right join। दुवैतिर NULL → full outer। NULL छैन र दुवै तालिकाभन्दा कम पङ्क्ति → inner।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The view holds no data of its own. Change a room in the Class table and the next SELECT * FROM StudentRoom shows the new value immediately — that is the sentence to write when a question asks how a view differs from a copy of a table.
items.ne: View सँग आफ्नो data हुँदैन। Class तालिकामा कोठा बदल्नुहोस्, अर्को पटक SELECT * FROM StudentRoom गर्दा नयाँ मान तुरुन्तै देखिन्छ — view र तालिकाको प्रतिलिपि कसरी फरक हुन् भनी सोध्दा यही वाक्य लेख्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Thinking WHERE chooses columns. WHERE marks > 60 does not put marks in the answer. Only the SELECT list decides which columns appear.
items.ne: WHERE ले स्तम्भ छान्छ भन्ने भ्रम। WHERE marks > 60 ले marks लाई उत्तरमा राख्दैन। कुन स्तम्भ देखिने भन्ने SELECT ले मात्र तय गर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Writing UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE. The statement is legal, so nothing warns you — it simply changes every row. Write the WHERE clause first, then the SET.
items.ne: WHERE नराखी UPDATE वा DELETE लेख्नु। कथन वैध हुने भएकाले चेतावनी आउँदैन — सबै पङ्क्ति बदलिन्छ। पहिले WHERE लेख्नुहोस्, अनि SET।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Comparing with NULL using =. WHERE class_id = NULL matches nothing, ever. NULL means "unknown", and nothing is equal to an unknown.
items.ne: NULL लाई = ले तुलना गर्नु। WHERE class_id = NULL ले कहिल्यै केही मिलाउँदैन। NULL को अर्थ "थाहा छैन" हो, र थाहा नभएकोसँग केही बराबर हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Forgetting the quotes on text. WHERE name = Ram asks the database for a column called Ram. It must be WHERE name = 'Ram'.
items.ne: पाठमा उद्धरण चिन्ह छुटाउनु। WHERE name = Ram ले Ram नामको स्तम्भ खोज्छ। WHERE name = 'Ram' हुनुपर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: This unit is the largest in the subject — 14 hours and the most marks. Questions come in three shapes: classify a statement as DDL, DML or DCL; write a short query from a description; and read a query and state its result. The writing questions are where the marks are, and they are marked on syntax as well as logic — so practise on paper, with the semicolon.
items.ne: यो युनिट विषयकै सबैभन्दा ठूलो हो — १४ घण्टा र सबैभन्दा धेरै अंक। प्रश्न तीन किसिमका आउँछन्: कथनलाई DDL, DML वा DCL मा छुट्याउने; विवरणबाट छोटो क्वेरी लेख्ने; र क्वेरी पढेर नतिजा भन्ने। अंक लेख्ने प्रश्नमा छन्, र तर्कसँगै वाक्यविन्यास पनि जाँचिन्छ — त्यसैले अर्धविरामसहित कागजमै अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Its three families are DDL (Data Definition Language — CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME), DML (Data Manipulation Language — SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) and DCL (Data Control Language — GRANT, REVOKE).
items.ne: परिभाषा र तीनै परिवारका नाम — प्रत्येकको पूरा नाम र दुई–तीन उदाहरण कथनसहित लेख्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Note the three things a marker looks for: quotes round 'Sales' because it is text, AND because both conditions must hold, and DESC because "highest first" is not the default.
items.ne: परीक्षकले हेर्ने तीन कुरा: पाठ भएकाले 'Sales' मा उद्धरण चिन्ह, दुवै सर्त चाहिने भएकाले AND, र "ठूलो पहिले" default नभएकाले DESC।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Any three clear differences earn the marks; the example statements make the answer unambiguous.
items.ne: स्पष्ट तीन भिन्नताले अंक दिन्छ; उदाहरण कथनले उत्तर अझ स्पष्ट बनाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: A SELECT runs FROM → WHERE → SELECT → ORDER BY. WHERE picks rows, SELECT picks columns, ORDER BY picks the order and removes nothing.
items.ne: SELECT यसरी चल्छ: FROM → WHERE → SELECT → ORDER BY। WHERE ले पङ्क्ति, SELECT ले स्तम्भ, ORDER BY ले क्रम — र यसले केही हटाउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: AND narrows the result, OR widens it. Text values need single quotes.
items.ne: AND ले नतिजा साँघुरो, OR ले फराकिलो बनाउँछ। पाठ मानलाई एकल उद्धरण चिन्ह चाहिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: DELETE removes rows and keeps the table; DROP removes the table itself. This is the difference examiners ask for most.
items.ne: DELETE ले पङ्क्ति हटाउँछ, तालिका राख्छ; DROP ले तालिका नै हटाउँछ। परीक्षकले सबैभन्दा धेरै सोध्ने भिन्नता यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE changes every row. It is legal, so nothing warns you.
items.ne: WHERE नभएको UPDATE वा DELETE ले सबै पङ्क्ति बदल्छ। वैध हुने भएकाले चेतावनी आउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: All five joins share one matching test; they differ only in what they keep of the rows that did not match. NULL in the result tells you which join it was.
items.ne: पाँचै join को मिलान जाँच उही हो; फरक केवल नमिलेका पङ्क्तिको के गर्ने भन्नेमा। नतिजाको NULL ले कुन join थियो भन्ने बताउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: A view is a stored SELECT that behaves like a table but holds no data of its own.
items.ne: View भनेको संग्रहित SELECT हो — तालिकाजस्तै व्यवहार गर्छ तर आफ्नो डाटा हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: SQL defines, manipulates and controls data in a relational database. Three families: DDL (structure), DML (data), DCL (permission).
items.ne: SQL ले रिलेसनल डाटाबेसको डाटा परिभाषित, सञ्चालन र नियन्त्रण गर्छ। तीन परिवार: DDL (संरचना), DML (डाटा), DCL (अधिकार)।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Definition — learn this wording SQL (Structured Query Language) is the standard language used to define, manipulate and control the data held in a relational database. It is not a programming language in the ordinary sense. You do not tell it how to find the rows — you state what you want, and the DBMS works out how. That is why one line of SQL can replace a page of loops. Almost every SQL statement is one sentence ending in a semicolon, and almost every one begins with a verb: SELECT, INSERT, CREATE, DROP. Reading the verb first tells you what is about to change.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्दमा सम्झनुहोस् SQL (Structured Query Language) रिलेसनल डाटाबेसमा रहेको डाटा परिभाषित गर्न, चलाउन र नियन्त्रण गर्न प्रयोग हुने मानक भाषा हो। यो साधारण अर्थमा प्रोग्रामिङ भाषा होइन। पङ्क्ति कसरी खोज्ने भन्नु पर्दैन — तपाईं के चाहियो भन्नुहुन्छ, कसरी निकाल्ने भन्ने DBMS ले हेर्छ। त्यसैले SQL को एक हरफले पूरा पानाको loop को काम गर्छ। प्रायः हरेक SQL कथन एउटा वाक्य हो, अन्त्यमा अर्धविराम। र प्रायः हरेक क्रियापदबाट सुरु हुन्छ: SELECT, INSERT, CREATE, DROP। पहिलो शब्द पढ्नेबित्तिकै के बदलिन लागेको हो थाहा हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.3 & 4.5 SELECT — asking the database a question
items.en: The shape of every query A SELECT answers one question: which rows, and which columns of them? Those two choices are made by two different clauses, and mixing them up is the most common mistake in this unit. WHERE chooses rows. It looks at each row in turn, tests the condition, and keeps the row or drops it. It can never change which columns appear. SELECT chooses columns. It cannot remove a row. ORDER BY chooses the order. It removes nothing at all — a result with three rows still has three rows after sorting.
items.ne: हरेक क्वेरीको बनावट SELECT ले एउटै प्रश्नको उत्तर दिन्छ: कुन पङ्क्ति, र तिनका कुन स्तम्भ? यी दुई छनोट फरक–फरक clause ले गर्छन्, र यिनै दुई मिसाउनु यस युनिटको सबैभन्दा सामान्य गल्ती हो। WHERE ले पङ्क्ति छान्छ। हरेक पङ्क्ति हेरेर सर्त जाँच्छ, अनि राख्छ वा हटाउँछ। कुन स्तम्भ देखिने भन्ने यसले बदल्न सक्दैन। SELECT ले स्तम्भ छान्छ। पङ्क्ति हटाउन सक्दैन। ORDER BY ले क्रम छान्छ। केही पनि हटाउँदैन — तीन पङ्क्ति भएको नतिजा क्रम मिलाएपछि पनि तीनै पङ्क्तिको हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.3 & 4.5 SELECT — asking the database a question
items.en: The five clauses the syllabus names WHERE tests one condition. AND joins two conditions that must both hold; OR joins two of which either will do. So WHERE marks > 60 AND class_id = 10 keeps fewer rows than WHERE marks > 60, and OR keeps more. If you cannot remember which way round, count rows: AND narrows, OR widens. ORDER BY sorts the result — ASC is the default, DESC reverses it. WITH gives a query a name so that the query after it can use that name like a table: WITH Toppers AS ( SELECT name, marks FROM Student WHERE marks > 80 ) SELECT name FROM Toppers ORDER BY marks DESC; One long nested query becomes two short readable ones, and the name can be used more than once. The difference from a view, which is 4.7, is the whole exam question: a view is stored in the database and stays until it is dropped; a WITH name exists only for the single statement that defines it and is gone the moment that statement finishes.
items.ne: पाठ्यक्रमले नाम लिएका पाँच clause WHERE ले एउटा सर्त जाँच्छ। AND ले दुवै पूरा हुनुपर्ने दुई सर्त जोड्छ; OR ले कुनै एक भए हुने दुई सर्त जोड्छ। त्यसैले WHERE marks > 60 AND class_id = 10 ले WHERE marks > 60 भन्दा थोरै पङ्क्ति राख्छ, र OR ले बढी। कुन कस्तो हो बिर्सिए पङ्क्ति गन्नुहोस्: AND ले साँघुरो बनाउँछ, OR ले फराकिलो। ORDER BY ले नतिजा क्रममा मिलाउँछ — ASC पूर्वनिर्धारित, DESC ले उल्टाउँछ। WITH ले क्वेरीलाई नाम दिन्छ, ताकि पछिको क्वेरीले त्यो नामलाई तालिकाजस्तै प्रयोग गर्न सकोस्: WITH Toppers AS ( SELECT name, marks FROM Student WHERE marks > 80 ) SELECT name FROM Toppers ORDER BY marks DESC; एउटा लामो नेस्टेड क्वेरी दुई छोटा पढ्न सजिला क्वेरी बन्छ, र त्यो नाम एकभन्दा बढी पटक प्रयोग गर्न सकिन्छ। View (४.७) सँगको फरक नै पूरै परीक्षा प्रश्न हो: view डाटाबेसमा भण्डारण हुन्छ र drop नगरेसम्म रहन्छ; WITH को नाम त्यसलाई बनाउने एउटै कथनभरि मात्र रहन्छ र कथन सकिनेबित्तिकै हराउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.2 DDL — building and removing the structure
items.en: The four DDL statements CREATE TABLE makes a new, empty table. You name each column and give it a data type, and you mark one column PRIMARY KEY. ALTER TABLE changes the structure of a table that already exists — adding a column, removing one, changing a type. The rows stay. DROP TABLE removes the table completely: its rows and its structure. After a DROP the name no longer exists. RENAME gives an existing table a new name. Nothing inside it changes.
items.ne: चार DDL कथन CREATE TABLE ले नयाँ, खाली तालिका बनाउँछ। हरेक स्तम्भको नाम र डाटा टाइप दिनुहुन्छ, र एउटालाई PRIMARY KEY तोक्नुहुन्छ। ALTER TABLE ले पहिले नै भएको तालिकाको संरचना बदल्छ — स्तम्भ थप्ने, हटाउने, टाइप बदल्ने। पङ्क्ति भने रहन्छन्। DROP TABLE ले तालिका पूरै हटाउँछ: पङ्क्ति र संरचना दुवै। DROP पछि त्यो नाम नै रहँदैन। RENAME ले भएकै तालिकालाई नयाँ नाम दिन्छ। भित्रको केही बदलिँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.6 Joins — reading two tables as one
items.en: Why a join is needed at all A normalised database splits information across tables on purpose. The student's name is in Student; the room is in Class. A question like "which room is Ram taught in?" touches both, so the two must be read together. That is a join. Every join starts the same way: a matching test, almost always foreign key = primary key. What separates the five kinds is only this — what happens to the rows that did not match. Inner throws them away. Left keeps all of the left table. Right keeps all of the right. Full outer keeps everything from both. Natural is an inner join that finds the shared column by itself.
items.ne: Join किन चाहिन्छ Normalise गरिएको डाटाबेसले जानाजान सूचना धेरै तालिकामा बाँड्छ। विद्यार्थीको नाम Student मा; कोठा Class मा। "राम कुन कोठामा पढ्छन्?" भन्ने प्रश्नले दुवै छुन्छ, त्यसैले दुवैलाई सँगै पढ्नुपर्छ। त्यही नै join हो। हरेक join उही तरिकाले सुरु हुन्छ: मिलान जाँच, प्रायः जसो foreign key = primary key। पाँच किसिमलाई छुट्याउने कुरा एउटै हो — नमिलेका पङ्क्तिको के हुन्छ। Inner ले फालिदिन्छ। Left ले बायाँ तालिकाका सबै राख्छ। Right ले दायाँका सबै। Full outer ले दुवैका सबै। Natural भनेको साझा स्तम्भ आफैं खोज्ने inner join हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.4 DCL — who is allowed to use the data
items.en: GRANT and REVOKE A school database is not read by one person. The class teacher may need to see marks; the office may need to change addresses; a student should see neither. DCL is how a database administrator sets those limits. GRANT gives a privilege to a user. REVOKE takes it back. GRANT SELECT ON Student TO teacher; GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON Student TO office; REVOKE UPDATE ON Student FROM office; Read the shape once and it is easy to reproduce: GRANT what ON which table TO whom, and REVOKE with FROM.
items.ne: GRANT र REVOKE विद्यालयको डाटाबेस एक जनाले मात्र पढ्दैन। कक्षा शिक्षकलाई अंक हेर्नु पर्ला; कार्यालयलाई ठेगाना बदल्नु पर्ला; विद्यार्थीले दुवै नहेरून्। यी सीमा तोक्ने काम DCL ले गर्छ। GRANT ले प्रयोगकर्तालाई अधिकार दिन्छ। REVOKE ले फिर्ता लिन्छ। बनावट एक पटक हेरे सम्झिन सजिलो छ: GRANT के ON कुन तालिका TO कसलाई, र REVOKE मा FROM आउँछ। यो साइटमा प्रयोगकर्ता र सर्भर नभएकाले सिमुलेटरले यी कथन चलाउँदैन — परीक्षामा पनि यिनको परिभाषा र वाक्यविन्यासबाटै सोधिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Definition — learn this wording A view is a stored SELECT statement that behaves like a table. It has a name and columns and can be queried, but it holds no data of its own — it reads from the real tables every time it is used. CREATE VIEW Passed AS SELECT name, marks FROM Student WHERE marks >= 40; Now SELECT * FROM Passed; works as though Passed were a table. Why views are used: they hide complexity (a long join becomes one name), and they restrict access — a teacher granted the view sees marks without being given the whole Student table.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्दमा सम्झनुहोस् View भनेको संग्रह गरिएको SELECT कथन हो, जुन तालिकाजस्तै व्यवहार गर्छ। यसको नाम र स्तम्भ हुन्छन् र query गर्न मिल्छ, तर आफ्नो डाटा हुँदैन — प्रयोग हुँदा हरेक पटक वास्तविक तालिकाबाटै पढ्छ। अब SELECT * FROM Passed; ले Passed लाई तालिकाजस्तै मानेर चल्छ। View किन प्रयोग हुन्छ: जटिलता लुकाउँछ (लामो join एउटा नाम बन्छ), र पहुँच सीमित गर्छ — view मात्र दिइएको शिक्षकले पूरै Student तालिका नपाई अंक हेर्न पाउँछन्।
