items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् The Student table has 4 rows. You run SELECT name FROM Student WHERE marks > 60; and three students scored above 60. How many rows and how many columns come back? Student तालिकामा ४ पङ्क्ति छन्। SELECT name FROM Student WHERE marks > 60; चलाउनुहुन्छ, र ६० भन्दा माथि तीन जनाले ल्याएका छन्। कति पङ्क्ति र कति स्तम्भ फर्किन्छ? 4 rows, 1 column 3 rows, 1 column 3 rows, 4 columns Two separate cuts. WHERE takes 4 rows down to 3. SELECT name takes 4 columns down to 1. Neither clause does the other one's job. Run it in the simulator below and watch both numbers change. दुई फरक कटाइ। WHERE ले ४ पङ्क्तिलाई ३ बनाउँछ। SELECT name ले ४ स्तम्भलाई १ बनाउँछ। एउटाले अर्कोको काम गर्दैन। तलको सिमुलेटरमा चलाएर दुवै सङ्ख्या बदलिएको हेर्नुहोस्। Interactive experiment
items.ne: · अन्तरक्रियात्मक प्रयोग

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · अन्तरक्रियात्मक प्रयोग The same query, five joins What you will learn: which rows each join keeps, by changing one word and watching the result grow. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: एउटै शब्द बदलेर नतिजा बढेको हेर्दै कुन join ले कुन पङ्क्ति राख्छ भन्ने। What to notice The teaching data has two deliberate gaps: Gita has no class, and room C-3 has no student. Those two gaps are the whole lesson. Press the join examples in order. Inner gives 3 rows — both gaps vanish. Left gives 4 — Gita comes back with NULL for her room. Right gives 4 — C-3 comes back with NULL for the name. Full outer gives 5 — both. If your data has no unmatched rows, all five joins return the same answer and you learn nothing from them. That is why this table was built with holes in it. पढाइका लागि दुई ठाउँ जानाजान खाली छन्: गीताको कक्षा छैन, र कोठा C-3 मा विद्यार्थी छैनन्। यी दुई खाली ठाउँ नै पूरा पाठ हुन्। उदाहरण क्रमैसँग थिच्नुहोस्। Inner ले ३ पङ्क्ति — दुवै खाली ठाउँ हराउँछन्। Left ले ४ — गीता कोठाको ठाउँमा NULL लिएर फर्किन्छिन्। Right ले ४ — C-3 नामको ठाउँमा NULL लिएर आउँछ। Full outer ले ५ — दुवै। नमिल्ने पङ्क्ति नै नभए पाँचै join ले उही उत्तर दिन्छन् र केही सिकिँदैन। Example 3 Which join produced this result? Question: a query on Student and Class returned four rows, and one of them had NULL in the room column. Which join was used, and why? Four joins are possible and only one fits. Name it before you open this, then check whether your reason was the NULL's position or only its presence — the position is what decides it. चार वटा join सम्भव छन्, मिल्ने एउटै हो। खोल्नुअघि नाम भन्नुहोस्, अनि जाँच्नुहोस् — तपाईंको कारण NULL को ठाउँ थियो कि खाली NULL भएकै? निर्णय गर्ने ठाउँले हो। Reasoning. A NULL on the right-hand column means a left row survived with no partner. An inner join would have dropped it, so it is not inner. A right join keeps unmatched right rows, which would put the NULL on the left instead. A full outer join would have returned five rows, not four. Answer LEFT OUTER JOIN Reason: every Student row was kept, and Gita had no matching Class row, so her room is NULL. Work backwards from where the NULL is. NULL on the right → left join. NULL on the left → right join. NULLs on both sides → full outer. No NULLs and fewer rows than either table → inner. NULL कता छ भन्नेबाट उल्टो सोच्नुहोस्। दायाँ NULL → left join। बायाँ NULL → right join। दुवैतिर NULL → full outer। NULL छैन र दुवै तालिकाभन्दा कम पङ्क्ति → inner। 4.4 DCL — who is allowed to use the data GRANT and REVOKE A school database is not read by one person. The class teacher may need to see marks; the office may need to change addresses; a student should see neither. DCL is how a database administrator sets those limits. GRANT gives a privilege to a user. REVOKE takes it back. GRANT SELECT ON Student TO teacher; GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON Student TO office; REVOKE UPDATE ON Student FROM office; Read the shape once and it is easy to reproduce: GRANT what ON which table TO whom, and REVOKE with FROM. GRANT र REVOKE विद्यालयको डाटाबेस एक जनाले मात्र पढ्दैन। कक्षा शिक्षकलाई अंक हेर्नु पर्ला; कार्यालयलाई ठेगाना बदल्नु पर्ला; विद्यार्थीले दुवै नहेरून्। यी सीमा तोक्ने काम DCL ले गर्छ। GRANT ले प्रयोगकर्तालाई अधिकार दिन्छ। REVOKE ले फिर्ता लिन्छ। बनावट एक पटक हेरे सम्झिन सजिलो छ: GRANT के ON कुन तालिका TO कसलाई, र REVOKE मा FROM आउँछ। यो साइटमा प्रयोगकर्ता र सर्भर नभएकाले सिमुलेटरले यी कथन चलाउँदैन — परीक्षामा पनि यिनको परिभाषा र वाक्यविन्यासबाटै सोधिन्छ। 4.7 SQL View Definition — learn this wording A view is a stored SELECT statement that behaves like a table. It has a name and columns and can be queried, but it holds no data of its own — it reads from the real tables every time it is used. CREATE VIEW Passed AS SELECT name, marks FROM Student WHERE marks >= 40; Now SELECT * FROM Passed; works as though Passed were a table. Why views are used: they hide complexity (a long join becomes one name), and they restrict access — a teacher granted the view sees marks without being given the whole Student table. परिभाषा — यही शब्दमा सम्झनुहोस् View भनेको संग्रह गरिएको SELECT कथन हो, जुन तालिकाजस्तै व्यवहार गर्छ। यसको नाम र स्तम्भ हुन्छन् र query गर्न मिल्छ, तर आफ्नो डाटा हुँदैन — प्रयोग हुँदा हरेक पटक वास्तविक तालिकाबाटै पढ्छ। अब SELECT * FROM Passed; ले Passed लाई तालिकाजस्तै मानेर चल्छ। View किन प्रयोग हुन्छ: जटिलता लुकाउँछ (लामो join एउटा नाम बन्छ), र पहुँच सीमित गर्छ — view मात्र दिइएको शिक्षकले पूरै Student तालिका नपाई अंक हेर्न पाउँछन्। Example 4 Writing a view, and saying why it is worth having Question: the office should be able to see each student's name and class room, but must not see marks. Write a view that gives them exactly that, and state two reasons a view is better here than handing over the tables. Step 1 — write the query first. A view is a stored SELECT, so start with the SELECT that returns the right columns: Working SELECT Student.name, Class.room FROM Student JOIN Class ON Student.class_id = Class.class_id; Step 2 — wrap it in CREATE VIEW and give it a name: Answer CREATE VIEW StudentRoom AS SELECT Student.name, Class.room FROM Student JOIN Class ON Student.class_id = Class.class_id; Now: SELECT * FROM StudentRoom; behaves exactly as though StudentRoom were a table. Two reasons a view is better than the tables: 1. SECURITY marks are not in the view, so the office cannot read them even by accident 2. SIMPLICITY the join is written once; the office never needs to know the two tables are separate The view holds no data of its own. Change a room in the Class table and the next SELECT * FROM StudentRoom shows the new value immediately — that is the sentence to write when a question asks how a view differs from a copy of a table. View सँग आफ्नो data हुँदैन। Class तालिकामा कोठा बदल्नुहोस्, अर्को पटक SELECT * FROM StudentRoom गर्दा नयाँ मान तुरुन्तै देखिन्छ — view र तालिकाको प्रतिलिपि कसरी फरक हुन् भनी सोध्दा यही वाक्य लेख्नुहोस्। Mistakes that cost marks here Using DELETE when the question says DROP. DELETE FROM Student; empties the table but leaves it standing — you can still insert into it tomorrow. DROP TABLE Student; removes the table itself. One is DML, the other is DDL. DROP भनेको ठाउँमा DELETE लेख्नु। DELETE FROM Student; ले तालिका खाली गर्छ तर तालिका रहन्छ। DROP TABLE Student; ले तालिका नै हटाउँछ। एउटा DML, अर्को DDL। Thinking WHERE chooses columns. WHERE marks > 60 does not put marks in the answer. Only the SELECT list decides which columns appear. WHERE ले स्तम्भ छान्छ भन्ने भ्रम। WHERE marks > 60 ले marks लाई उत्तरमा राख्दैन। कुन स्तम्भ देखिने भन्ने SELECT ले मात्र तय गर्छ। Writing UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE. The statement is legal, so nothing warns you — it simply changes every row. Write the WHERE clause first, then the SET. WHERE नराखी UPDATE वा DELETE लेख्नु। कथन वैध हुने भएकाले चेतावनी आउँदैन — सबै पङ्क्ति बदलिन्छ। पहिले WHERE लेख्नुहोस्, अनि SET। Comparing with NULL using =. WHERE class_id = NULL matches nothing, ever. NULL means "unknown", and nothing is equal to an unknown. NULL लाई = ले तुलना गर्नु। WHERE class_id = NULL ले कहिल्यै केही मिलाउँदैन। NULL को अर्थ "थाहा छैन" हो, र थाहा नभएकोसँग केही बराबर हुँदैन। Forgetting the quotes on text. WHERE name = Ram asks the database for a column called Ram. It must be WHERE name = 'Ram'. पाठमा उद्धरण चिन्ह छुटाउनु। WHERE name = Ram ले Ram नामको स्तम्भ खोज्छ। WHERE name = 'Ram' हुनुपर्छ। DELETE empties the table. DROP removes the table. DELETE ले तालिका खाली गर्छ। DROP ले तालिका हटाउँछ। Exam focus — what is asked from this unit This unit is the largest in the subject — 14 hours and the most marks. Questions come in three shapes: classify a statement as DDL, DML or DCL; write a short query from a description; and read a query and state its result. The writing questions are where the marks are, and they are marked on syntax as well as logic — so practise on paper, with the semicolon. यो युनिट विषयकै सबैभन्दा ठूलो हो — १४ घण्टा र सबैभन्दा धेरै अंक। प्रश्न तीन किसिमका आउँछन्: कथनलाई DDL, DML वा DCL मा छुट्याउने; विवरणबाट छोटो क्वेरी लेख्ने; र क्वेरी पढेर नतिजा भन्ने। अंक लेख्ने प्रश्नमा छन्, र तर्कसँगै वाक्यविन्यास पनि जाँचिन्छ — त्यसैले अर्धविरामसहित कागजमै अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्। 2 marks Practice question What is SQL? Name its three families of statements. SQL के हो? यसका तीन परिवारका नाम लेख्नुहोस्। Show the answer SQL (Structured Query Language) is the standard language used to define, manipulate and control the data in a relational database. Its three families are DDL (Data Definition Language — CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME), DML (Data Manipulation Language — SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) and DCL (Data Control Language — GRANT, REVOKE). परिभाषा र तीनै परिवारका नाम — प्रत्येकको पूरा नाम र दुई–तीन उदाहरण कथनसहित लेख्नुहोस्। 3 marks Practice question Write an SQL statement to create a table Book with a book id (the primary key), a title of up to 50 characters and a price. Book तालिका बनाउने SQL लेख्नुहोस् — book id (प्राथमिक कुञ्जी), बढीमा ५० अक्षरको शीर्षक, र मूल्य। Show the answer CREATE TABLE Book ( book_id INT PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR(50), price INT ); One mark for the CREATE TABLE line with brackets, one for the correct data types, one for PRIMARY KEY on book_id. कोष्ठकसहितको CREATE TABLE लाई एक अंक, सही डाटा टाइपलाई एक, र book_id मा PRIMARY KEY लाई एक। 3 marks Practice question A table Employee(emp_id, name, dept, salary) is given. Write a query to show the name and salary of every employee in the "Sales" department earning more than 30000, highest salary first. Employee(emp_id, name, dept, salary) तालिका दिइएको छ। "Sales" विभागमा ३०००० भन्दा बढी तलब पाउने सबैको नाम र तलब, ठूलो तलब पहिले आउने गरी देखाउने क्वेरी लेख्नुहोस्। Show the answer SELECT name, salary FROM Employee WHERE dept = 'Sales' AND salary > 30000 ORDER BY salary DESC; Note the three things a marker looks for: quotes round 'Sales' because it is text, AND because both conditions must hold, and DESC because "highest first" is not the default. परीक्षकले हेर्ने तीन कुरा: पाठ भएकाले 'Sales' मा उद्धरण चिन्ह, दुवै सर्त चाहिने भएकाले AND, र "ठूलो पहिले" default नभएकाले DESC। 3 marks Practice question Differentiate between DELETE and DROP with an example of each. DELETE र DROP बीचको भिन्नता उदाहरणसहित लेख्नुहोस्। Show the answer DELETE DROP ------ ---- DML DDL removes ROWS removes the TABLE structure stays structure goes too can use WHERE no WHERE table can be refilled table must be recreated DELETE FROM Student WHERE marks < 40; DROP TABLE Student; Any three clear differences earn the marks; the example statements make the answer unambiguous. स्पष्ट तीन भिन्नताले अंक दिन्छ; उदाहरण कथनले उत्तर अझ स्पष्ट बनाउँछ। Key points to revise

items.en: A join needs an ON condition saying which columns must match — for example ON Student.class_id = Class.class_id. Without it every row would pair with every row.

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: ON compares two columns with = . The joins in this syllabus all match on equality.
items.ne: ON ले दुई स्तम्भलाई = ले तुलना गर्छ। यस पाठ्यक्रमका सबै join बराबरीमा मिल्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.3 & 4.5 SELECT — asking the database a question
items.en: What you will learn: how a query narrows the data in stages, so you can work out a result on paper before you ever run it.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: क्वेरीले डाटालाई चरण–चरणमा कसरी साँघुरो पार्छ, जसले गर्दा नचलाईकनै कागजमा नतिजा निकाल्न सक्नुहुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.2 DDL — building and removing the structure
items.en: What you will learn: what INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE actually do to a table, and why DELETE and DROP are not the same thing.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: INSERT, UPDATE र DELETE ले तालिकामा साँच्चै के गर्छन्, र DELETE र DROP किन उस्तै होइनन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: 4.6 Joins — reading two tables as one
items.en: What you will learn: which rows each join keeps, by changing one word and watching the result grow.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: एउटै शब्द बदलेर नतिजा बढेको हेर्दै कुन join ले कुन पङ्क्ति राख्छ भन्ने।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Normalization removes the three anomalies caused by repeating a fact in many rows. Less space is a side effect, and queries often get slower, not faster, because more joins are needed.
items.ne: Normalization ले उही तथ्य धेरै पङ्क्तिमा दोहोरिँदा आउने तीन anomaly हटाउँछ। कम ठाउँ सहायक असर हो, र join बढ्ने भएकाले क्वेरी प्रायः छिटो होइन, ढिलो हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: 1NF requires every cell to hold a single atomic value. Two subjects in one cell is a repeating group, and splitting it into separate rows is the first step of normalising.
items.ne: 1NF ले हरेक कक्षमा एउटै अविभाज्य मान माग्छ। एउटै कक्षमा दुई विषय दोहोरिने समूह हो, र यसलाई छुट्टै पङ्क्तिमा बाँड्नु normalise गर्ने पहिलो चरण हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The key is both columns together, but name depends on only part of it. That is a partial dependency, and removing it is exactly what 2NF does. It can only happen when the key is composite.
items.ne: कुञ्जी दुवै स्तम्भ मिलेर हो, तर name त्यसको एक भागमा मात्र निर्भर छ। यही partial dependency हो, र 2NF ले हटाउने पनि यही। कुञ्जी composite भएमा मात्र यो सम्भव हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A non-key column depending on another non-key column is a transitive dependency, and 3NF forbids it. The fix is to move class_id and class_room into a Class table of their own.
items.ne: कुञ्जी नभएको स्तम्भ अर्को कुञ्जी नभएको स्तम्भमा निर्भर हुनु transitive dependency हो, र 3NF ले यसलाई निषेध गर्छ। समाधान: class_id र class_room लाई छुट्टै Class तालिकामा सार्ने।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Read it as "A determines B". student_id → name holds, because one id gives one name. The reverse usually does not: two students may share a name.
items.ne: "A ले B तय गर्छ" भनेर पढ्नुहोस्। student_id → name मिल्छ, किनभने एउटा id ले एउटै नाम दिन्छ। उल्टो प्रायः मिल्दैन: दुई विद्यार्थीको नाम उही हुन सक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Deleting one thing has destroyed an unrelated fact — the room still exists, but the database no longer knows about it. That is a deletion anomaly, and normalising into a separate Class table prevents it.
items.ne: एउटा कुरा हटाउँदा असम्बन्धित तथ्य नष्ट भयो — कोठा अझै छ, तर डाटाबेसलाई थाहा छैन। यही deletion anomaly हो, र छुट्टै Class तालिका बनाए रोकिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Each normal form removes exactly one named problem. 1NF removes repeating groups — a cell holding more than one value. 2NF removes partial dependency. 3NF removes transitive dependency. Say the name of the problem in your answer; that is what the marks are for.
items.ne: हरेक normal form ले ठ्याक्कै एउटा नामअङ्कित समस्या हटाउँछ। 1NF ले दोहोरिने समूह — एउटै कक्षमा एकभन्दा बढी मान। 2NF ले partial dependency। 3NF ले transitive dependency। उत्तरमा समस्याको नाम लेख्नुहोस्; अंक त्यसैको हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Saying normalization is done to save space. It is done to remove insertion, deletion and update anomalies. Space is a side effect.
items.ne: Normalization ठाउँ बचाउन गरिन्छ भन्नु। यो insertion, deletion र update anomaly हटाउन गरिन्छ। ठाउँ बचत सहायक असर हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: One badly designed table, normalised to 3NF step by step.
items.ne: नराम्रो डिजाइनको एउटा तालिकालाई चरण–चरणमा 3NF सम्म।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The starting table has two faults: one cell holds two subjects, and class_room is repeated on every row of the same class.
items.ne: सुरुको तालिकामा दुई दोष छन्: एउटै कक्षमा दुई विषय, र उही कक्षाका हरेक पङ्क्तिमा class_room दोहोरिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: 1NF: make every cell hold ONE value. Split the subject list into separate rows. The repeating group is gone.
items.ne: 1NF: हरेक कक्षमा एउटै मान राख्नुहोस्। विषयको सूचीलाई छुट्टै पङ्क्तिमा बाँड्नुहोस्। दोहोरिने समूह हट्यो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: 2NF: the key is now (id, subject), but name depends on id alone — a PARTIAL dependency. Split it out into two tables.
items.ne: 2NF: कुञ्जी अब (id, subject) हो, तर name id मा मात्र निर्भर छ — PARTIAL निर्भरता। दुई तालिकामा छुट्याउनुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: 3NF: class_room depends on class_id, which depends on id — a TRANSITIVE dependency. Move it to its own Class table. Now every column depends on the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key.
items.ne: 3NF: class_room, class_id मा निर्भर छ र class_id, id मा — TRANSITIVE निर्भरता। छुट्टै Class तालिकामा सार्नुहोस्। अब हरेक स्तम्भ कुञ्जीमा मात्र निर्भर हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Which normal form does this break?
items.ne: यसले कुन normal form तोड्छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Read the table, decide which rule it breaks first, and commit before you check. Work down the forms in order — a table that breaks 1NF is not yet worth testing against 2NF.
items.ne: तालिका पढ्नुहोस्, पहिले कुन नियम तोड्छ छान्नुहोस्, अनि जाँच्नुहोस्। क्रमैसँग हेर्नुहोस् — 1NF नै नतोडेको तालिकालाई मात्र 2NF मा जाँच्ने हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Already in 3NF
items.ne: पहिले नै 3NF मा

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: One cell holds two values. 1NF requires every cell to be atomic, so this fails at the first form — split it into one row per subject before testing anything else.
items.ne: एउटै कक्षमा दुई मान छन्। 1NF ले हरेक कक्ष अविभाज्य हुनुपर्ने माग्छ, त्यसैले पहिलो रूपमै असफल — अरू जाँच्नुअघि हरेक विषयलाई छुट्टै पङ्क्तिमा बाँड्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The key is both columns together, but student_name depends on roll alone — a PARTIAL dependency, which is exactly what 2NF forbids. Every cell is atomic, so 1NF is satisfied.
items.ne: कुञ्जी दुवै स्तम्भ मिलेर हो, तर student_name roll मा मात्र निर्भर छ — PARTIAL निर्भरता, जुन 2NF ले निषेध गर्छ। हरेक कक्ष अविभाज्य भएकाले 1NF पूरा भएको छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: class_room depends on class_id, which is not a key — a TRANSITIVE dependency. The key is a single column so there is no part of it to depend on, which is why 2NF is already satisfied.
items.ne: class_room, class_id मा निर्भर छ र class_id कुञ्जी होइन — TRANSITIVE निर्भरता। कुञ्जी एउटै स्तम्भ भएकाले त्यसको "भाग" हुँदैन, त्यसैले 2NF पहिले नै पूरा छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Atomic values, a single-column key so no partial dependency is possible, and the one non-key column depends on the key directly. Nothing left to remove — this is 3NF.
items.ne: अविभाज्य मान, एउटै स्तम्भको कुञ्जी भएकाले partial निर्भरता सम्भव छैन, र कुञ्जी नभएको एउटै स्तम्भ सिधै कुञ्जीमा निर्भर छ। हटाउनुपर्ने केही छैन — यो 3NF हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: customer_id and customer_city both depend on order_id alone, not on the whole key — partial dependency, so 2NF fails first. A transitive dependency is also present, but you fix the earlier form first.
items.ne: customer_id र customer_city दुवै order_id मा मात्र निर्भर छन्, पूरै कुञ्जीमा होइन — partial निर्भरता, त्यसैले पहिले 2NF असफल। Transitive निर्भरता पनि छ, तर पहिलेको रूप पहिले सुधार्ने।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: All three kinds on one table, so they can be told apart rather than recited. Read where the arrow starts — the whole key, part of the key, or a column that is not the key at all. That single question decides which normal form a table has broken, and it is the same table the normalisation walkthrough below uses.
items.ne: तीनै किसिम एउटै तालिकामा, ताकि घोकेर होइन, छुट्याएर भन्न सकियोस्। तीर कहाँबाट सुरु हुन्छ हेर्नुहोस् — पूरै कुञ्जीबाट, कुञ्जीको एक भागबाट, कि कुञ्जी नै नभएको स्तम्भबाट। यही एउटा प्रश्नले तालिकाले कुन normal form भङ्ग गर्‍यो निर्णय गर्छ, र तल normalization हेर्दा पनि यही तालिका चल्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Normalise a small table to 3NF, naming the anomaly removed at each step.
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा: functional dependency परिभाषित गर्न र A → B पढ्न, full–partial–transitive निर्भरता चिन्न, normalization के हो र किन चाहिन्छ भन्न, 1NF–2NF–3NF का नियम भन्न, र सानो तालिकालाई हरेक चरणमा हट्ने समस्याको नाम दिँदै 3NF सम्म लैजान सक्नुहुनेछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Three tables, and now each fact is written once. Change room A-1 and you change one row, not forty. That is the anomaly gone, which is the whole point — write that sentence in your answer and you have shown you understand normalization rather than memorised it.
items.ne: तीन तालिका, र अब हरेक तथ्य एक पटक मात्र लेखिएको छ। कोठा A-1 बदल्दा एउटै पङ्क्ति बदलिन्छ, चालीस होइन। anomaly हट्यो — उत्तरमा यही वाक्य लेख्नुभयो भने घोकेको होइन, बुझेको देखिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Read the reason even when you are right. On the last case nothing is wrong at all — recognising a table that is already in 3NF is as examinable as fixing one that is not.
items.ne: सधैं क्रमैसँग हेर्नुहोस्: हरेक कक्ष अविभाज्य छ? अनि partial निर्भरता छ? अनि transitive? पहिलो "छैन" नै उत्तर हो। सही भए पनि कारण पढ्नुहोस् — अन्तिम केसमा केही गलत छैन, र पहिले नै 3NF मा भएको तालिका चिन्न सक्नु पनि उत्तिकै सोधिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The key is a pair. Before you open this, name the normal form that fails — and say which half of the key each non-key column hangs off. The name of the form follows from that answer, not the other way round.
items.ne: Key जोडीमा छ। खोल्नुअघि भङ्ग हुने normal form भन्नुहोस् — र हरेक non-key स्तम्भ key को कुन आधामा अडेको छ पनि भन्नुहोस्। form को नाम त्यही उत्तरबाट आउँछ, उल्टो होइन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Notice the key is composite, which is what makes a partial dependency possible at all. If the key had been a single column, this table would already have been in 2NF and you would have gone straight to looking for a transitive dependency.
items.ne: कुञ्जी composite छ — त्यसैले partial निर्भरता सम्भव भयो। कुञ्जी एउटै स्तम्भको भएको भए यो तालिका पहिले नै 2NF मा हुन्थ्यो र सिधै transitive निर्भरता खोज्नुपर्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Jumping straight to 3NF. The marks are for the steps. Show 1NF, then 2NF, then 3NF, and name the problem removed at each one.
items.ne: सिधै 3NF मा पुग्नु। अंक चरणका लागि हुन्। 1NF, 2NF, 3NF देखाउनुहोस् र हरेकमा हटेको समस्याको नाम लेख्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Looking for a partial dependency when the key is a single column. There is no "part" of a one-column key, so a table with a simple key that is in 1NF is automatically in 2NF.
items.ne: एउटै स्तम्भको कुञ्जीमा partial dependency खोज्नु। एक–स्तम्भे कुञ्जीको "भाग" हुँदैन, त्यसैले 1NF मा भएको त्यस्तो तालिका आफैं 2NF मा हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Forgetting the foreign key after splitting. When Class is split out, Student must keep class_id to point back at it — otherwise the link is lost.
items.ne: छुट्याएपछि foreign key बिर्सनु। Class छुट्टिएपछि Student मा class_id रहनुपर्छ, नत्र जोडाइ हराउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: This unit is examined by doing, not by describing. The standard question hands you one badly designed table and asks you to normalise it to 3NF. It is worth several marks and they are given per step, so a partial answer that gets to 2NF correctly still earns most of them — but only if you show the intermediate tables and name the dependency you removed. Never present just the final three tables.
items.ne: यो युनिट वर्णन गरेर होइन, गरेर जाँचिन्छ। सामान्य प्रश्नले नराम्रो डिजाइनको एउटा तालिका दिएर 3NF सम्म लैजान भन्छ। अंक चरणअनुसार दिइन्छ, त्यसैले 2NF सम्म सही पुगेको अपूरो उत्तरले पनि धेरै अंक पाउँछ — तर बीचका तालिका देखाएर हटेको निर्भरताको नाम लेखेमा मात्र। अन्तिम तीन तालिका मात्र नलेख्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: It is needed because a table that repeats the same fact in many rows can be left inconsistent when one copy is changed and the others are not.
items.ne: परिभाषा र किन चाहिन्छ — तीनै anomaly को नाम लिनुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: One mark each. Note that 2NF and 3NF both begin by requiring the previous form.
items.ne: एक–एक अंक। 2NF र 3NF दुवै अघिल्लो रूपको माग गर्दै सुरु हुन्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: One mark for each normal form reached correctly, and one for naming the dependency removed at each step.
items.ne: सही पुगेको हरेक normal form लाई एक अंक, र हरेक चरणमा हटेको निर्भरताको नाम लेखेकोमा एक।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: A → B means A determines B — one value of A gives exactly one value of B.
items.ne: A → B को अर्थ A ले B तय गर्छ — A को एउटा मानले B को ठ्याक्कै एउटा मान दिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: 1NF removes repeating groups. 2NF removes partial dependency. 3NF removes transitive dependency. One form, one named problem.
items.ne: 1NF ले दोहोरिने समूह, 2NF ले partial dependency, 3NF ले transitive dependency हटाउँछ। एउटा रूप, एउटा नामअङ्कित समस्या।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: A partial dependency needs a composite key. With a single-column key, 1NF already gives you 2NF.
items.ne: Partial dependency लाई composite कुञ्जी चाहिन्छ। एक–स्तम्भे कुञ्जीमा 1NF ले नै 2NF दिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Each form includes the ones before it, so always work 1NF → 2NF → 3NF and show the intermediate tables.
items.ne: हरेक रूपले अघिल्लोलाई समेट्छ, त्यसैले सधैं 1NF → 2NF → 3NF क्रममा काम गर्नुहोस् र बीचका तालिका देखाउनुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: After splitting a table, keep the foreign key that points back — otherwise the link between them is lost.
items.ne: तालिका छुट्याएपछि फर्केर देखाउने foreign key राख्नुहोस्, नत्र जोडाइ हराउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Name the normal form, then name the dependency that blocks the next one
items.ne: नर्मल फर्म पहिचान गर्नुहोस्, अनि अर्को फर्ममा जान नदिने dependency नाम लिनुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: 1NF: no repeating groups — every cell holds one value. 2NF: 1NF and no PARTIAL dependency — no non-key column depends on only part of a composite key. 3NF: 2NF and no TRANSITIVE dependency — no non-key column depends on another non-key column.
items.ne: 1NF: दोहोरिने समूह छैन — हरेक कक्षमा एउटै मान। 2NF: 1NF र PARTIAL dependency छैन — कुनै non-key स्तम्भ composite key को एक भागमा मात्र निर्भर छैन। 3NF: 2NF र TRANSITIVE dependency छैन — कुनै non-key स्तम्भ अर्को non-key स्तम्भमा निर्भर छैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Student(roll, name, subject1, subject2, subject3). Which normal form is it in, and what must change?
items.ne: Student(roll, name, subject1, subject2, subject3)। यो कुन नर्मल फर्ममा छ, र के बदल्नुपर्छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Does any column hold a repeating group? Answer yes or no
items.ne: कुनै स्तम्भमा दोहोरिने समूह छ? yes वा no

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: subject1, subject2 and subject3 are the same fact repeated across three columns. That is a repeating group.
items.ne: subject1, subject2, subject3 एउटै तथ्य तीन स्तम्भमा दोहोरिएको हो। यो दोहोरिने समूह हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: So which normal form is it in? Answer 0NF, 1NF, 2NF or 3NF
items.ne: त्यसैले यो कुन फर्ममा छ? 0NF, 1NF, 2NF वा 3NF

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A table with a repeating group has not reached 1NF yet.
items.ne: दोहोरिने समूह भएको तालिका अझै 1NF मा पुगेको छैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Which form does splitting the repeated columns into rows reach?
items.ne: दोहोरिएका स्तम्भलाई पङ्क्तिमा छुट्याउँदा कुन फर्म आइपुग्छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Student(roll, name, subject) with one subject per row holds one value in every cell, which is exactly what 1NF asks.
items.ne: Student(roll, name, subject) — प्रति पङ्क्ति एउटा subject राख्दा हरेक कक्षमा एउटै मान हुन्छ, जुन 1NF ले माग्ने कुरा हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: After the fix, which form is the table in?
items.ne: सच्याएपछि तालिका कुन फर्ममा हुन्छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The repeating group is what 1NF forbids. Nothing about keys has been examined yet — that is the next question, not this one.
items.ne: दोहोरिने समूह नै 1NF ले निषेध गर्ने कुरा हो। key बारे अझै केही हेरिएको छैन — त्यो अर्को प्रश्न हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Marks(roll, subject, student_name, marks) — the key is (roll, subject). It is already in 1NF. Which form is it in, and why can it go no further?
items.ne: Marks(roll, subject, student_name, marks) — key (roll, subject) हो। यो 1NF मा छ। यो कुन फर्ममा छ, र किन अगाडि बढ्न सक्दैन?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: student_name depends on which part of the key? Answer roll, subject or both
items.ne: student_name key को कुन भागमा निर्भर छ? roll, subject वा both

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A student's name is fixed by their roll number alone. The subject has nothing to do with it.
items.ne: विद्यार्थीको नाम roll ले मात्र निश्चित हुन्छ। subject को यसमा कुनै भूमिका छैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A non-key column depending on PART of a composite key is called what? Answer partial or transitive
items.ne: composite key को एक भागमा मात्र निर्भर non-key स्तम्भलाई के भनिन्छ? partial वा transitive

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Part of the key, so partial. Transitive is the other one — a non-key column depending on another NON-KEY column.
items.ne: key को एक भाग, त्यसैले partial। transitive अर्को हो — non-key स्तम्भ अर्को NON-KEY स्तम्भमा निर्भर।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A partial dependency breaks which form? Answer 2NF or 3NF
items.ne: partial dependency ले कुन फर्म भङ्ग गर्छ? 2NF वा 3NF

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: 2NF is exactly "1NF and no partial dependency". So the table stops at 1NF.
items.ne: 2NF भनेकै "1NF र partial dependency छैन" हो। त्यसैले तालिका 1NF मै रोकिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Which form is this table in?
items.ne: यो तालिका कुन फर्ममा छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: It reaches 1NF and stops there, because student_name depends on roll alone. Splitting Student(roll, student_name) away takes it to 2NF.
items.ne: यो 1NF सम्म पुगेर रोकिन्छ, किनभने student_name roll मा मात्र निर्भर छ। Student(roll, student_name) छुट्याएपछि 2NF मा पुग्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Book(book_id, title, publisher_id, publisher_city) — the key is book_id alone. Which form is it in?
items.ne: Book(book_id, title, publisher_id, publisher_city) — key book_id मात्र हो। यो कुन फर्ममा छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Repeating group? yes or no
items.ne: दोहोरिने समूह? yes वा no

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Every cell holds one value, so 1NF is satisfied.
items.ne: हरेक कक्षमा एउटै मान छ, त्यसैले 1NF पुगेको छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Can there be a partial dependency here? yes or no
items.ne: यहाँ partial dependency हुन सक्छ? yes वा no

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The key is a single column. A partial dependency needs a COMPOSITE key to be partial to, so 2NF is automatic here.
items.ne: key एउटै स्तम्भ हो। partial dependency हुन COMPOSITE key चाहिन्छ, त्यसैले यहाँ 2NF आफैं पुग्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: publisher_city depends on which column?
items.ne: publisher_city कुन स्तम्भमा निर्भर छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The city belongs to the publisher, not to the book. And publisher_id is not the key.
items.ne: सहर प्रकाशकको हो, पुस्तकको होइन। र publisher_id key होइन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A non-key column depending on another non-key column is called what?
items.ne: non-key स्तम्भ अर्को non-key स्तम्भमा निर्भर हुनुलाई के भनिन्छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: book_id → publisher_id → publisher_city. The dependency travels through a middle column, so it is transitive, and 3NF forbids it.
items.ne: book_id → publisher_id → publisher_city। निर्भरता बीचको स्तम्भबाट जान्छ, त्यसैले transitive, र 3NF ले यसलाई निषेध गर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: So which form is Book in?
items.ne: त्यसैले Book कुन फर्ममा छ?

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: 1NF yes, 2NF yes (single-column key), 3NF no — the transitive dependency stops it. Split Publisher(publisher_id, publisher_city) away to reach 3NF.
items.ne: 1NF छ, 2NF छ (एउटै स्तम्भको key), 3NF छैन — transitive dependency ले रोक्छ। Publisher(publisher_id, publisher_city) छुट्याएपछि 3NF मा पुगिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Order(order_id, product_id, quantity, product_name) — the key is (order_id, product_id). Which normal form is it in? Answer 1NF, 2NF or 3NF.
items.ne: Order(order_id, product_id, quantity, product_name) — key (order_id, product_id) हो। यो कुन नर्मल फर्ममा छ? 1NF, 2NF वा 3NF।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Normal form
items.ne: नर्मल फर्म

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: product_name depends on product_id alone — part of the composite key. That is a partial dependency, so 2NF fails and the table stops at 1NF. If you answered 2NF, you probably checked for a transitive dependency and missed the partial one: always test the key BEFORE the non-key columns.
items.ne: product_name product_id मा मात्र निर्भर छ — composite key को एक भाग। यो partial dependency हो, त्यसैले 2NF पुग्दैन र तालिका 1NF मै रोकिन्छ। 2NF भन्नुभयो भने सम्भवतः transitive खोज्दै partial छुटाउनुभयो: सधैं non-key भन्दा पहिले key जाँच्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Normalization removes insertion, deletion and update anomalies. Saving space is a side effect, not the reason.
items.ne: Normalization ले insertion, deletion र update anomaly हटाउँछ। ठाउँ बचत कारण होइन, सहायक असर हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Why a table can be "wrong" even when it works A table can hold correct data today and still be badly designed. The test is what happens when it changes. Put the class's room number on every student row, and you have written the same fact forty times. Change the room and you must find all forty. Miss one and the database now disagrees with itself. That is an update anomaly. Delete the last student in a class, and the room number disappears with them, even though the room still exists — a deletion anomaly. And a new class with no students yet cannot be recorded at all — an insertion anomaly. Normalization exists to remove these three anomalies. Saving disk space is a side effect, not the purpose.
items.ne: काम गरिरहेको तालिका पनि किन "गलत" हुन सक्छ तालिकामा आज सही data होला, तर डिजाइन नराम्रो हुन सक्छ। जाँच त्यो बदलिँदा के हुन्छ भन्नेमा हो। कक्षाको कोठा नम्बर हरेक विद्यार्थीको पङ्क्तिमा राख्नुभयो भने उही तथ्य चालीस पटक लेखिन्छ। कोठा बदल्दा चालीसै ठाउँ खोज्नुपर्छ। एउटा छुट्यो भने डाटाबेस आफैंसँग बाझिन्छ। यही update anomaly हो। कक्षाको अन्तिम विद्यार्थी हटाउँदा कोठा नम्बर पनि सँगै हराउँछ, कोठा भने रहन्छ — deletion anomaly। र विद्यार्थी नभएको नयाँ कक्षा राख्नै सकिँदैन — insertion anomaly। Normalization यी तीन anomaly हटाउन छ। डिस्क बचत यसको उद्देश्य होइन, सहायक असर हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Definition — learn this wording Attribute B is functionally dependent on attribute A, written A → B, if each value of A determines exactly one value of B. Read A → B as "A determines B". In a Student table, student_id → name: give me the id and the name is fixed. The reverse is not true — two students may share a name, so name → student_id does not hold. Full dependency — B depends on the whole key. Partial dependency — B depends on only part of a composite key. Transitive dependency — A → B and B → C, so A → C through a non-key column. Those three names are the whole of this topic, and each one is removed by one normal form.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्दमा सम्झनुहोस् एट्रिब्युट B, एट्रिब्युट A मा functionally dependent छ — A → B लेखिन्छ — यदि A को हरेक मानले B को ठ्याक्कै एउटा मान तय गर्छ भने। A → B लाई "A ले B तय गर्छ" भनेर पढ्नुहोस्। Student तालिकामा student_id → name: id दिए नाम निश्चित हुन्छ। उल्टो भने होइन — दुई विद्यार्थीको नाम उही हुन सक्छ। Full dependency — B पूरै कुञ्जीमा निर्भर। Partial dependency — B composite कुञ्जीको एक भाग मा मात्र निर्भर। Transitive dependency — A → B र B → C, त्यसैले कुञ्जी नभएको स्तम्भ हुँदै A → C। यी तीन नाम नै यो टपिकको सार हुन्, र हरेकलाई एउटा normal form ले हटाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The three rules, stated exactly First Normal Form (1NF). A relation is in 1NF if every attribute holds only atomic (single) values and there are no repeating groups. Second Normal Form (2NF). A relation is in 2NF if it is in 1NF and every non-key attribute is fully functionally dependent on the whole primary key — that is, no partial dependency. Third Normal Form (3NF). A relation is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and no non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute — that is, no transitive dependency. Notice the shape: each form includes the one before it. A table cannot be in 3NF without already being in 2NF and 1NF, which is why they are always applied in order.
items.ne: तीन नियम, ठ्याक्कै First Normal Form (1NF). हरेक एट्रिब्युटले अविभाज्य (एउटै) मान मात्र राखेको र दोहोरिने समूह नभएको रिलेसन 1NF मा हुन्छ। Second Normal Form (2NF). 1NF मा भएको र हरेक कुञ्जी–बाहेकको एट्रिब्युट पूरै primary key मा पूर्ण रूपमा निर्भर भएको — अर्थात् partial dependency नभएको। Third Normal Form (3NF). 2NF मा भएको र कुनै पनि कुञ्जी–बाहेकको एट्रिब्युट अर्को कुञ्जी–बाहेकको एट्रिब्युटमा निर्भर नभएको — अर्थात् transitive dependency नभएको। बनावट हेर्नुहोस्: हरेक रूपले अघिल्लोलाई समेट्छ। 1NF र 2NF नभई 3NF हुन सक्दैन, त्यसैले क्रमैसँग लागू गरिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् A table has the composite key (student_id, subject) and also holds the student's name. What kind of dependency is student_id → name? एउटा तालिकाको composite कुञ्जी (student_id, subject) छ र विद्यार्थीको नाम पनि छ। student_id → name कस्तो निर्भरता हो? Full Partial Transitive Partial. The key is both columns together, but name depends on only student_id — half the key. That is the definition of a partial dependency, and it is exactly what 2NF removes. A partial dependency is only possible when the key is composite; with a single-column key there is no "part" of it to depend on. Partial। कुञ्जी दुवै स्तम्भ मिलेर हो, तर name student_id मा मात्र निर्भर छ — आधा कुञ्जीमा। partial dependency को परिभाषा यही हो, र 2NF ले हटाउने पनि यही। कुञ्जी composite भएमा मात्र partial dependency सम्भव हुन्छ। {{dia:dbDependencies}} All three kinds on one table, so they can be told apart rather than recited. Read where the arrow starts — the whole key, part of the key, or a column that is not the key at all. That single question decides which normal form a table has broken, and it is the same table the normalisation walkthrough below uses. तीनै किसिम एउटै तालिकामा, ताकि घोकेर होइन, छुट्याएर भन्न सकियोस्। तीर कहाँबाट सुरु हुन्छ हेर्नुहोस् — पूरै कुञ्जीबाट, कुञ्जीको एक भागबाट, कि कुञ्जी नै नभएको स्तम्भबाट। यही एउटा प्रश्नले तालिकाले कुन normal form भङ्ग गर्‍यो निर्णय गर्छ, र तल normalization हेर्दा पनि यही तालिका चल्छ। 5.2 & 5.3 Normalization to 3NF {{dia:normalForms}} The three rules, stated exactly First Normal Form (1NF). A relation is in 1NF if every attribute holds only atomic (single) values and there are no repeating groups. Second Normal Form (2NF). A relation is in 2NF if it is in 1NF and every non-key attribute is fully functionally dependent on the whole primary key — that is, no partial dependency. Third Normal Form (3NF). A relation is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and no non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute — that is, no transitive dependency. Notice the shape: each form includes the one before it. A table cannot be in 3NF without already being in 2NF and 1NF, which is why they are always applied in order. तीन नियम, ठ्याक्कै First Normal Form (1NF). हरेक एट्रिब्युटले अविभाज्य (एउटै) मान मात्र राखेको र दोहोरिने समूह नभएको रिलेसन 1NF मा हुन्छ। Second Normal Form (2NF). 1NF मा भएको र हरेक कुञ्जी–बाहेकको एट्रिब्युट पूरै primary key मा पूर्ण रूपमा निर्भर भएको — अर्थात् partial dependency नभएको। Third Normal Form (3NF). 2NF मा भएको र कुनै पनि कुञ्जी–बाहेकको एट्रिब्युट अर्को कुञ्जी–बाहेकको एट्रिब्युटमा निर्भर नभएको — अर्थात् transitive dependency नभएको। बनावट हेर्नुहोस्: हरेक रूपले अघिल्लोलाई समेट्छ। 1NF र 2NF नभई 3NF हुन सक्दैन, त्यसैले क्रमैसँग लागू गरिन्छ। Example 1 Normalising a table to 3NF, step by step Question: normalise this table to 3NF, naming the problem removed at each step. Given Student( roll, name, class_id, class_room, subjects ) roll name class_id class_room subjects 1 Ram 10 A-1 Maths, Science 2 Sita 10 A-1 Maths 3 Hari 11 B-2 Science Step 1 — 1NF. The subjects cell holds two values. Split it so every cell holds one value; the key becomes (roll, subject): 1NF Student( roll, subject, name, class_id, class_room ) 1 Maths Ram 10 A-1 1 Science Ram 10 A-1 2 Maths Sita 10 A-1 3 Science Hari 11 B-2 Problem removed: repeating group Step 2 — 2NF. The key is (roll, subject), but name, class_id and class_room depend on roll alone — a partial dependency. Split the table: 2NF Student( roll, name, class_id, class_room ) Takes ( roll, subject ) Problem removed: partial dependency Step 3 — 3NF. In Student, class_room depends on class_id, which depends on roll — a transitive dependency through a non-key column. Move it out: 3NF — answer Student( roll, name, class_id ) FK → Class.class_id Class ( class_id, class_room ) Takes ( roll, subject ) Problem removed: transitive dependency Three tables, and now each fact is written once. Change room A-1 and you change one row, not forty. That is the anomaly gone, which is the whole point — write that sentence in your answer and you have shown you understand normalization rather than memorised it. तीन तालिका, र अब हरेक तथ्य एक पटक मात्र लेखिएको छ। कोठा A-1 बदल्दा एउटै पङ्क्ति बदलिन्छ, चालीस होइन। anomaly हट्यो — उत्तरमा यही वाक्य लेख्नुभयो भने घोकेको होइन, बुझेको देखिन्छ। Practise the judgement
items.ne: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Which normal form does this table break? What you will learn: to spot the FIRST rule a table breaks, which is the whole skill the exam question tests. Knowing the three definitions is not the same as being able to apply them to a table you have not seen. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: तालिकाले पहिले कुन नियम तोड्छ भनी चिन्न — परीक्षाले जाँच्ने सीप यही हो। तीन परिभाषा जान्नु र नदेखेको तालिकामा लागू गर्न सक्नु फरक कुरा हुन्। How to use this Work down the forms in order every time: is every cell atomic? then is there a partial dependency? then a transitive one? The first "no" is your answer, and a table that breaks 1NF is not yet worth testing against 2NF. Read the reason even when you are right. On the last case nothing is wrong at all — recognising a table that is already in 3NF is as examinable as fixing one that is not. सधैं क्रमैसँग हेर्नुहोस्: हरेक कक्ष अविभाज्य छ? अनि partial निर्भरता छ? अनि transitive? पहिलो "छैन" नै उत्तर हो। सही भए पनि कारण पढ्नुहोस् — अन्तिम केसमा केही गलत छैन, र पहिले नै 3NF मा भएको तालिका चिन्न सक्नु पनि उत्तिकै सोधिन्छ। Example 2 Naming the dependency before you split Question: in Enrol( student_id, course_id, student_name, course_fee ) with the key (student_id, course_id), name every dependency and say which normal form fails. The key is a pair. Before you open this, name the normal form that fails — and say which half of the key each non-key column hangs off. The name of the form follows from that answer, not the other way round. Key जोडीमा छ। खोल्नुअघि भङ्ग हुने normal form भन्नुहोस् — र हरेक non-key स्तम्भ key को कुन आधामा अडेको छ पनि भन्नुहोस्। form को नाम त्यही उत्तरबाट आउँछ, उल्टो होइन। Step 1 — write the dependencies out. This is the step students skip, and it is where the marks are: Working student_id → student_name course_id → course_fee (student_id, course_id) → nothing else Step 2 — test each against the key. Both student_name and course_fee depend on half the key, not the whole of it. Two partial dependencies. Answer Fails 2NF — partial dependency (two of them). Enrol ( student_id, course_id ) Student( student_id, student_name ) Course ( course_id, course_fee ) Notice the key is composite, which is what makes a partial dependency possible at all. If the key had been a single column, this table would already have been in 2NF and you would have gone straight to looking for a transitive dependency. कुञ्जी composite छ — त्यसैले partial निर्भरता सम्भव भयो। कुञ्जी एउटै स्तम्भको भएको भए यो तालिका पहिले नै 2NF मा हुन्थ्यो र सिधै transitive निर्भरता खोज्नुपर्थ्यो। Practise it — the help comes away
items.ne: · अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् — सहयोग घट्दै जान्छ

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: · अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् — सहयोग घट्दै जान्छ Mistakes that cost marks here Saying normalization is done to save space. It is done to remove insertion, deletion and update anomalies. Space is a side effect. Normalization ठाउँ बचाउन गरिन्छ भन्नु। यो insertion, deletion र update anomaly हटाउन गरिन्छ। ठाउँ बचत सहायक असर हो। Jumping straight to 3NF. The marks are for the steps. Show 1NF, then 2NF, then 3NF, and name the problem removed at each one. सिधै 3NF मा पुग्नु। अंक चरणका लागि हुन्। 1NF, 2NF, 3NF देखाउनुहोस् र हरेकमा हटेको समस्याको नाम लेख्नुहोस्। Looking for a partial dependency when the key is a single column. There is no "part" of a one-column key, so a table with a simple key that is in 1NF is automatically in 2NF. एउटै स्तम्भको कुञ्जीमा partial dependency खोज्नु। एक–स्तम्भे कुञ्जीको "भाग" हुँदैन, त्यसैले 1NF मा भएको त्यस्तो तालिका आफैं 2NF मा हुन्छ। Forgetting the foreign key after splitting. When Class is split out, Student must keep class_id to point back at it — otherwise the link is lost. छुट्याएपछि foreign key बिर्सनु। Class छुट्टिएपछि Student मा class_id रहनुपर्छ, नत्र जोडाइ हराउँछ। Normalise to remove anomalies, not to save space. Space is a side effect. Anomaly हटाउन normalise गरिन्छ, ठाउँ बचाउन होइन। ठाउँ त सँगै आउने कुरा हो। Exam focus — what is asked from this unit This unit is examined by doing, not by describing. The standard question hands you one badly designed table and asks you to normalise it to 3NF. It is worth several marks and they are given per step, so a partial answer that gets to 2NF correctly still earns most of them — but only if you show the intermediate tables and name the dependency you removed. Never present just the final three tables. यो युनिट वर्णन गरेर होइन, गरेर जाँचिन्छ। सामान्य प्रश्नले नराम्रो डिजाइनको एउटा तालिका दिएर 3NF सम्म लैजान भन्छ। अंक चरणअनुसार दिइन्छ, त्यसैले 2NF सम्म सही पुगेको अपूरो उत्तरले पनि धेरै अंक पाउँछ — तर बीचका तालिका देखाएर हटेको निर्भरताको नाम लेखेमा मात्र। अन्तिम तीन तालिका मात्र नलेख्नुहोस्। 2 marks Practice question Define normalization. Why is it needed? Normalization को परिभाषा दिनुहोस्। यो किन चाहिन्छ? Show the answer Normalization is the process of organising the attributes and relations of a database to reduce data redundancy and remove undesirable characteristics such as insertion, deletion and update anomalies. It is needed because a table that repeats the same fact in many rows can be left inconsistent when one copy is changed and the others are not. परिभाषा र किन चाहिन्छ — तीनै anomaly को नाम लिनुहोस्। 3 marks Practice question State the conditions for 1NF, 2NF and 3NF. 1NF, 2NF र 3NF का सर्त लेख्नुहोस्। Show the answer 1NF every attribute holds atomic (single) values, and there are no repeating groups 2NF in 1NF, AND every non-key attribute is fully dependent on the whole primary key (no partial dependency) 3NF in 2NF, AND no non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute (no transitive dependency) One mark each. Note that 2NF and 3NF both begin by requiring the previous form. एक–एक अंक। 2NF र 3NF दुवै अघिल्लो रूपको माग गर्दै सुरु हुन्छन्। 4 marks Practice question Normalise the following to 3NF, showing each step: Order( order_id, item, customer_id, customer_city ), where an order may contain several items. निम्नलाई चरणसहित 3NF सम्म लैजानुहोस्: Order( order_id, item, customer_id, customer_city ), जहाँ एउटा अर्डरमा धेरै सामान हुन सक्छन्। Show the answer 1NF one row per item, key = (order_id, item) Order( order_id, item, customer_id, customer_city ) removed: repeating group 2NF customer_id and customer_city depend on order_id alone — a PARTIAL dependency Order( order_id, customer_id, customer_city ) Items( order_id, item ) removed: partial dependency 3NF customer_city depends on customer_id, which depends on order_id — a TRANSITIVE dependency Order ( order_id, customer_id ) Customer( customer_id, customer_city ) Items ( order_id, item ) removed: transitive dependency One mark for each normal form reached correctly, and one for naming the dependency removed at each step. सही पुगेको हरेक normal form लाई एक अंक, र हरेक चरणमा हटेको निर्भरताको नाम लेखेकोमा एक। Key points to revise
items.ne: — दोहोर्‍याउनुपर्ने मुख्य बुँदा

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Relational Database Design
items.ne: रिलेसनल डाटाबेस डिजाइन

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: What you will learn: to spot the FIRST rule a table breaks, which is the whole skill the exam question tests. Knowing the three definitions is not the same as being able to apply them to a table you have not seen.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: तालिकाले पहिले कुन नियम तोड्छ भनी चिन्न — परीक्षाले जाँच्ने सीप यही हो। तीन परिभाषा जान्नु र नदेखेको तालिकामा लागू गर्न सक्नु फरक कुरा हुन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A transaction is usually several statements, not one. What makes it a transaction is the all-or-nothing promise: a bank transfer is a debit and a credit, and neither may happen alone.
items.ne: ट्रान्ज्याक्सनमा प्रायः धेरै कथन हुन्छन्, एउटा होइन। यसलाई ट्रान्ज्याक्सन बनाउने कुरा "पूरै वा बिल्कुल होइन" भन्ने वचन हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Durability protects work that has committed. Atomicity is the opposite promise — it undoes work that had NOT committed. The test is always whether a COMMIT happened.
items.ne: Durability ले commit भइसकेको काम जोगाउँछ। Atomicity उल्टो वचन हो — commit नभएको काम फिर्ता लैजान्छ। जाँच सधैं COMMIT भयो कि भएन भन्ने हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: With no COMMIT record in the log, recovery undoes everything the transaction did. That is atomicity: half a transfer may not survive. Had it committed, redo would have re-applied it instead.
items.ne: Log मा COMMIT रेकर्ड नभएकाले recovery ले ट्रान्ज्याक्सनले गरेका सबै काम उल्टाउँछ। यही atomicity हो: आधा रकम सारेको बाँच्न पाउँदैन। Commit भएको भए redo ले फेरि लागू गर्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Every transaction ends in exactly one of these two. Active, partially committed and failed are all states it passes through on the way.
items.ne: हरेक ट्रान्ज्याक्सन यी दुईमध्ये ठ्याक्कै एउटामा टुङ्गिन्छ। Active, partially committed र failed बाटोमा पर्ने अवस्था हुन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The first withdrawal has vanished. Neither clerk did anything wrong — each did correct arithmetic on a value that was correct when read. The fault is uncontrolled interleaving, which locks prevent.
items.ne: पहिलो निकासी हरायो। कसैले गलत गरेको होइन — दुवैले पढ्दाको सही मानमा सही गणित गरे। दोष अनियन्त्रित क्रम मिसिनुमा छ, जसलाई lock ले रोक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: ROLLBACK returns the database to the state it was in before the transaction began. COMMIT is the opposite — it makes the changes permanent. Exactly one of the two ends a transaction.
items.ne: ROLLBACK ले डाटाबेसलाई ट्रान्ज्याक्सन सुरु हुनुअघिकै अवस्थामा फर्काउँछ। COMMIT उल्टो हो — परिवर्तनलाई स्थायी बनाउँछ। ट्रान्ज्याक्सन यीमध्ये एउटाले टुङ्गिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: COMMIT and ROLLBACK. COMMIT makes every change of the transaction permanent — after it, the work survives a crash. ROLLBACK undoes every change the transaction made, returning the database to the state it was in before the transaction began. Exactly one of the two ends a transaction.
items.ne: COMMIT ले ट्रान्ज्याक्सनका सबै परिवर्तन स्थायी बनाउँछ — त्यसपछि crash भए पनि काम बाँच्छ। ROLLBACK ले गरेका सबै परिवर्तन फिर्ता लैजान्छ र डाटाबेसलाई सुरुको अवस्थामा पुर्‍याउँछ। ट्रान्ज्याक्सन यी दुईमध्ये ठ्याक्कै एउटाले टुङ्गिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Leaving FAILED and ABORTED out of the state diagram. The failure path is half the diagram and usually half the marks.
items.ne: अवस्था चित्रमा FAILED र ABORTED नराख्नु। असफल बाटो चित्रको आधा हो र प्रायः अंकको पनि आधा।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: A transaction from start to finish, including the path that fails.
items.ne: ट्रान्ज्याक्सन सुरुदेखि अन्त्यसम्म, असफल हुने बाटोसहित।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: ACTIVE — the transaction has started and its statements are running.
items.ne: ACTIVE — ट्रान्ज्याक्सन सुरु भयो र यसका कथन चलिरहेका छन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: PARTIALLY COMMITTED — the last statement has run, but the changes are not yet safely on disk.
items.ne: PARTIALLY COMMITTED — अन्तिम कथन चल्यो, तर परिवर्तन अझै डिस्कमा सुरक्षित छैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: COMMITTED — the changes are permanent. This is the only state that keeps the work, and durability is the promise that a crash now cannot undo it.
items.ne: COMMITTED — परिवर्तन स्थायी भयो। काम बाँच्ने एउटै अवस्था यही हो, र अब crash भए पनि नहराओस् भन्ने वचन नै durability हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: FAILED — something went wrong, at any point. A transaction can fail from ACTIVE or from PARTIALLY COMMITTED.
items.ne: FAILED — जुनसुकै बेला केही बिग्रियो। ACTIVE वा PARTIALLY COMMITTED दुवैबाट असफल हुन सक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: ABORTED — the database rolls back every change the transaction made, so it is as if it never ran. That is atomicity doing its job.
items.ne: ABORTED — डाटाबेसले ट्रान्ज्याक्सनले गरेका सबै परिवर्तन फिर्ता लैजान्छ, चलेकै थिएन जस्तो। atomicity ले गर्ने काम यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Learn each property by the disaster it prevents. A definition you can attach to a failure is a definition you can reproduce under pressure.
items.ne: हरेक गुणलाई त्यसले रोक्ने विपत्तिबाट सम्झनुहोस्। असफलतासँग जोडिएको परिभाषा परीक्षामा सजिलै सम्झिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Say what COMMIT and ROLLBACK each do.
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा: ट्रान्ज्याक्सनको परिभाषा दिन र बैंक रकम सार्दा किन एउटै ट्रान्ज्याक्सन हुनुपर्छ भन्न, concurrency के हो र यसले ल्याउने समस्या नाम लिन, ACID का चार गुण व्याख्या गर्न, असफल हुने बाटोसहित अवस्था कोर्न, र COMMIT–ROLLBACK ले के गर्छ भन्न सक्नुहुनेछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Now switch to One at a time. The lock forces clerk 2 to read after clerk 1 has written, so they start from 4000 and the final balance is 2000. Same two transactions, same arithmetic, different order.
items.ne: दुवै एकैचोटि मा चरण–चरण जानुहोस् र तीन बाकस हेर्नुहोस्। चरण २ मै दुवै कर्मचारीसँग ५००० छ — केही बिग्रेको देखिनुभन्दा चार चरण अगाडि नै समस्या सुरु भइसक्यो। गणित कहिल्यै गलत हुँदैन; कर्मचारी २ ले सुरु गरेको मान मात्र पुरानो भइसकेको थियो। कसैले गल्ती गर्दैन, तैपनि पैसा हराउँछ। अब एक–एक गरी मा जानुहोस्: lock ले कर्मचारी २ लाई कर्मचारी १ ले लेखेपछि मात्र पढ्न दिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The whole schedule is above. Work out the balance the database is left holding, and the balance it should have held — the gap between those two numbers is the name of the problem.
items.ne: पूरा schedule माथि छ। डाटाबेसमा अन्तमा बाँकी रहने रकम, र रहनुपर्ने रकम निकाल्नुहोस् — ती दुई सङ्ख्याको फरक नै समस्याको नाम हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: The giveaway in any schedule is two reads before the first write. Look for that pattern and you can name the problem without tracing the arithmetic at all.
items.ne: कुनै पनि schedule मा सङ्केत यही हो: पहिलो write अघि दुई read। यो ढाँचा भेटे गणित नै नगरी समस्याको नाम भन्न सकिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: If the crash had come after COMMIT, the answer would be Ram 4000 and Sita 3000 — and the property being enforced would be durability instead. The COMMIT record is the only thing that decides which.
items.ne: Crash COMMIT पछि आएको भए उत्तर राम ४००० र सीता ३००० हुन्थ्यो — र लागू हुने गुण durability हुन्थ्यो। कुन हो भन्ने तय गर्ने एउटै कुरा COMMIT रेकर्ड हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Confusing atomicity with durability. Atomicity protects an uncommitted transaction by undoing it; durability protects a committed one by keeping it.
items.ne: Atomicity र durability मिसाउनु। Atomicity ले commit नभएको फिर्ता लैजान्छ; durability ले commit भएको जोगाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Describing a transaction as "one SQL statement". It is one logical unit of work, which is usually several statements.
items.ne: ट्रान्ज्याक्सनलाई "एउटा SQL कथन" भन्नु। यो एउटा तार्किक काम हो, जसमा प्रायः धेरै कथन हुन्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Saying concurrency is bad and should be avoided. It is necessary; what must be avoided is uncontrolled concurrency.
items.ne: Concurrency नराम्रो हो, हटाउनुपर्छ भन्नु। यो आवश्यक हो; हटाउनुपर्ने कुरा अनियन्त्रित concurrency हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Two questions come from this unit almost every year. The first asks you to explain the ACID properties — four marks, one per property, and each answer is one clear sentence plus an example of what goes wrong without it. The second asks for the transaction state diagram, where the marks are for including the failure path, which is the half most answers leave out.
items.ne: यस युनिटबाट प्रायः हरेक वर्ष दुई प्रश्न आउँछन्। पहिलोले ACID गुण व्याख्या गर्न भन्छ — चार अंक, हरेकलाई एक, र हरेक उत्तर एउटा स्पष्ट वाक्य र नभए के बिग्रन्छ भन्ने उदाहरण। दोस्रोले ट्रान्ज्याक्सनको अवस्था चित्र माग्छ, जहाँ अंक असफल बाटो समावेश गरेकोमा हुन्छ — प्रायः उत्तरमा छुट्ने आधा त्यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: One mark per property. Naming the property, stating the promise and giving the failure it prevents is a complete answer to each.
items.ne: हरेक गुणलाई एक अंक। नाम, वचन र नभए के बिग्रन्छ — यत्ति भए पूरा उत्तर।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: One mark for ACTIVE → PARTIALLY COMMITTED → COMMITTED, one for the FAILED → ABORTED path from both earlier states, and one for naming the two final states.
items.ne: पहिलो लहरलाई एक अंक, दुवै अवस्थाबाट FAILED → ABORTED बाटोलाई एक, र दुई अन्तिम अवस्थाका नाम लेखेकोमा एक।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: COMMIT makes the changes permanent; ROLLBACK undoes them. One of the two ends every transaction.
items.ne: COMMIT ले परिवर्तन स्थायी बनाउँछ; ROLLBACK ले फिर्ता लैजान्छ। हरेक ट्रान्ज्याक्सन यीमध्ये एउटाले टुङ्गिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: ACID: Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (rules always hold), Isolation (no half-done work is visible), Durability (committed work survives a crash).
items.ne: ACID: Atomicity (सबै वा केही होइन), Consistency (नियम सधैं पालना), Isolation (आधा काम नदेखिने), Durability (commit भएको crash पछि पनि रहने)।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Atomicity undoes an uncommitted transaction; durability keeps a committed one. The COMMIT record decides which applies.
items.ne: Atomicity ले commit नभएको फिर्ता लैजान्छ; durability ले commit भएको राख्छ। COMMIT रेकर्डले तय गर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: States: ACTIVE → PARTIALLY COMMITTED → COMMITTED, or → FAILED → ABORTED. Only COMMITTED and ABORTED are final.
items.ne: अवस्था: ACTIVE → PARTIALLY COMMITTED → COMMITTED, वा → FAILED → ABORTED। अन्तिम अवस्था COMMITTED र ABORTED मात्र।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: Concurrency is necessary, not optional. Uncontrolled concurrency causes the lost update problem; locks prevent it.
items.ne: Concurrency आवश्यक हो, वैकल्पिक होइन। अनियन्त्रित भए lost update समस्या आउँछ; lock ले रोक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: A transaction is one logical unit of work that must happen completely or not at all.
items.ne: ट्रान्ज्याक्सन भनेको एउटै तार्किक काम हो — पूरै हुनुपर्ने वा बिल्कुल नहुनुपर्ने।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Definition — learn this wording A transaction is a single logical unit of work made up of one or more database operations, which must be carried out completely or not at all. The standard example is a bank transfer of Rs 1000 from Ram to Sita. It is two operations: 1. Ram's balance = Ram's balance − 1000 2. Sita's balance = Sita's balance + 1000 Neither line is a transfer on its own. If the power fails between them, Rs 1000 has left Ram's account and arrived nowhere. Grouping them into one transaction is the promise that this cannot happen: either both lines take effect, or neither does.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्दमा सम्झनुहोस् ट्रान्ज्याक्सन भनेको एक वा बढी डाटाबेस कार्य मिलेर बनेको एउटै तार्किक काम हो, जुन पूरै हुनुपर्छ वा बिल्कुल हुनुहुँदैन। सामान्य उदाहरण: रामबाट सीतालाई रु १००० पठाउनु। यो दुई काम हो। कुनै एक हरफ आफैंमा रकम सार्नु होइन। दुईबीच बिजुली गयो भने रु १००० रामको खाताबाट निस्क्यो तर कतै पुगेन। दुवैलाई एउटै ट्रान्ज्याक्सनमा राख्नु भनेको यस्तो हुन नदिने वचन हो: या दुवै लागू हुन्छन्, या कुनै पनि हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Why two users at once is a problem Concurrency is several transactions running at the same time. A database with one user at a time would be safe and useless — a bank has thousands of users at once — so concurrency is necessary, and the DBMS must control it. The classic failure is the lost update. Two clerks both read a balance of 5000. One subtracts 1000 and writes 4000. The other, working from the value it read before that, subtracts 2000 and writes 3000. The first withdrawal has vanished — the balance should be 2000. Nothing was written incorrectly. Each clerk did correct arithmetic on a value that was correct when they read it. The fault is entirely in the interleaving, which is why the DBMS controls it with locks: a row being changed is locked until the transaction ends.
items.ne: एकैचोटि दुई प्रयोगकर्ता किन समस्या Concurrency भनेको धेरै ट्रान्ज्याक्सन एकैचोटि चल्नु हो। एक पटकमा एक जना मात्र चलाउने डाटाबेस सुरक्षित त होला, तर काम लाग्दैन — बैंकमा हजारौं प्रयोगकर्ता एकैचोटि हुन्छन् — त्यसैले concurrency चाहिन्छ, र DBMS ले नियन्त्रण गर्नुपर्छ। क्लासिक समस्या lost update हो। दुई कर्मचारीले ५००० मौज्दात पढे। एउटाले १००० घटाएर ४००० लेख्यो। अर्कोले, त्योभन्दा अघि पढेको मानबाट २००० घटाएर ३००० लेख्यो। पहिलो निकासी हरायो — मौज्दात २००० हुनुपर्थ्यो। कसैले गलत लेखेको होइन। दुवैले पढ्दाको सही मानमा सही गणित गरे। दोष पूरै क्रम मिसिनु मा छ, त्यसैले DBMS ले lock ले नियन्त्रण गर्छ: बदलिँदै गरेको पङ्क्ति ट्रान्ज्याक्सन नसकिँदासम्म बन्द रहन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/dbms
items.en: Reading the state diagram A transaction begins in ACTIVE and stays there while its statements run. When the last statement finishes it moves to PARTIALLY COMMITTED — the work is done in memory but not yet safely on disk. From there, if all is well it reaches COMMITTED and the changes are permanent. If anything goes wrong — at any point, from either of the first two states — it moves to FAILED, and from FAILED it is rolled back to ABORTED. An aborted transaction leaves no trace. The database is exactly as it was before the transaction started, which is atomicity being enforced. Only COMMITTED and ABORTED are final. Every transaction ends in one of them.
items.ne: अवस्था चित्र पढ्ने तरिका ट्रान्ज्याक्सन ACTIVE बाट सुरु हुन्छ र कथन चलेसम्म त्यहीँ रहन्छ। अन्तिम कथन सकिएपछि PARTIALLY COMMITTED मा जान्छ — काम मेमोरीमा सकियो तर डिस्कमा सुरक्षित भइसकेको छैन। त्यहाँबाट सबै ठीक भए COMMITTED मा पुग्छ र परिवर्तन स्थायी हुन्छ। केही बिग्रियो भने — पहिलो दुई अवस्थामध्ये जुनसुकैबाट — FAILED मा जान्छ, र FAILED बाट फिर्ता लगिएर ABORTED हुन्छ। Abort भएको ट्रान्ज्याक्सनले कुनै चिन्ह छाड्दैन। डाटाबेस सुरु हुनुअघिकै अवस्थामा रहन्छ — यही atomicity लागू भएको हो। COMMITTED र ABORTED मात्र अन्तिम अवस्था हुन्। हरेक ट्रान्ज्याक्सन यीमध्ये एउटामा टुङ्गिन्छ।
