items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् A driver uses a steering wheel without knowing how the engine works. Which feature of OOP does that describe? चालकले इन्जिन कसरी चल्छ नजानीकनै स्टेयरिङ चलाउँछन्। यसले OOP को कुन विशेषता जनाउँछ? Encapsulation Abstraction Inheritance Abstraction. Complexity is hidden and only what you need is shown. The test that separates the two: abstraction hides COMPLEXITY, encapsulation hides DATA. A private variable with a getter is encapsulation; a dashboard that shows speed without the mechanism is abstraction. Unit 4 spends a whole section on this pair — it is asked most years. Abstraction। जटिलता लुकाइएको छ र चाहिने कुरा मात्र देखाइएको छ। छुट्याउने जाँच: abstraction ले जटिलता लुकाउँछ, encapsulation ले डाटा। Getter सहितको private चल encapsulation हो; संयन्त्र नदेखाई गति देखाउने ड्यासबोर्ड abstraction हो। Practise the judgement
items.ne: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Name the feature from what the program does What you will learn: to name an OOP feature from a described situation, which is how this unit is actually examined — not by reciting the list. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: वर्णन गरिएको परिस्थितिबाट OOP विशेषताको नाम दिन — यो युनिट यसरी नै जाँचिन्छ, सूची घोकेर होइन। How to use this For each case ask one question before you answer: what is being hidden? Data hidden behind functions is encapsulation. Complexity hidden behind a simple interface is abstraction. A class taking members from another is inheritance. One name behaving in more than one form is polymorphism. Two cases are both polymorphism — one decided by the compiler, one decided while the program runs. Read the reasons: the exam asks you to name which kind. उत्तर दिनुअघि एउटै प्रश्न सोध्नुहोस्: के लुकाइँदै छ? फङ्सनपछाडि लुकेको डाटा = encapsulation। सरल अन्तरमुखपछाडि लुकेको जटिलता = abstraction। अर्कोका मेम्बर लिने क्लास = inheritance। एउटै नाम धेरै रूपमा = polymorphism। दुई केस polymorphism कै हुन् — एउटा compiler ले, अर्को चल्दै गर्दा तय हुन्छ। 2.5 Tokens and Character Set Token A token is the smallest individual unit of a C++ program that has meaning to the compiler. When the compiler reads your program it first breaks it into tokens. The character set is every character C++ understands: letters A–Z and a–z, digits 0–9, special symbols such as + - * / = < > ( ) { } ; ,, and white space (space, tab, newline). टोकन टोकन भनेको C++ प्रोग्रामको सबैभन्दा सानो अर्थपूर्ण एकाइ हो, जुन कम्पाइलरले बुझ्छ। कम्पाइलरले प्रोग्राम पढ्दा पहिले यसलाई टोकनमा टुक्र्याउँछ। Character set भनेको C++ ले बुझ्ने सबै अक्षर हो: A–Z, a–z, ०–९, विशेष चिन्ह + - * / = ( ) { } ;, र खाली ठाउँ। Type of tokenMeaningExamples KeywordsReserved words with a fixed meaning. You cannot use them as your own names. पहिल्यै अर्थ तोकिएका शब्द — आफ्नो नामका रूपमा प्रयोग गर्न मिल्दैन। int, class, if, else, return, void, public IdentifiersNames the programmer creates for variables, functions and classes. प्रोग्रामरले भेरिएबल, फङ्सन र क्लासलाई राखेको नाम। roll, sum, Student, display Constants / LiteralsFixed values that never change while the program runs. प्रोग्राम चल्दा नबदलिने मान। 25, 3.14, 'A', "Ram", true OperatorsSymbols that perform an operation on values. मानमाथि काम गर्ने चिन्ह। + - * / % = == < > && << Punctuators / SeparatorsSymbols that separate or group parts of the program. प्रोग्रामका भाग छुट्याउने वा समूह बनाउने चिन्ह। ; , ( ) { } [ ] # StringsA sequence of characters written inside double quotes. डबल कोट भित्रका अक्षरहरूको शृंखला। "Hello Gyansetu" Example 1 Find the tokens in one line of code int sum = a + 25; Count the tokens in that line and write your number down before opening this. Almost everyone who gets it wrong forgets the same one — and it is the character at the very end. त्यो लाइनका token गन्नुहोस् र खोल्नुअघि आफ्नो सङ्ख्या लेख्नुहोस्। बिराउनेहरू प्रायः उही एउटा बिर्सन्छन् — र त्यो सबैभन्दा अन्तिमको अक्षर हो। This single line contains seven tokens: int (keyword), sum (identifier), = (operator), a (identifier), + (operator), 25 (constant), ; (punctuator). Questions like "identify the tokens in the given statement" are common — count carefully. यो एउटै लाइनमा सात टोकन छन्। "दिइएको कथनमा token पहिचान गर्नुहोस्" भन्ने प्रश्न बारम्बार आउँछ — ध्यान दिएर गन्नुहोस्। 2.6 Data Types and Format Data typeSizeWhat it storesExample int4 bytesWhole numbers, no decimal point दशमलव नभएको पूर्ण संख्याint roll = 15; float4 bytesDecimal numbers, about 6 digits of precision दशमलव भएको संख्याfloat m = 78.5; double8 bytesDecimal numbers with higher precision अझ शुद्ध दशमलव संख्याdouble p = 3.14159; char1 byteA single character in single quotes सिंगल कोटमा एउटा अक्षरchar g = 'A'; bool1 byteOnly true (1) or false (0) true वा false मात्रbool pass = true; void—"No value" — used when a function returns nothing कुनै मान नहुनेvoid show() stringvariesA sequence of characters; needs <string> अक्षरहरूको शृंखलाstring n = "Ram"; 2.7 Basic Input and Output cout and cin cout << sends data out to the screen. << is called the insertion operator. cin >> takes data in from the keyboard. >> is called the extraction operator. Both are objects defined in the header file <iostream> and both live inside the namespace std. endl moves the cursor to a new line. Memory trick: the arrows point in the direction the data travels. cout << x — data flows out of x into cout. cin >> x — data flows from cin into x. cout र cin cout << ले डाटा स्क्रिनमा बाहिर पठाउँछ। << लाई insertion operator भनिन्छ। cin >> ले किबोर्डबाट डाटा भित्र लिन्छ। >> लाई extraction operator भनिन्छ। दुवै <iostream> हेडर फाइलमा भएका अब्जेक्ट हुन् र std नेमस्पेस भित्र बस्छन्। endl ले नयाँ लाइनमा लैजान्छ। सम्झने तरिका: तीर जता फर्किएको छ, डाटा त्यतै जान्छ। 2.8 Basic Program Structure {{dia:programAnatomy}} Every C++ program has these same parts. Learn to label them. हरेक C++ प्रोग्राममा यीनै भाग हुन्छन्। नाम दिन सिक्नुहोस्। Example 2 A complete program that reads input #include <iostream> using namespace std; int main() { int a, b, sum; cout << "Enter two numbers: "; cin >> a >> b; // read both values sum = a + b; cout << "Sum = " << sum << endl; return 0; } Output (if the user types 12 and 8) Enter two numbers: 12 8 Sum = 20 Practise it — the help comes away
items.ne: · अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् — सहयोग घट्दै जान्छ

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् — सहयोग घट्दै जान्छ Common mistakes in program structure Forgetting using namespace std; — then cout is undefined and you must write std::cout. Writing cin << a; instead of cin >> a; — the arrows are the wrong way round. Missing the semicolon ; at the end of a statement. Writing Main() or MAIN() — C++ is case sensitive, it must be main(). यी चार गल्ती सबैभन्दा बढी हुन्छन्: namespace बिर्सने, cin मा तीर उल्टो लेख्ने, सेमीकोलन छुटाउने, र main लाई ठूलो अक्षरमा लेख्ने। C++ मा सानो–ठूलो अक्षरले फरक पार्छ। cin >> takes in, cout << puts out. The arrows point where the data goes. cin >> ले भित्र लिन्छ, cout << ले बाहिर पठाउँछ। तीरले डाटा जाने दिशा देखाउँछ। 2.9 Control Statements StatementWhat it doesSyntax ifRuns a block only when the condition is true.सर्त सही भएमा मात्र चल्छ।if(cond){ ... } if…elseOne block if true, another block if false.सही भए एउटा, गलत भए अर्को ब्लक।if(cond){}else{} if…else ladderChecks many conditions one by one from the top down.माथिबाट धेरै सर्त क्रमशः जाँच्छ।if(){}else if(){}else{} Nested ifAn if inside another if.एउटा if भित्र अर्को if।if(a){ if(b){} } switchChooses one case out of many by matching a value. Each case needs break.मान मिलाएर धेरैमध्ये एउटा case छान्छ।switch(x){ case 1: ... } forRepeats a block a known number of times.कति पटक दोहोरिने थाहा हुँदा।for(i=0;i<n;i++){} whileRepeats while a condition is true. The condition is checked first — entry controlled. May run zero times.सर्त पहिले जाँच्छ, त्यसैले ० पटक पनि चल्न सक्छ।while(cond){} do…whileRuns the block at least once, then checks the condition — exit controlled.कम्तीमा एक पटक चल्छ, अनि मात्र सर्त जाँच्छ।do{ }while(cond); breakExits the loop or switch immediately.तुरुन्तै लुप वा switch बाट बाहिर निस्कन्छ।break; continueSkips the rest of this round and jumps to the next round.यो चक्र छोडेर अर्को चक्रमा जान्छ।continue; Example 3 if…else ladder — printing a grade #include <iostream> using namespace std; int main() { int marks = 78; if (marks >= 90) cout << "Grade A+"; else if (marks >= 75) cout << "Grade A"; else if (marks >= 60) cout << "Grade B"; else cout << "Grade C"; return 0; } marks is 78. Name the grade that prints, and say how many of the four tests are actually evaluated before the program stops testing. A ladder is not four separate ifs, and that is the marks difference. marks = ७८ छ। कुन grade छापिन्छ भन्नुहोस्, र प्रोग्रामले परीक्षण रोक्नुअघि चारमध्ये कति परीक्षण साँच्चै गर्छ पनि भन्नुहोस्। ladder भनेको छुट्टाछुट्टै चार वटा if होइन, र अङ्कको फरक त्यहीँ छ। Output Grade A The ladder is checked from the top. 78 fails the first test (78 >= 90 is false) but passes the second (78 >= 75 is true), so it prints Grade A and stops — the remaining conditions are never checked. माथिबाट क्रमशः जाँचिन्छ। ७८ पहिलो सर्तमा असफल भयो तर दोस्रोमा सफल भयो, त्यसैले "Grade A" छापेर रोकियो — बाँकी सर्त जाँचिँदैनन्। Example 4 while vs do…while — the difference that gets tested int i = 10; while (i < 5) { // condition is FALSE at the start cout << "while runs"; } // body runs ZERO times int j = 10; do { cout << "do-while runs"; // body runs ONCE first } while (j < 5); // then the condition fails Output do-while runs Same condition, same starting value — but while printed nothing and do…while printed once. That is the whole difference: while checks first, do…while acts first. उही सर्त, उही सुरुको मान — तर while ले केही छापेन र do…while ले एक पटक छाप्यो। फरक यही हो: while ले पहिले जाँच्छ, do…while ले पहिले काम गर्छ। Exam focus — questions asked from this unit SEE exam connection
items.ne: · परीक्षा जोड

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · परीक्षा जोड Structured vs object-oriented programming, and the features of OOP, are the two most repeated questions from this unit. Structured र OOP को तुलना, अनि OOP का विशेषता — यी दुई सबैभन्दा बढी दोहोरिने प्रश्न हुन्। Q1 · Define OOP. Explain any four features of OOP. [6 marks] Show the answer OOP is a programming method that solves a big problem by breaking it into small parts called objects, binding together the data and the functions that operate on that data so that no other part of the code can access the data directly. Any four of: Object — a real-world entity with data and behaviour; Class — a blueprint from which objects are created; Encapsulation — binding data and functions in one unit and hiding the data; Abstraction — showing only essential features and hiding internal details; Inheritance — one class acquiring the properties of another; Polymorphism — one name behaving in many forms. परिभाषा + कुनै चार विशेषताको एक–एक लाइन व्याख्या लेख्नुहोस्। Q2 · Differentiate between procedural and object-oriented programming. [5 marks] Show the answer Write it as a table with at least five rows: basic unit (function vs object), approach (top-down vs bottom-up), focus (procedure vs data), data security (global and less secure vs private and more secure), reusability (difficult vs easy through inheritance), and examples (C vs C++). तालिकाको रूपमा कम्तीमा पाँच हरफ लेख्नुहोस् — तालिकाले पूरा अंक ल्याउँछ। Q3 · What is a token? Name the six types of tokens in C++ with one example each. [4 marks] Show the answer A token is the smallest individual unit of a C++ program that has meaning to the compiler. The six types are: keywords (int), identifiers (sum), constants (25), operators (+), punctuators (;) and strings ("Ram"). परिभाषा + छवटै प्रकार + एक–एक उदाहरण दिनुहोस्। Q4 · Differentiate between while and do…while loops. [3 marks] Show the answer while is entry controlled — the condition is tested before the body runs, so the body may run zero times. do…while is exit controlled — the body runs first and the condition is tested afterwards, so the body always runs at least once. Also, do…while ends with a semicolon after the condition. entry vs exit controlled, ० पटक vs कम्तीमा एक पटक, र अन्त्यको सेमीकोलन — यी तीन बुँदा लेखे पुग्छ। Key points to revise

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A constructor has no return type — not even void. Its name must exactly match the class name.
items.ne: कन्स्ट्रक्टरको return type हुँदैन — void पनि होइन। नाम क्लासकै नामसँग ठ्याक्कै मिल्नुपर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A destructor is written as ~ClassName(). The tilde (~) marks it as a destructor.
items.ne: डिस्ट्रक्टर ~ClassName() भनेर लेखिन्छ। टिल्ड (~) ले यो डिस्ट्रक्टर हो भन्ने जनाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The scope resolution operator :: tells the compiler which class the function belongs to, e.g. void Student::display().
items.ne: Scope resolution operator :: ले फङ्सन कुन क्लासको हो भनेर कम्पाइलरलाई बताउँछ, जस्तै void Student::display()।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A class is only a blueprint and takes no memory. Memory is allocated when an object is created from it.
items.ne: क्लास केवल नक्सा हो, यसले मेमोरी लिँदैन। अब्जेक्ट बनेपछि मात्र मेमोरी छुट्याइन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Both constructors run first in creation order, printing AA. Then the destructors run in reverse order, printing XX. So the output is AAXX.
items.ne: दुवै कन्स्ट्रक्टर बनेको क्रममा पहिले चल्छन् — AA छाप्छन्। अनि डिस्ट्रक्टर उल्टो क्रममा चल्छन् — XX छाप्छन्। त्यसैले आउटपुट AAXX हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: s1.~Student(); yourself. And the destruction order is always the reverse of the creation order — like plates on a stack.
items.ne: दुवै आफैं बोलिन्छन् — हातले बोलाउनु पर्दैन। नष्ट हुने क्रम सधैं बनेको उल्टो हुन्छ, स्ट्याकमा थुपारेको प्लेट जस्तै।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: 3.3 Declaring a Class and its Objects
items.en: }. A class declaration is a statement, so it must end with a semicolon. Leaving it out produces a long, confusing list of compiler errors.
items.ne: क्लासको बन्द ब्रेस पछि सेमीकोलन बिर्सनु — यो युनिटको सबैभन्दा सामान्य गल्ती हो। };

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Can this line reach that member?
items.ne: यो हरफले त्यो मेम्बरमा पुग्न सक्छ?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A member is declared in a base class and used somewhere. Decide whether the line compiles. The place students lose the mark is inside a derived class, where private and protected behave differently.
items.ne: Base क्लासमा घोषित मेम्बर कतै प्रयोग भएको छ। त्यो हरफ compile हुन्छ कि हुँदैन छान्नुहोस्। अंक गुम्ने ठाउँ derived क्लासभित्र हो, जहाँ private र protected फरक व्यवहार गर्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Yes — it compiles
items.ne: हुन्छ — compile हुन्छ

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: No — error
items.ne: हुँदैन — त्रुटि

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A private member is reachable only from inside its own class. main() is outside, so this is an error. Private is the default for a class, which is why forgetting to write public is such a common mistake.
items.ne: Private मेम्बरमा आफ्नै क्लासभित्रबाट मात्र पुग्न सकिन्छ। main() बाहिर छ, त्यसैले त्रुटि हो। क्लासमा default नै private हुने भएकाले public लेख्न बिर्सनु सामान्य गल्ती हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Protected is reachable from a derived class. This is the ONLY difference between protected and private, and it is what protected exists for.
items.ne: Protected मा derived क्लासबाट पुग्न सकिन्छ। Protected र private बीचको एउटै फरक यही हो, र protected हुनुको कारण पनि यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A derived class does NOT inherit access to a private member. It exists inside the object, but B cannot touch it directly — the callout in 5.1 calls it the parent's personal diary. Change private to protected and it compiles.
items.ne: Derived क्लासले private मेम्बरमा पहुँच पाउँदैन। त्यो अब्जेक्टभित्र छ, तर B ले सिधै छुन सक्दैन — ५.१ को उदाहरणमा यसलाई बाबुको व्यक्तिगत डायरी भनिएको छ। private लाई protected बनाए compile हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Protected helps a DERIVED class, not the outside world. From main() it behaves exactly like private. Students who learn "protected is less strict" often miss this.
items.ne: Protected ले derived क्लासलाई सहयोग गर्छ, बाहिरी संसारलाई होइन। main() बाट यो ठ्याक्कै private जस्तै हुन्छ। "Protected कम कडा हो" भनेर सिकेकाहरू यहीँ चुक्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Public is reachable from anywhere. This is the case that makes the other four meaningful — without it the table would just say "no".
items.ne: Public मा जहाँबाट पनि पुग्न सकिन्छ। यही केसले बाँकी चारलाई अर्थपूर्ण बनाउँछ — नत्र तालिकाले "हुँदैन" मात्र भन्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: One blueprint, three objects. Each object owns its data; the functions are shared.
items.ne: एउटा नक्सा, तीन अब्जेक्ट। डाटा हरेकको आफ्नै, फङ्सन साझा।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Three rings of access. Outside code can only reach the public ring.
items.ne: पहुँचका तीन घेरा। बाहिरको कोडले public घेरासम्म मात्र पुग्न सक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Constructors run in creation order; destructors run in the exact reverse order.
items.ne: कन्स्ट्रक्टर बनेको क्रममा, डिस्ट्रक्टर ठ्याक्कै उल्टो क्रममा चल्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: One-line memory hook A class is the house design on paper. An object is the real house built from it. One design can produce many houses — and you cannot live inside the design. That is exactly why a class takes no memory but an object does.
items.ne: क्लास = कागजमा कोरेको घरको नक्सा। अब्जेक्ट = त्यसबाट बनेको साँच्चिकै घर। एउटा नक्साबाट धेरै घर बन्छ — र नक्सामा बस्न मिल्दैन। त्यसैले क्लासले मेमोरी लिँदैन, अब्जेक्टले लिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Accessible only inside the same class. Not from outside the class, and not even from a derived class. This is the default for a class.
items.ne: उही क्लास भित्रबाट मात्र। बाहिरबाट वा derived क्लासबाट पनि हुँदैन। क्लासमा यही default हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Accessible from anywhere — inside the class, through an object, and from derived classes. This is the default for a struct.
items.ne: जताबाट पनि — क्लास भित्र, अब्जेक्टबाट, र derived क्लासबाट।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Accessible inside the class and inside its derived classes, but not through an object from outside.
items.ne: क्लास भित्र र त्यसका derived क्लास भित्र मात्र; बाहिरको अब्जेक्टबाट हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Note the trap: in a struct the default is public instead. Same language, opposite default — and that difference is worth a mark when the question gives you a struct.
items.ne: Private। class मा default private हुन्छ, त्यसैले x बाहिरबाट पुग्न सकिँदैन — public: लेख्न बिर्सँदा सुरुका प्रोग्राममा "member is inaccessible" आउनुको कारण यही हो। ध्यान दिनुहोस्: struct मा default public हुन्छ। उही भाषा, उल्टो default।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Case 4 is the one that catches people who learned "protected is less strict". From outside the class, protected behaves exactly like private.
items.ne: केस २ र ३ मा एउटै कोड छ, एउटै शब्द फरक — protected बाट private — र उत्तर उल्टिन्छ। दुई specifier बीचको पूरा फरक त्यही शब्द हो, र त्यो derived क्लासभित्र मात्र देखिन्छ। केस ४ ले "protected कम कडा हो" भन्ने भ्रम भत्काउँछ: क्लासबाहिरबाट protected ठ्याक्कै private जस्तै हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Six lines are printed. Write all six down, in order, before opening this. The order is the answer: each constructor announces itself when it runs, so the first three lines tell you which one was chosen and when.
items.ne: छ वटा लाइन छापिन्छन्। खोल्नुअघि क्रम मिलाएर छैटै लेख्नुहोस्। क्रम नै उत्तर हो: हरेक constructor चल्दा आफ्नो नाम भन्छ, त्यसैले पहिलो तीन लाइनले कुन कहिले रोजियो भन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: All three constructors have the same name — the compiler picks the right one by counting and checking the arguments. That is constructor overloading, and it is an example of compile-time polymorphism.
items.ne: तीनै कन्स्ट्रक्टरको नाम उही छ — कम्पाइलरले आर्गुमेन्ट हेरेर सही एउटा छान्छ। यसैलाई constructor overloading भनिन्छ, र यो compile-time polymorphism कै उदाहरण हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Class A class is a user-defined data type that acts as a blueprint or template. It groups data members (the variables) and member functions (the methods) together into one unit. A class does not take any memory — it is only a design. Memory is allocated only when an object is created from it.
items.ne: क्लास क्लास भनेको प्रयोगकर्ताले बनाएको डाटा टाइप हो, जुन नक्सा (blueprint) जस्तै काम गर्छ। यसले डाटा मेम्बर (भेरिएबल) र मेम्बर फङ्सन (मेथड) लाई एउटै एकाइमा राख्छ। क्लासले मेमोरी लिँदैन — यो डिजाइन मात्र हो। अब्जेक्ट बनेपछि मात्र मेमोरी छुट्याइन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Object An object is a variable of a class — one real copy built from the blueprint. An object does take memory, and each object has its own separate copy of the data members. The act of creating an object from a class is called instantiation.
items.ne: अब्जेक्ट अब्जेक्ट भनेको क्लासको भेरिएबल हो — नक्सा हेरेर बनाइएको वास्तविक प्रति। अब्जेक्टले मेमोरी लिन्छ, र हरेक अब्जेक्टसँग आफ्नै छुट्टै डाटा हुन्छ। क्लासबाट अब्जेक्ट बनाउने कामलाई instantiation भनिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Constructor A constructor is a special member function that is called automatically when an object is created. Its job is to initialise the object's data. Its name is exactly the same as the class name. It has no return type — not even void. It can take parameters and can be overloaded. Three types: Default constructor — takes no arguments. Parameterized constructor — takes arguments to set the starting values. Copy constructor — creates a new object as a copy of an existing one, written Student(Student &s).
items.ne: कन्स्ट्रक्टर कन्स्ट्रक्टर एउटा विशेष मेम्बर फङ्सन हो, जुन अब्जेक्ट बन्ने बित्तिकै आफैं बोलिन्छ। यसको काम डाटालाई सुरुवाती मान दिनु हो। नाम क्लासकै नामसँग ठ्याक्कै मिल्नुपर्छ। return type हुँदैन — void पनि होइन। प्यारामिटर लिन सक्छ र overload पनि हुन सक्छ। तीन प्रकार: Default — कुनै आर्गुमेन्ट नलिने। Parameterized — सुरुको मान तोक्न आर्गुमेन्ट लिने। Copy — भइरहेको अब्जेक्टको प्रतिलिपि बनाउने।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Destructor A destructor is a special member function that is called automatically when an object is destroyed — that is, when it goes out of scope. Its job is to free the memory the object was using. Its name is the class name with a tilde ~ in front. It has no return type and takes no parameters. It cannot be overloaded — a class has exactly one destructor. Objects are destroyed in the reverse order of their creation.
items.ne: डिस्ट्रक्टर डिस्ट्रक्टर एउटा विशेष मेम्बर फङ्सन हो, जुन अब्जेक्ट नष्ट हुँदा आफैं बोलिन्छ। यसको काम अब्जेक्टले लिएको मेमोरी खाली गर्नु हो। नाम अगाडि टिल्ड ~ राखेर क्लासकै नाम। return type हुँदैन र प्यारामिटर पनि लिँदैन। overload गर्न मिल्दैन — क्लासमा एउटा मात्र डिस्ट्रक्टर हुन्छ। अब्जेक्टहरू बनेको उल्टो क्रममा नष्ट हुन्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् A class is written with no access specifier at all: class A { int x; };. What is x? कुनै access specifier नलेखी क्लास बनाइयो: class A { int x; };। x के हुन्छ? public protected private Private. In a class the default is private, so x cannot be reached from outside — and this is why a beginner's first program often fails to compile with "member is inaccessible" when they forgot to write public:. Note the trap: in a struct the default is public instead. Same language, opposite default — and that difference is worth a mark when the question gives you a struct. Private। class मा default private हुन्छ, त्यसैले x बाहिरबाट पुग्न सकिँदैन — public: लेख्न बिर्सँदा सुरुका प्रोग्राममा "member is inaccessible" आउनुको कारण यही हो। ध्यान दिनुहोस्: struct मा default public हुन्छ। उही भाषा, उल्टो default। Practise the judgement
items.ne: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Does this line compile? What you will learn: to apply the access table instead of reciting it — especially inside a derived class, where private and protected stop behaving the same. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: पहुँच तालिका घोक्नुभन्दा लागू गर्न — विशेष गरी derived क्लासभित्र, जहाँ private र protected फरक हुन्छन्। What to notice Cases 2 and 3 are the same code with one word changed — protected becomes private — and the answer flips. That single word is the entire difference between the two specifiers, and it only shows up inside a derived class. Case 4 is the one that catches people who learned "protected is less strict". From outside the class, protected behaves exactly like private. केस २ र ३ मा एउटै कोड छ, एउटै शब्द फरक — protected बाट private — र उत्तर उल्टिन्छ। दुई specifier बीचको पूरा फरक त्यही शब्द हो, र त्यो derived क्लासभित्र मात्र देखिन्छ। केस ४ ले "protected कम कडा हो" भन्ने भ्रम भत्काउँछ: क्लासबाहिरबाट protected ठ्याक्कै private जस्तै हुन्छ। 3.3 Declaring a Class and its Objects Example 1 A complete class with data members and member functions #include <iostream> #include <string> using namespace std; class Student { // class = blueprint private: // hidden from outside string name; // data member int roll; // data member public: // usable from outside void setData(string n, int r) { // member function name = n; roll = r; } void display() { // member function cout << name << " - " << roll << endl; } }; // <-- this semicolon is compulsory int main() { Student s1, s2; // s1 and s2 are OBJECTS s1.setData("Ram", 15); // dot operator s2.setData("Sita", 16); s1.display(); s2.display(); return 0; } Output Ram - 15 Sita - 16 Notice that s1 and s2 used the same display() function but printed different values — because each object carries its own copy of name and roll. s1 र s2 ले उही display() प्रयोग गरे तर फरक मान छापे — किनकि हरेक अब्जेक्टसँग आफ्नै name र roll छ। The single most common error in this unit Forgetting the semicolon after the closing brace of a class: }; not }. A class declaration is a statement, so it must end with a semicolon. Leaving it out produces a long, confusing list of compiler errors. क्लासको बन्द ब्रेस पछि सेमीकोलन बिर्सनु — यो युनिटको सबैभन्दा सामान्य गल्ती हो। }; लेख्नुपर्छ, } मात्र होइन। Defining a member function outside the class Example 2 Using the scope resolution operator :: class Student { private: string name; int roll; public: void setData(string n, int r); // only DECLARED here void display(); // only DECLARED here }; // DEFINED outside, using ClassName::functionName void Student::setData(string n, int r) { name = n; roll = r; } void Student::display() { cout << name << " - " << roll << endl; } The scope resolution operator :: tells the compiler which class the function belongs to. Without Student:: the compiler would treat display() as an ordinary global function that knows nothing about name or roll. Scope resolution operator :: ले फङ्सन कुन क्लासको हो भनेर कम्पाइलरलाई बताउँछ। Student:: नलेखे कम्पाइलरले यसलाई सामान्य global फङ्सन ठान्छ, जसलाई name र roll को केही थाहा हुँदैन। 3.5 Constructor and Destructor Constructor A constructor is a special member function that is called automatically when an object is created. Its job is to initialise the object's data. Its name is exactly the same as the class name. It has no return type — not even void. It can take parameters and can be overloaded. Three types: Default constructor — takes no arguments. Parameterized constructor — takes arguments to set the starting values. Copy constructor — creates a new object as a copy of an existing one, written Student(Student &s). कन्स्ट्रक्टर कन्स्ट्रक्टर एउटा विशेष मेम्बर फङ्सन हो, जुन अब्जेक्ट बन्ने बित्तिकै आफैं बोलिन्छ। यसको काम डाटालाई सुरुवाती मान दिनु हो। नाम क्लासकै नामसँग ठ्याक्कै मिल्नुपर्छ। return type हुँदैन — void पनि होइन। प्यारामिटर लिन सक्छ र overload पनि हुन सक्छ। तीन प्रकार: Default — कुनै आर्गुमेन्ट नलिने। Parameterized — सुरुको मान तोक्न आर्गुमेन्ट लिने। Copy — भइरहेको अब्जेक्टको प्रतिलिपि बनाउने। Destructor A destructor is a special member function that is called automatically when an object is destroyed — that is, when it goes out of scope. Its job is to free the memory the object was using. Its name is the class name with a tilde ~ in front. It has no return type and takes no parameters. It cannot be overloaded — a class has exactly one destructor. Objects are destroyed in the reverse order of their creation. डिस्ट्रक्टर डिस्ट्रक्टर एउटा विशेष मेम्बर फङ्सन हो, जुन अब्जेक्ट नष्ट हुँदा आफैं बोलिन्छ। यसको काम अब्जेक्टले लिएको मेमोरी खाली गर्नु हो। नाम अगाडि टिल्ड ~ राखेर क्लासकै नाम। return type हुँदैन र प्यारामिटर पनि लिँदैन। overload गर्न मिल्दैन — क्लासमा एउटा मात्र डिस्ट्रक्टर हुन्छ। अब्जेक्टहरू बनेको उल्टो क्रममा नष्ट हुन्छन्। {{dia:ctorDtor}} Constructors run in creation order; destructors run in the exact reverse order. कन्स्ट्रक्टर बनेको क्रममा, डिस्ट्रक्टर ठ्याक्कै उल्टो क्रममा चल्छ। Example 3 Constructor overloading — three constructors in one class #include <iostream> using namespace std; class Box { int len, wid; public: Box() { // 1. default constructor len = 1; wid = 1; cout << "Default called" << endl; } Box(int l, int w) { // 2. parameterized constructor len = l; wid = w; cout << "Parameterized called" << endl; } Box(Box &b) { // 3. copy constructor len = b.len; wid = b.wid; cout << "Copy called" << endl; } void area() { cout << "Area = " << len * wid << endl; } }; int main() { Box b1; // calls the default Box b2(4, 6); // calls the parameterized Box b3 = b2; // calls the copy constructor b1.area(); b2.area(); b3.area(); return 0; } Six lines are printed. Write all six down, in order, before opening this. The order is the answer: each constructor announces itself when it runs, so the first three lines tell you which one was chosen and when. छ वटा लाइन छापिन्छन्। खोल्नुअघि क्रम मिलाएर छैटै लेख्नुहोस्। क्रम नै उत्तर हो: हरेक constructor चल्दा आफ्नो नाम भन्छ, त्यसैले पहिलो तीन लाइनले कुन कहिले रोजियो भन्छ। Output Default called Parameterized called Copy called Area = 1 Area = 24 Area = 24 All three constructors have the same name — the compiler picks the right one by counting and checking the arguments. That is constructor overloading, and it is an example of compile-time polymorphism. तीनै कन्स्ट्रक्टरको नाम उही छ — कम्पाइलरले आर्गुमेन्ट हेरेर सही एउटा छान्छ। यसैलाई constructor overloading भनिन्छ, र यो compile-time polymorphism कै उदाहरण हो। Exam favourite — the automatic call Constructors and destructors are called automatically. You never write s1.Student(); or s1.~Student(); yourself. And the destruction order is always the reverse of the creation order — like plates on a stack. दुवै आफैं बोलिन्छन् — हातले बोलाउनु पर्दैन। नष्ट हुने क्रम सधैं बनेको उल्टो हुन्छ, स्ट्याकमा थुपारेको प्लेट जस्तै। Exam focus — questions asked from this unit SEE exam connection
items.ne: · परीक्षा जोड

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · परीक्षा जोड Access specifiers and the constructor/destructor rules are asked as both short questions and output prediction. Access specifier र constructor/destructor का नियम छोटो प्रश्न र आउटपुट दुवैमा सोधिन्छ। Q1 · Differentiate between a class and an object. [3 marks] Show the answer A class is a blueprint or template that defines the data members and member functions; an object is an instance of that class. A class takes no memory, while an object takes memory when it is created. A class is declared once, but many objects can be created from it. Example: class Student{ }; is the class, Student s1; creates the object. नक्सा vs घर, मेमोरी लिँदैन vs लिन्छ, एक पटक घोषणा vs धेरै अब्जेक्ट — यी तीन बुँदा लेख्नुहोस्। Q2 · Explain the three access specifiers in C++. Which is the default? [4 marks] Show the answer private — accessible only inside the same class; not from outside and not from a derived class. public — accessible from anywhere, including through an object. protected — accessible inside the class and inside its derived classes, but not through an object from outside. In a class the default is private. (In a struct the default is public.) तीनवटैको एक–एक लाइन + default चाहिँ private हो भनेर लेख्न नबिर्सनुहोस्। Q3 · What is a constructor? Write its characteristics and name its types. [5 marks] Show the answer A constructor is a special member function that is automatically invoked when an object of the class is created, and it is used to initialise the object's data members. Characteristics: its name is the same as the class name; it has no return type, not even void; it is called automatically; it can take parameters; it can be overloaded. Types: default constructor, parameterized constructor and copy constructor. परिभाषा + पाँच विशेषता + तीन प्रकार — पूरा अंकका लागि तीनै भाग चाहिन्छ। Q4 · Differentiate between a constructor and a destructor. [4 marks] Show the answer Write it as a table: when called (on creation vs on destruction); name (class name vs class name with ~); parameters (can take them vs cannot); overloading (can be overloaded vs cannot, only one per class); purpose (initialise / allocate memory vs clean up / free memory). तालिकाको रूपमा पाँच हरफ लेख्नुहोस्। Key points to revise

items.en: Class and Object
items.ne: क्लास र अब्जेक्ट

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: What you will learn: to apply the access table instead of reciting it — especially inside a derived class, where private and protected stop behaving the same.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: पहुँच तालिका घोक्नुभन्दा लागू गर्न — विशेष गरी derived क्लासभित्र, जहाँ private र protected फरक हुन्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: That is encapsulation (data hiding). Abstraction instead hides the complexity of HOW the work is done.
items.ne: यो encapsulation (data hiding) हो। Abstraction ले चाहिँ काम "कसरी" हुन्छ भन्ने जटिलता लुकाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Abstraction is about DESIGN — deciding what to show. Encapsulation is about IMPLEMENTATION — wrapping the data with the functions that may touch it. A car pedal is abstraction: you press it without knowing the engine. The sealed engine casing is encapsulation. They work together but are not the same, and the exam asks you to tell them apart.
items.ne: Abstraction डिजाइन को कुरा हो — के देखाउने भन्ने निर्णय। Encapsulation कार्यान्वयन को — data लाई छुन पाउने function सँगै बेर्ने काम। गाडीको पेडल abstraction हो: इन्जिन नजानी थिच्नुहुन्छ। बन्द इन्जिन बाकस encapsulation हो। सँगै काम गर्छन् तर एउटै होइनन्, र परीक्षाले छुट्याउन भन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Private data with public functions is the standard shape: outside code must go through a function, which can check the value before storing it. Making data public defeats the purpose entirely — anything could set a student's marks to −5. Global variables are the opposite of encapsulation.
items.ne: Private data र public function मानक ढाँचा हो: बाहिरको कोड function हुँदै आउनुपर्छ, र त्यो function ले राख्नुअघि मान जाँच्न सक्छ। Data public बनाउँदा उद्देश्य नै सकिन्छ — जसले पनि विद्यार्थीको अंक −5 बनाइदिन सक्छ। Global variable त encapsulation को ठीक उल्टो हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: You are given a simple interface — cout << x — and everything underneath it is hidden. That is abstraction: showing only what is needed to use the thing. The C++ library is itself built on this idea, which is why you can write a program on day one.
items.ne: तपाईंलाई सरल इन्टरफेस दिइएको छ — cout << x — र मुनिको सबै लुकाइएको छ। यही abstraction हो: प्रयोग गर्न चाहिने मात्र देखाउनु। C++ library आफैँ यही विचारमा बनेको छ, त्यसैले पहिलो दिनै प्रोग्राम लेख्न सकिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The setter is a gate. It can reject a negative age, clamp an impossible one, or record that a change happened — none of which is possible when outside code writes the variable directly. Speed and memory are unchanged, and inheritance does not depend on access specifiers at all.
items.ne: Setter एउटा ढोका हो। यसले ऋणात्मक उमेर अस्वीकार गर्न, असम्भव मान सीमित गर्न, वा परिवर्तन भएको अभिलेख राख्न सक्छ — बाहिरको कोडले सीधै variable लेख्दा यीमध्ये केही पनि सम्भव हुँदैन। गति र मेमोरी उस्तै रहन्छ, र inheritance access specifier मा भर पर्दैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Abstraction or encapsulation?
items.ne: Abstraction कि encapsulation?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The pair the paper asks you to differentiate almost every year. One test settles every case: is complexity being hidden, or is data being protected?
items.ne: परीक्षामा झन्डै हरेक वर्ष फरक छुट्याउन भनिने जोडी। एउटै जाँचले सबै केस मिलाउँछ: जटिलता लुकाइँदै छ, कि डाटा जोगाइँदै छ?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Complexity is hidden and only the necessary interface is shown. Abstraction answers "what does it do?" and hides "how".
items.ne: जटिलता लुकाइएको छ र आवश्यक अन्तरमुख मात्र देखाइएको छ। Abstraction ले "के गर्छ?" भन्छ र "कसरी" लुकाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Data is bound with its functions and protected from direct access. Encapsulation answers "who may touch this?" The private keyword is its usual sign.
items.ne: डाटा आफ्ना फङ्सनसँग बाँधिएको र सिधै पहुँचबाट जोगिएको छ। Encapsulation ले "यसलाई कसले छुन पाउँछ?" भन्छ। private शब्द यसको सङ्केत हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The class states WHAT must exist without saying HOW. A pure virtual function is abstraction in its strongest form.
items.ne: क्लासले के हुनुपर्छ भन्छ, कसरी भन्दैन। Pure virtual फङ्सन abstraction को सबैभन्दा बलियो रूप हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Binding data and functions into a single unit IS the definition of encapsulation — the wrapping itself, before any hiding.
items.ne: डाटा र फङ्सनलाई एउटै इकाइमा बाँध्नु नै encapsulation को परिभाषा हो — लुकाउनुभन्दा अघि, बाँध्ने काम आफैंमा।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Necessary information shown, mechanism hidden. If instead the question said the speed value could not be changed from outside, that would be encapsulation.
items.ne: आवश्यक जानकारी देखाइएको, संयन्त्र लुकाइएको। बरु "गति बाहिरबाट बदल्न मिल्दैन" भनेको भए त्यो encapsulation हुन्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: You get simple, safe buttons. The complicated part stays behind a wall you cannot see past — and because the buttons never change, the hidden part can be rewritten freely.
items.ne: तपाईंलाई सजिलो र सुरक्षित बटन मात्र दिइन्छ। जटिल भाग नदेखिने पर्खाल पछाडि रहन्छ — बटन नफेरिने भएकाले भित्रको कोड जहिले पनि बदल्न सकिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The private data sits in a capsule. The only way in is through a public function that can refuse a bad value.
items.ne: private डाटा क्याप्सुल भित्र हुन्छ। भित्र पस्ने एक मात्र बाटो public फङ्सन हो, जसले गलत मान अस्वीकार गर्न सक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The car abstracts all of that away. If the manufacturer redesigns the entire engine next year, you still drive it the same way — because the interface (the controls) did not change. That is the real benefit of abstraction in programming too.
items.ne: उदाहरण — गाडी चलाउनु। तपाईंलाई स्टेरिङ, एक्सिलेटर र ब्रेक मात्र चाहिन्छ; इन्जिन भित्र के हुन्छ थाहा पाउनु पर्दैन। भोलि कम्पनीले पूरै इन्जिन फेरे पनि तपाईंले उसैगरी चलाउनुहुन्छ — किनकि नियन्त्रण (interface) फेरिएन। प्रोग्रामिङमा पनि abstraction को साँचो फाइदा यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: square() helper — is completely hidden. That is abstraction.
items.ne: प्रयोगकर्ताले एउटा सजिलो फङ्सन बोलाएर जवाफ पाउँछ। कसरी गणना भयो — private square()

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A negative amount is passed to the setter. Decide what the balance is afterwards — and whether the program stopped, complained, or simply carried on. Which of those three it does is the point of the example.
items.ne: setter मा ऋणात्मक रकम पठाइएको छ। त्यसपछि balance कति हुन्छ निर्णय गर्नुहोस् — र प्रोग्राम रोकियो, गुनासो गर्‍यो, कि सामान्य रूपमा अघि बढ्यो? तीनमध्ये कुन गर्छ भन्ने नै यो उदाहरणको मुख्य कुरा हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Exam focus — questions asked from this unit
items.en: Abstraction hides the complexity or implementation — the "how" — and is a design-level concept achieved through abstract classes and access specifiers; it focuses on what an object does. Encapsulation hides the data — the "what" — and is an implementation-level concept achieved by making data private and providing public getters and setters; it focuses on protecting the data.
items.ne: तालिकाको रूपमा चार हरफ लेख्नुहोस्: के लुकाउँछ, कुन तह, कसरी हासिल हुन्छ, केमा ध्यान।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Definition — learn this wording Abstraction means showing only the essential features of an object to the user and hiding the internal implementation details — that is, hiding how the work is actually done. In C++ abstraction is achieved in two ways: using classes with access specifiers (data and helper functions kept private, only the useful functions made public), and at a higher level using abstract classes.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्द कण्ठ पार्नुहोस् एब्स्ट्र्याक्सन भनेको प्रयोगकर्तालाई आवश्यक कुरा मात्र देखाउने र भित्री काम कसरी हुन्छ भन्ने लुकाउने हो। C++ मा यो दुई तरिकाले हासिल गरिन्छ: access specifier सहितको क्लास (डाटा र सहायक फङ्सन private, काम लाग्ने फङ्सन मात्र public), र माथिल्लो तहमा abstract class मार्फत।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Advantages of abstraction Reduces complexity — the user sees a small, simple interface instead of thousands of lines. Increases security — internal data and helper functions cannot be misused. Easy to change later — the hidden code can be rewritten without breaking any program that uses it. Improves reusability — the same class can be used in many programs. Avoids code duplication and makes maintenance easier.
items.ne: एब्स्ट्र्याक्सनका फाइदा जटिलता घटाउँछ — हजारौं लाइनको सट्टा सानो, सजिलो interface मात्र देखिन्छ। सुरक्षा बढाउँछ — भित्री डाटा र सहायक फङ्सनको दुरुपयोग हुँदैन। पछि बदल्न सजिलो — लुकेको कोड बदल्दा प्रयोग गर्ने प्रोग्राम बिग्रँदैन। पुनः प्रयोग — उही क्लास धेरै प्रोग्राममा चल्छ। दोहोरो कोड हट्छ र मर्मत सजिलो हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Abstract class and pure virtual function
items.en: The higher level of abstraction A pure virtual function is a virtual function with no body, written by putting = 0 after it. It is a promise that says "every child class must provide this function". A class that contains at least one pure virtual function is called an abstract class. You cannot create an object of an abstract class — it exists only to be inherited.
items.ne: माथिल्लो तहको abstraction Pure virtual function भनेको शरीर नभएको virtual फङ्सन हो, जसमा पछाडि = 0 लेखिन्छ। यसले "हरेक सन्तान क्लासले यो फङ्सन दिनैपर्छ" भन्ने वाचा गर्छ। कम्तीमा एउटा pure virtual function भएको क्लासलाई abstract class भनिन्छ। यसको अब्जेक्ट बनाउन मिल्दैन — यो इनहेरिट गर्नकै लागि मात्र हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Definition — learn this wording Encapsulation means binding data members and member functions together into a single unit (the class), and hiding the data from direct outside access by declaring it private. Outside code must then go through public functions — usually called setter and getter functions — to change or read that data. For this reason encapsulation is also called data hiding.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्द कण्ठ पार्नुहोस् इनक्याप्सुलेसन भनेको डाटा मेम्बर र मेम्बर फङ्सनलाई एउटै एकाइ (क्लास) मा बाँध्ने र डाटालाई private बनाएर बाहिरबाट सिधै छुन नदिने हो। त्यसपछि बाहिरको कोडले डाटा बदल्न वा पढ्न public फङ्सन (setter/getter) प्रयोग गर्नै पर्छ। त्यसैले यसलाई data hiding पनि भनिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Advantages of encapsulation Data security — data cannot be changed accidentally or wrongly from outside. Full control — the setter can validate the value before storing it. Read-only or write-only access — provide only a getter, or only a setter, as needed. Easier maintenance and testing — the class can be changed inside without affecting other code. Achieves data hiding, which is one of the main goals of OOP.
items.ne: इनक्याप्सुलेसनका फाइदा डाटा सुरक्षा — बाहिरबाट गल्तीले डाटा बदलिन सक्दैन। पूर्ण नियन्त्रण — setter ले मान राख्नु अघि जाँच्न सक्छ। पढ्ने मात्र वा लेख्ने मात्र पहुँच दिन सकिन्छ। मर्मत र परीक्षण सजिलो — भित्र बदल्दा अरू कोडमा असर पर्दैन। Data hiding हासिल हुन्छ, जुन OOP कै मुख्य लक्ष्य हो।

items.en: A negative amount is passed to the setter. Decide what the balance is afterwards — and whether the program stopped, complained, or simply carried on. Which of those three it does is the point of the example. setter मा ऋणात्मक रकम पठाइएको छ। त्यसपछि balance कति हुन्छ निर्णय गर्नुहोस् — र प्रोग्राम रोकियो, गुनासो गर्‍यो, कि सामान्य रूपमा अघि बढ्यो? तीनमध्ये कुन गर्छ भन्ने नै यो उदाहरणको मुख्य कुरा हो। Output Invalid amount rejected Balance = 5000 This is the whole point of encapsulation. If balance were public, a.balance = -500; would have silently corrupted the account. The setter is a guard at the only door. encapsulation को मुख्य उद्देश्य यही हो। balance public भएको भए a.balance = -500; ले चुपचाप खाता बिगार्थ्यो। setter एउटै ढोकामा उभिएको पहरेदार हो। Advantages of encapsulation Data security — data cannot be changed accidentally or wrongly from outside. Full control — the setter can validate the value before storing it. Read-only or write-only access — provide only a getter, or only a setter, as needed. Easier maintenance and testing — the class can be changed inside without affecting other code. Achieves data hiding, which is one of the main goals of OOP. इनक्याप्सुलेसनका फाइदा डाटा सुरक्षा — बाहिरबाट गल्तीले डाटा बदलिन सक्दैन। पूर्ण नियन्त्रण — setter ले मान राख्नु अघि जाँच्न सक्छ। पढ्ने मात्र वा लेख्ने मात्र पहुँच दिन सकिन्छ। मर्मत र परीक्षण सजिलो — भित्र बदल्दा अरू कोडमा असर पर्दैन। Data hiding हासिल हुन्छ, जुन OOP कै मुख्य लक्ष्य हो। The difference students always get wrong Say it in one line each Abstraction hides the complexity — the "how". Encapsulation hides the data — the "what". Abstraction is a design idea: decide what to show. Encapsulation is an implementation idea: actually protect the data using private plus getters and setters. Abstraction ले जटिलता ("कसरी" गर्ने) लुकाउँछ। Encapsulation ले डाटा ("के" छ) लुकाउँछ। एउटा डिजाइन को कुरा, अर्को कार्यान्वयन/सुरक्षा को कुरा। BasisAbstractionEncapsulation What it hidesHides the complexity / implementation — the "how".Hides the data — the "what". LevelA design-level idea.An implementation-level idea. Achieved byAbstract classes and pure virtual functions; access specifiers.private data with public getter and setter functions. FocusFocuses on what an object does.Focuses on how the data is protected. PurposeTo reduce complexity for the user.To secure the data from misuse. Common mistake Writing "both hide something, so they are the same". They are not. In the Account example above, encapsulation is balance being private. Abstraction is the user being given only setBalance() and getBalance() and never needing to know what happens inside them. items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् A bank class keeps balance private and offers deposit() and withdraw(). Someone writes account.balance = -5000;. What happens? बैंक क्लासले balance private राखेको छ र deposit() तथा withdraw() दिन्छ। कसैले account.balance = -5000; लेख्यो। के हुन्छ? The balance becomes −5000 It will not compile It compiles but is ignored It will not compile. The compiler refuses before the program ever runs — which is the point. Encapsulation is not a warning or a convention; the private keyword makes the invalid change impossible to write. That is the answer to "why bother with getters and setters?". Every change now goes through withdraw(), which is a single place to refuse a negative balance. Say this in an exam answer and you have shown the purpose, not just the definition. Compile नै हुँदैन। प्रोग्राम चल्नुअघि नै compiler ले अस्वीकार गर्छ — मुख्य कुरा यही हो। Encapsulation चेतावनी वा परम्परा होइन; private शब्दले गलत परिवर्तन लेख्नै नसकिने बनाउँछ। "Getter–setter किन चाहियो?" को उत्तर यही हो: हरेक परिवर्तन withdraw() हुँदै जान्छ, जहाँ ऋणात्मक मौज्दात एकै ठाउँमा रोक्न सकिन्छ। Practise the judgement

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Abstraction or encapsulation? Decide, then check What you will learn: to settle the pair with one question instead of two remembered definitions — which is what you will have time for in the hall. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: दुई घोकेका परिभाषाको सट्टा एउटै प्रश्नले यो जोडी छुट्याउन — परीक्षा हलमा त्यति नै समय हुन्छ। The one question that settles it Is complexity being hidden, or is data being protected? Complexity → abstraction. Data → encapsulation. Every case in this drill answers to that one test, and so does every version of this question the paper asks. Watch case 5 in particular. The situation barely changes — a dashboard showing speed — but the reason given changes the answer. The examiner is testing the reason, not the scenario. जटिलता लुकाइँदै छ, कि डाटा जोगाइँदै छ? जटिलता → abstraction। डाटा → encapsulation। यस अभ्यासका सबै केस यही एउटै जाँचले मिल्छन्। केस ५ विशेष हेर्नुहोस्: परिस्थिति उस्तै छ तर दिइएको कारणले उत्तर बदल्छ — परीक्षकले कारण जाँच्छन्। Exam focus — questions asked from this unit SEE exam connection
items.ne: · परीक्षा जोड

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · परीक्षा जोड Abstraction versus encapsulation is the comparison examiners return to. Learn the one-line difference exactly. Abstraction र Encapsulation को भिन्नता परीक्षकले पटक–पटक सोध्छन्। एक वाक्यको फरक ठ्याक्कै सिक्नुहोस्। Q1 · Define abstraction. Write any three advantages. [4 marks] Show the answer Abstraction is the process of showing only the essential features of an object to the user while hiding the internal implementation details of how the work is done. Advantages: it reduces complexity for the user; it increases security because internal details cannot be misused; and the internal code can be changed later without affecting the programs that use the class. परिभाषा + कुनै तीन फाइदा। गाडीको उदाहरण दिए झन् राम्रो। Q2 · What is encapsulation? Write a C++ program to demonstrate it. [5 marks] Show the answer Encapsulation is the process of binding data members and member functions together into a single unit called a class, and hiding the data from direct outside access by declaring it private. It is also known as data hiding. For the program, write the Account class from Example 3 above: a private balance, a public setBalance() and a public getBalance(), with main() creating an object and using the two functions. परिभाषा + माथिको Example 3 कै प्रोग्राम लेख्नुहोस्। Q3 · Differentiate between abstraction and encapsulation. [4 marks] Show the answer Abstraction hides the complexity or implementation — the "how" — and is a design-level concept achieved through abstract classes and access specifiers; it focuses on what an object does. Encapsulation hides the data — the "what" — and is an implementation-level concept achieved by making data private and providing public getters and setters; it focuses on protecting the data. तालिकाको रूपमा चार हरफ लेख्नुहोस्: के लुकाउँछ, कुन तह, कसरी हासिल हुन्छ, केमा ध्यान। Q4 · What is an abstract class? [2 marks] Show the answer An abstract class is a class that contains at least one pure virtual function — a virtual function with no body, declared using = 0. An object of an abstract class cannot be created; it exists only to be inherited, and every derived class must provide a definition for the pure virtual function. pure virtual function भएको क्लास; यसको अब्जेक्ट बन्दैन। Key points to revise
items.ne: — दोहोर्‍याउनुपर्ने मुख्य बुँदा

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Abstraction and Encapsulation
items.ne: एब्स्ट्र्याक्सन र इनक्याप्सुलेसन

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: The difference students always get wrong
items.en: What you will learn: to settle the pair with one question instead of two remembered definitions — which is what you will have time for in the hall.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: दुई घोकेका परिभाषाको सट्टा एउटै प्रश्नले यो जोडी छुट्याउन — परीक्षा हलमा त्यति नै समय हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Base class constructors always run before derived ones, starting from the top-most base. So the order is Animal, then Dog, then Puppy.
items.ne: Base क्लासको कन्स्ट्रक्टर सधैं derived भन्दा पहिले चल्छ, सबैभन्दा माथिबाट सुरु हुँदै। क्रम: Animal → Dog → Puppy।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Hierarchical inheritance is one parent with many children — the picture branches downward. Multiple inheritance is the reverse: one child with many parents. Multilevel is a chain, A to B to C. Reading the SHAPE of the diagram is the fastest way to answer this kind of question.
items.ne: Hierarchical inheritance भनेको एउटा बाबु, धेरै छोरा — चित्र तलतिर फैलिन्छ। Multiple यसको उल्टो हो: एउटा छोरा, धेरै बाबु। Multilevel शृंखला हो, A देखि B देखि C। चित्रको आकार पढ्नु यस्ता प्रश्नको सबैभन्दा छिटो उत्तर हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A derived class inherits the private members — they exist in the object and take up space — but it cannot name them. It must go through a public or protected function of the base. This is exactly why protected exists: it means "private to the outside world, visible to my children".
items.ne: Derived class ले private member पाउँछ — ती object मा हुन्छन् र ठाउँ ओगट्छन् — तर नाम लिएर छुन सक्दैन। Base कै public वा protected function हुँदै जानुपर्छ। protected हुनुको कारण ठ्याक्कै यही हो: "बाहिरका लागि private, मेरा छोराछोरीका लागि देखिने"।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: C++ uses a colon, then the access specifier, then the base class name. extends is Java and inherits is not a C++ keyword at all. Option 4 has the syntax right but the direction backwards — it would make Person inherit from Student, which is the wrong way round.
items.ne: C++ मा कोलन, अनि access specifier, अनि base class को नाम लेखिन्छ। extends Java को हो र inherits C++ को keyword नै होइन। चौथो विकल्पको वाक्य-संरचना ठीक छ तर दिशा उल्टो — यसले Person लाई Student बाट inherit गराउँछ, जुन उल्टो हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Reusability is the point: common behaviour lives in one tested place and every child gets it. That also makes a program easier to extend — a new derived class needs only what is different. Inheritance does not change access rules, and a derived object is normally LARGER, not smaller, since it carries the base part too.
items.ne: पुनः प्रयोग नै मुख्य कुरा हो: साझा व्यवहार एउटै परीक्षित ठाउँमा रहन्छ र हरेक छोराले पाउँछ। यसले विस्तार पनि सजिलो बनाउँछ — नयाँ derived class लाई फरक भएको कुरा मात्र चाहिन्छ। Inheritance ले पहुँचका नियम बदल्दैन, र derived object सामान्यतया ठूलो हुन्छ, सानो होइन — किनकि base को भाग पनि बोक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: This diamond shape mixes hierarchical and multiple inheritance, so it is hybrid. D inherits A through B and again through C, so A's members arrive twice and a reference to one becomes ambiguous. C++ solves it with a virtual base class, which makes the compiler keep only one copy of A.
items.ne: यो हीरा आकारले hierarchical र multiple inheritance मिसाउँछ, त्यसैले hybrid हो। D ले A लाई B हुँदै र फेरि C हुँदै पाउँछ, त्यसैले A का member दुई पटक आउँछन् र कुनै एउटालाई बोलाउँदा अन्योल हुन्छ। C++ ले virtual base class ले समाधान गर्छ, जसले compiler लाई A को एउटै प्रति राख्न लगाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: private means "this class only", and inheriting does not loosen it — x is inherited by B but B is not allowed to touch it. protected is the specifier that exists for exactly this situation: visible to derived classes, still hidden from the outside world. Note that the inheritance mode (public here) changes what happens to the base's public and protected members; it never grants access to its private ones.
items.ne: private को अर्थ "यही class मात्र" हो, र inheritance ले यो खुकुलो बनाउँदैन — x B मा सर्छ तर B ले छुन पाउँदैन। यस्तै अवस्थाका लागि बनेको specifier protected हो: derived class ले देख्छ, बाहिरी संसारले देख्दैन। Inheritance mode (यहाँ public) ले base का public र protected मेम्बरको हैसियत बदल्छ; private मेम्बरमा पहुँच कहिल्यै दिँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Constructor and destructor order — asked very often
items.en: The rule in one line When a derived object is created, the base class constructor runs FIRST, then the derived constructor. Destructors run in the exact reverse: derived destructor first, then base destructor.
items.ne: derived अब्जेक्ट बन्दा पहिले base को कन्स्ट्रक्टर चल्छ, अनि derived को। डिस्ट्रक्टर ठ्याक्कै उल्टो — पहिले derived, अनि base।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: One Puppy object is about to be created. Press Next and watch the ORDER.
items.ne: एउटा Puppy अब्जेक्ट बन्न लागेको छ। Next थिच्नुहोस् र क्रम हेर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Animal() runs first — the top-most base class is always constructed first.
items.ne: पहिले Animal() चल्छ — सबैभन्दा माथिको base क्लास सधैं पहिले बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Dog() runs second, once its own base is ready.
items.ne: आफ्नो base तयार भएपछि दोस्रोमा Dog() चल्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Puppy() runs last. The object is now completely built.
items.ne: अन्तिममा Puppy() चल्छ। अब अब्जेक्ट पूरै तयार भयो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Now it is destroyed. ~Puppy() runs FIRST — the most derived class goes first.
items.ne: अब नष्ट हुँदैछ। पहिले ~Puppy() चल्छ — सबैभन्दा तलको derived क्लास पहिले जान्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: ~Dog() runs second.
items.ne: दोस्रोमा ~Dog() चल्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: ~Animal() runs last. Destruction is the exact reverse of construction — this is the exam answer.
items.ne: अन्तिममा ~Animal() चल्छ। नष्ट हुने क्रम बन्ने क्रमको ठ्याक्कै उल्टो हो — परीक्षाको उत्तर यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Which type of inheritance?
items.ne: यो कुन प्रकारको inheritance हो?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Count the classes and count the arrows. One base with many children is not the same as one child with many parents, and multilevel is not multiple.
items.ne: क्लास गन्नुहोस् र तीर गन्नुहोस्। एउटा base का धेरै छोरा र एउटा छोराका धेरै बाबु फरक कुरा हुन्, र multilevel भनेको multiple होइन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A chain: C derives from B, and B derives from A. Each class has ONE parent, but the chain has more than one level. Students call this "multiple" — it is not, because no class here has two parents.
items.ne: एउटा शृंखला: C, B बाट र B, A बाट आउँछ। हरेक क्लासको एउटै बाबु छ, तर शृंखलामा एकभन्दा बढी तह छन्। विद्यार्थीले यसलाई "multiple" भन्छन् — होइन, किनभने कुनै क्लासका दुई बाबु छैनन्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: ONE class with TWO base classes. This is the only type where a single class has more than one parent, and it is the one C++ allows while Java does not.
items.ne: एउटै क्लासका दुई base क्लास। एउटै क्लासका एकभन्दा बढी बाबु हुने प्रकार यही मात्र हो, र C++ ले दिने तर Java ले नदिने पनि यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: ONE base with MANY derived classes — the branches go downwards from a single parent. Compare with multiple, where the arrows converge upwards into one child.
items.ne: एउटै base बाट धेरै derived क्लास — हाँगा एउटै बाबुबाट तल जान्छन्। Multiple सँग तुलना गर्नुहोस्, जहाँ तीर माथितिर एउटै छोरामा मिल्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: One base, one derived, one arrow. Every other type is built from this one, which is why it is worth being able to name it quickly.
items.ne: एउटा base, एउटा derived, एउटा तीर। बाँकी सबै प्रकार यसैबाट बन्छन्, त्यसैले छिटो नाम दिन सक्नु काम लाग्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Read the widest shape first. A has two children (B and C), which makes the diagram hierarchical; D hanging under B adds a level but does not change what the whole picture is called. A paper asking for ONE name wants the dominant shape — and a hybrid is what you call it if the question allows.
items.ne: पहिले सबैभन्दा फराकिलो आकार हेर्नुहोस्। A का दुई छोरा (B र C) छन्, त्यसैले चित्र hierarchical हो; B मुनिको D ले तह थप्छ तर पूरै चित्रको नाम बदल्दैन। एउटै नाम मागिएमा प्रमुख आकार भन्नुहोस् — प्रश्नले दिए hybrid पनि भन्न सकिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The two arrows that get through and the one that does not. A derived class reuses public and protected members; a private member still exists inside every object but the child cannot reach it.
items.ne: दुई तीर पुग्छन्, एउटा पुग्दैन। Derived क्लासले public र protected मेम्बर पुनः प्रयोग गर्छ; private मेम्बर हरेक अब्जेक्टभित्र हुन्छ तर छोराले छुन पाउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: What the derived class actually receives
items.en: The one rule that never changes: private members are never inherited, in any mode.
items.ne: कहिल्यै नफेरिने नियम: private मेम्बर कुनै पनि मोडमा इनहेरिट हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: All five types, plus the diamond problem that hybrid inheritance can create.
items.ne: पाँचै प्रकार, र hybrid inheritance ले ल्याउन सक्ने diamond problem।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Constructor and destructor order — asked very often
items.en: One object, three constructors. Base first going down, derived first coming back up.
items.ne: एउटा अब्जेक्ट, तीन कन्स्ट्रक्टर। बन्दा base पहिले, नष्ट हुँदा derived पहिले।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: private behaves in inheritance.
items.ne: उदाहरण — परिवार। छोराले बाबुबाट आँखाको रङ, थर र रगतको समूह पाउँछ, र आफ्नै छुट्टै गुण पनि राख्छ। तर सबै कुरा पाउँदैन — बाबुको private मेम्बर व्यक्तिगत डायरी जस्तै हो: छ त, तर छोराले सिधै खोल्न पाउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Derived. That is inheritance doing its job.
items.ne: अब्जेक्ट d

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: What the derived class actually receives
items.en: Never inherited / not accessible in the derived class, in any mode.
items.ne: कुनै पनि मोडमा derived क्लासले base को private मेम्बर सिधै प्रयोग गर्न पाउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: What the derived class actually receives
items.en: private.
items.ne: base को private

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: One base class → one derived class. The simplest form.
items.ne: एउटा base बाट एउटा derived क्लास।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A chain — a derived class itself becomes the base of another class. Grandparent → parent → child.
items.ne: शृंखला — derived क्लास आफैं अर्कोको base बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Two or more base classes → one derived class. The bases are separated by commas.
items.ne: दुई वा बढी base बाट एउटा derived क्लास।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: One base class → many derived classes. Several children share one parent.
items.ne: एउटा base बाट धेरै derived क्लास।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A combination of two or more of the above types — for example hierarchical plus multiple. This can create the diamond problem.
items.ne: माथिका दुई वा बढी प्रकारको मिश्रण।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: One child, two parents. Decide which line comes from which class before opening this — and whether the printing order is the order the bases were inherited in, or the order the calls were written in.
items.ne: एउटा child, दुई parent। खोल्नुअघि कुन लाइन कुन class बाट आउँछ निर्णय गर्नुहोस् — र छापिने क्रम base inherit गरेको क्रम हो कि call लेखिएको क्रम हो?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: The diamond problem and virtual base class
items.en: Case 5 mixes two shapes on purpose, because a real question sometimes does. Read the reason for how to answer when a diagram is not purely one type.
items.ne: दुई गणनाले प्रायः सबै केस मिलाउँछन्। कुनै एउटा क्लासका कति बाबु छन्? एकभन्दा बढी → multiple। एउटा base का कति छोरा छन्? एकभन्दा बढी → hierarchical। हरेकको एउटै बाबु तर धेरै तह भएको शृंखला → multilevel। केस ५ मा जानाजान दुई आकार मिसिएका छन्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Constructor and destructor order — asked very often
items.en: This is the promise in the title — so keep it. One object, four lines of output. Write all four down in order before opening this. The destructor order is not the constructor order, and that is the exam question.
items.ne: शीर्षकमा गरिएको वाचा यही हो — त्यसैले पूरा गर्नुहोस्। एउटै object, चार लाइन output। खोल्नुअघि चारै लाइन क्रम मिलाएर लेख्नुहोस्। destructor को क्रम constructor को क्रम होइन, र परीक्षाको प्रश्न त्यही हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Constructor and destructor order — asked very often
items.en: Four lines from one object. The base is built first (you cannot build the first floor before the ground floor) and destroyed last.
items.ne: एउटै अब्जेक्टबाट चार लाइन। base पहिले बन्छ (भुइँतला नबनाई पहिलो तला बन्दैन) र अन्तिममा भत्किन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Exam focus — questions asked from this unit
items.en: Types of inheritance and constructor call order carry the marks here — the order question appears very often.
items.ne: Inheritance का प्रकार र constructor चल्ने क्रममा अंक छन् — क्रमको प्रश्न धेरै पटक आउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Exam focus — questions asked from this unit
items.en: class Dog : public Animal { };
items.ne: परिभाषा + base/derived + syntax — तीनै लेख्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: Exam focus — questions asked from this unit
items.en: Single — one base, one derived (A → B). Multilevel — a chain where a derived class becomes a base (A → B → C). Multiple — two or more bases, one derived (A and B → C). Hierarchical — one base, many derived (A → B and A → C). Hybrid — a combination of two or more of the above; may cause the diamond problem, solved with a virtual base class.
items.ne: पाँचै चित्र कोर्नुहोस् र एक–एक लाइन व्याख्या दिनुहोस्। चित्र बिना पूरा अंक आउँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Work out the order constructors and destructors run in
items.ne: constructor र destructor कुन क्रममा चल्छन् भन्ने पत्ता लगाउनुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Construction goes BASE FIRST, down to the most derived class. Destruction is the exact reverse: the most derived class is destroyed first. For multiple inheritance, bases run in the order they are LISTED after the colon.
items.ne: निर्माण BASE बाट सुरु भई सबैभन्दा derived कक्षासम्म जान्छ। विनाश ठ्याक्कै उल्टो: सबैभन्दा derived कक्षा पहिले नष्ट हुन्छ। multiple inheritance मा base हरू colon पछि जुन क्रममा लेखिएका छन् त्यही क्रममा चल्छन्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: class Animal { }; class Dog : public Animal { }; You write: Dog d; — which constructor runs first?
items.ne: class Animal { }; class Dog : public Animal { }; तपाईं लेख्नुहुन्छ: Dog d; — कुन constructor पहिले चल्छ?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Which constructor runs first?
items.ne: कुन constructor पहिले चल्छ?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The base is built first. A derived object cannot exist until the part it inherits already does.
items.ne: base पहिले बन्छ। derived वस्तु त्यतिन्जेल हुनै सक्दैन जब सम्म आफूले पाएको भाग बनेको हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Which constructor runs second?
items.ne: कुन constructor दोस्रोमा चल्छ?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Dog is the most derived class, so it is built last — on top of a finished Animal.
items.ne: Dog सबैभन्दा derived हो, त्यसैले अन्तिममा — तयार भइसकेको Animal माथि बन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: When d goes out of scope, which destructor runs FIRST?
items.ne: d को scope सकिँदा कुन destructor पहिले चल्छ?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Destruction is the exact reverse of construction, so the most derived class goes first.
items.ne: विनाश निर्माणको ठ्याक्कै उल्टो हो, त्यसैले सबैभन्दा derived पहिले जान्छ।

items.en: Down the chain to build, back up the chain to destroy. That one sentence answers every question of this shape.

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The order of the bases comes from the class header, not from anything else. That is the single fact this question is testing.

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: class X { }; class Y { }; class Z : public Y, public X { }; You write: Z z; — write the full construction and destruction order, separated by spaces, using ~ for destructors.
items.ne: class X { }; class Y { }; class Z : public Y, public X { }; तपाईं लेख्नुहुन्छ: Z z; — निर्माण र विनाशको पूरा क्रम लेख्नुहोस्, खाली ठाउँले छुट्याएर, destructor लाई ~ राखेर।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Y comes before X because the header says "public Y, public X" — the names are deliberately out of alphabetical order to catch exactly that. If you answered X Y Z, you sorted the names instead of reading the header.
items.ne: header मा "public Y, public X" लेखिएकाले Y, X भन्दा पहिले आउँछ — नाम जानीजानी वर्णक्रम बाहिर राखिएका छन्, यही समात्न। X Y Z भन्नुभयो भने header पढ्नुको सट्टा नाम क्रमबद्ध गर्नुभयो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Definition — learn this wording Inheritance is the process by which one class acquires (gets) the properties and member functions of another class. The class that gives its features is the base class (also called parent or super class). The class that receives them is the derived class (also called child or sub class). The main purpose is reusability of code — common code is written once in the base class and reused by every derived class. Inheritance represents an "IS-A" relationship: a Dog IS-A Animal, a Circle IS-A Shape. If you cannot say "IS-A", inheritance is probably the wrong tool.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्द कण्ठ पार्नुहोस् इनहेरिटेन्स भनेको एउटा क्लासले अर्को क्लासका गुण र मेम्बर फङ्सन प्राप्त गर्ने प्रक्रिया हो। गुण दिने क्लास base class (बाबु/parent) हो। गुण पाउने क्लास derived class (छोरा/child) हो। मुख्य उद्देश्य कोडको पुनः प्रयोग हो — साझा कोड एक पटक base मा लेख्ने र सबै derived क्लासमा चलाउने। इनहेरिटेन्सले "IS-A" सम्बन्ध जनाउँछ: Dog एक प्रकारको Animal हो, Circle एक प्रकारको Shape हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Advantages of inheritance Reusability — common code is written once and reused by every child class. Saves time and reduces code size — no duplication. Easy to extend — new features go in a derived class without touching the tested base class. Supports polymorphism — function overriding is impossible without inheritance. Better structure — the parent–child relationship models the real world clearly. Easier maintenance — fixing a bug in the base class fixes it for every derived class at once.
items.ne: इनहेरिटेन्सका फाइदा पुनः प्रयोग — साझा कोड एक पटक लेखेर सबै सन्तान क्लासमा चलाइन्छ। समय र कोड बचत — दोहोरो लेख्नु पर्दैन। सजिलो विस्तार — परीक्षण भइसकेको base नछोई derived मा नयाँ सुविधा थपिन्छ। Polymorphism सम्भव बनाउँछ — inheritance बिना overriding हुँदैन। राम्रो संरचना — बाबु–छोराको सम्बन्धले वास्तविक संसार प्रस्ट देखाउँछ। सजिलो मर्मत — base मा गल्ती सुधार्दा सबै derived क्लासमा एकैचोटि सुधार हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: The diamond problem and virtual base class
items.en: The problem In hybrid inheritance, suppose B and C both inherit from A, and D inherits from both B and C. D then receives two copies of everything in A — one through B and one through C. When you write d.show() the compiler cannot decide which copy to use, and reports an ambiguity error. Because the diagram is diamond-shaped, this is called the diamond problem.
items.ne: समस्या Hybrid inheritance मा मानौं B र C दुवैले A बाट इनहेरिट गर्छन्, र D ले B र C दुवैबाट। तब D ले A का सबै कुराको दुई प्रति पाउँछ — एउटा B बाट, अर्को C बाट। d.show() लेख्दा कम्पाइलरले कुन प्रति चलाउने भन्ने निर्णय गर्न सक्दैन र ambiguity error देखाउँछ। चित्र हीरा जस्तो देखिने भएकाले यसलाई diamond problem भनिन्छ।

items.en: private is inherited but not reachable. Use protected if the child must touch it.

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: The diamond problem and virtual base class
items.en: Multilevel. It is a chain: C from B, B from A. Every class here has exactly one parent — the chain simply has more than one level. Multiple means one class with two parents (class C : public A, public B), which is a different picture entirely. Count parents, not levels.
items.ne: Multilevel। यो शृंखला हो: C, B बाट र B, A बाट। यहाँ हरेक क्लासको एउटै बाबु छ — शृंखलामा तह मात्र धेरै छन्। Multiple भनेको एउटै क्लासका दुई बाबु हुनु हो। तह होइन, बाबु गन्नुहोस्।
