items.en: One child, two parents. Decide which line comes from which class before opening this — and whether the printing order is the order the bases were inherited in, or the order the calls were written in. एउटा child, दुई parent। खोल्नुअघि कुन लाइन कुन class बाट आउँछ निर्णय गर्नुहोस् — र छापिने क्रम base inherit गरेको क्रम हो कि call लेखिएको क्रम हो? Output Tall from father Fair from mother Smart on my own The diamond problem and virtual base class The problem In hybrid inheritance, suppose B and C both inherit from A, and D inherits from both B and C. D then receives two copies of everything in A — one through B and one through C. When you write d.show() the compiler cannot decide which copy to use, and reports an ambiguity error. Because the diagram is diamond-shaped, this is called the diamond problem. समस्या Hybrid inheritance मा मानौं B र C दुवैले A बाट इनहेरिट गर्छन्, र D ले B र C दुवैबाट। तब D ले A का सबै कुराको दुई प्रति पाउँछ — एउटा B बाट, अर्को C बाट। d.show() लेख्दा कम्पाइलरले कुन प्रति चलाउने भन्ने निर्णय गर्न सक्दैन र ambiguity error देखाउँछ। चित्र हीरा जस्तो देखिने भएकाले यसलाई diamond problem भनिन्छ। Example 3 Solving it with a virtual base class class A { public: void show() { cout << "From A"; } }; class B : virtual public A { }; // <-- virtual class C : virtual public A { }; // <-- virtual class D : public B, public C { }; int main() { D d; d.show(); // now unambiguous - only ONE copy of A exists return 0; } Output From A The keyword virtual tells C++ to keep only one shared copy of A, so the ambiguity disappears. A base class declared this way is called a virtual base class. virtual शब्दले C++ लाई A को एउटै साझा प्रति राख्न भन्छ, त्यसैले अलमल हट्छ। यसरी घोषित base क्लासलाई virtual base class भनिन्छ। Predict first
items.ne: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् class B : public A, and class C : public B. What is this called? class B : public A, र class C : public B। यसलाई के भनिन्छ? Multiple inheritance Multilevel inheritance Hierarchical inheritance Multilevel. It is a chain: C from B, B from A. Every class here has exactly one parent — the chain simply has more than one level. Multiple means one class with two parents (class C : public A, public B), which is a different picture entirely. Count parents, not levels. Multilevel। यो शृंखला हो: C, B बाट र B, A बाट। यहाँ हरेक क्लासको एउटै बाबु छ — शृंखलामा तह मात्र धेरै छन्। Multiple भनेको एउटै क्लासका दुई बाबु हुनु हो। तह होइन, बाबु गन्नुहोस्। Practise the judgement
items.ne: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Name the type of inheritance from the code What you will learn: to tell the five types apart quickly — the paper gives you code or a diagram and asks for the name, and multilevel versus multiple is where the mark is lost. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: पाँच प्रकार छिटो छुट्याउन — परीक्षामा कोड वा चित्र दिएर नाम सोधिन्छ, र अंक multilevel र multiple बीचमै गुम्छ। How to use this Two counts settle almost every case. How many parents does any one class have? More than one → multiple. How many children does one base have? More than one → hierarchical. A chain where each class has one parent but there is more than one level → multilevel. Case 5 mixes two shapes on purpose, because a real question sometimes does. Read the reason for how to answer when a diagram is not purely one type. दुई गणनाले प्रायः सबै केस मिलाउँछन्। कुनै एउटा क्लासका कति बाबु छन्? एकभन्दा बढी → multiple। एउटा base का कति छोरा छन्? एकभन्दा बढी → hierarchical। हरेकको एउटै बाबु तर धेरै तह भएको शृंखला → multilevel। केस ५ मा जानाजान दुई आकार मिसिएका छन्। Constructor and destructor order — asked very often {{dia:ctorOrder}} One object, three constructors. Base first going down, derived first coming back up. एउटा अब्जेक्ट, तीन कन्स्ट्रक्टर। बन्दा base पहिले, नष्ट हुँदा derived पहिले। The rule in one line When a derived object is created, the base class constructor runs FIRST, then the derived constructor. Destructors run in the exact reverse: derived destructor first, then base destructor. derived अब्जेक्ट बन्दा पहिले base को कन्स्ट्रक्टर चल्छ, अनि derived को। डिस्ट्रक्टर ठ्याक्कै उल्टो — पहिले derived, अनि base। Example 4 Proving the order — predict this output before you read it #include <iostream> using namespace std; class A { public: A() { cout << "A constructor" << endl; } ~A() { cout << "A destructor" << endl; } }; class B : public A { public: B() { cout << "B constructor" << endl; } ~B() { cout << "B destructor" << endl; } }; int main() { B obj; // only ONE object is created return 0; } This is the promise in the title — so keep it. One object, four lines of output. Write all four down in order before opening this. The destructor order is not the constructor order, and that is the exam question. शीर्षकमा गरिएको वाचा यही हो — त्यसैले पूरा गर्नुहोस्। एउटै object, चार लाइन output। खोल्नुअघि चारै लाइन क्रम मिलाएर लेख्नुहोस्। destructor को क्रम constructor को क्रम होइन, र परीक्षाको प्रश्न त्यही हो। Output A constructor B constructor B destructor A destructor Four lines from one object. The base is built first (you cannot build the first floor before the ground floor) and destroyed last. एउटै अब्जेक्टबाट चार लाइन। base पहिले बन्छ (भुइँतला नबनाई पहिलो तला बन्दैन) र अन्तिममा भत्किन्छ। Practise it — the help comes away
items.ne: · अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् — सहयोग घट्दै जान्छ

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् — सहयोग घट्दै जान्छ Exam focus — questions asked from this unit SEE exam connection
items.ne: · परीक्षा जोड

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · परीक्षा जोड Types of inheritance and constructor call order carry the marks here — the order question appears very often. Inheritance का प्रकार र constructor चल्ने क्रममा अंक छन् — क्रमको प्रश्न धेरै पटक आउँछ। Q1 · Define inheritance. Explain base class and derived class with syntax. [4 marks] Show the answer Inheritance is the process by which one class acquires the properties and member functions of another class. The class whose features are inherited is called the base class (parent), and the class that inherits them is called the derived class (child). The main purpose is reusability of code. Syntax: class Derived : access_mode Base { … }; for example class Dog : public Animal { }; परिभाषा + base/derived + syntax — तीनै लेख्नुहोस्। Q2 · Explain the types of inheritance with suitable diagrams. [6 marks] Show the answer Draw all five diagrams and give one line each: Single — one base, one derived (A → B). Multilevel — a chain where a derived class becomes a base (A → B → C). Multiple — two or more bases, one derived (A and B → C). Hierarchical — one base, many derived (A → B and A → C). Hybrid — a combination of two or more of the above; may cause the diamond problem, solved with a virtual base class. पाँचै चित्र कोर्नुहोस् र एक–एक लाइन व्याख्या दिनुहोस्। चित्र बिना पूरा अंक आउँदैन। Q3 · What is the output of the given program? (base and derived constructors) [3 marks] Show the answer Apply the rule: base class constructor first, then derived; destructors in exact reverse order. For a two-level program the answer is: A constructor, B constructor, B destructor, A destructor. For a three-level chain (Animal → Dog → Puppy) it is: Animal, Dog, Puppy going in and ~Puppy, ~Dog, ~Animal coming out. नियम लगाउनुहोस्: बन्दा माथिबाट तल, नष्ट हुँदा तलबाट माथि। Q4 · What is the diamond problem? How is it solved? [3 marks] Show the answer In hybrid inheritance, when two classes B and C both inherit from the same base A, and a fourth class D inherits from both B and C, class D receives two copies of A's members. The compiler cannot decide which copy to use, causing an ambiguity error. This is called the diamond problem. It is solved by declaring A as a virtual base class: class B : virtual public A { }; — then only one shared copy of A exists. समस्या + virtual कीवर्डको समाधान — दुवै लेख्नुहोस्। Key points to revise
items.ne: — दोहोर्‍याउनुपर्ने मुख्य बुँदा

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Inheritance
items.ne: इनहेरिटेन्स — गुण सर्ने प्रक्रिया

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.topic: The diamond problem and virtual base class
items.en: What you will learn: to tell the five types apart quickly — the paper gives you code or a diagram and asks for the name, and multilevel versus multiple is where the mark is lost.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: पाँच प्रकार छिटो छुट्याउन — परीक्षामा कोड वा चित्र दिएर नाम सोधिन्छ, र अंक multilevel र multiple बीचमै गुम्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: In overloading the compiler picks the correct function from the arguments before the program runs, so it is compile-time (static) polymorphism.
items.ne: Overloading मा कम्पाइलरले आर्गुमेन्ट हेरेर प्रोग्राम चल्नु अघि नै सही फङ्सन छान्छ, त्यसैले यो compile-time polymorphism हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Overriding means a derived class redefines a base class function, so a base and derived class — that is, inheritance — must exist.
items.ne: Overriding मा derived क्लासले base क्लासको फङ्सन पुनः लेख्छ, त्यसैले base र derived क्लास — अर्थात् inheritance — हुनैपर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: A virtual function tells C++ to decide at run time, by looking at the actual object the base pointer points to.
items.ne: virtual फङ्सनले C++ लाई चल्दै गर्दा, base पोइन्टरले देखाएको वास्तविक अब्जेक्ट हेरेर निर्णय गर्न लगाउँछ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Overloading needs the same name with a DIFFERENT parameter list — different types, or a different number of parameters. Option 2 changes the types, so it is valid. Option 1 differs only in return type, which C++ rejects. Option 3 only renames the parameters, so the two are identical. Option 4 has two different names, so it is not overloading at all.
items.ne: Overloading लाई उही नाम तर फरक parameter सूची चाहिन्छ — फरक किसिम, वा फरक सङ्ख्या। दोस्रोले किसिम बदल्छ, त्यसैले मान्य छ। पहिलोमा return type मात्र फरक छ, जसलाई C++ ले अस्वीकार गर्छ। तेस्रोले parameter को नाम मात्र बदल्छ, त्यसैले दुवै उही हुन्। चौथोमा नाम नै फरक छ, त्यसैले overloading होइन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: If the compiler can tell which function will run just by reading the code, the decision is made early — static or early binding. That is overloading. When the decision can only be made while the program runs, using a virtual function through a base pointer, it is dynamic or late binding.
items.ne: कोड पढेरै कुन function चल्छ भनी compiler ले भन्न सक्छ भने निर्णय चाँडै हुन्छ — static वा early binding। त्यो overloading हो। Base pointer हुँदै virtual function प्रयोग गर्दा निर्णय प्रोग्राम चल्दा मात्र हुन सक्छ भने त्यो dynamic वा late binding हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Without virtual the compiler decides from the POINTER's type, not the object's, so Shape's version runs even though the object really is a Circle. Adding virtual to the base function is what defers the decision to run time and makes Circle's version run. This single keyword is the most examined point in the unit.
items.ne: virtual नभए compiler ले object होइन, pointer को किसिम हेरेर निर्णय गर्छ — त्यसैले object साँच्चै Circle भए पनि Shape कै संस्करण चल्छ। Base function मा virtual थप्दा निर्णय चल्ने बेलासम्म पर सर्छ र Circle कै संस्करण चल्छ। यस युनिटमा सबैभन्दा बढी सोधिने बिन्दु यही एउटा keyword हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The same line p->draw() is about to run twice. Watch where it ends up.
items.ne: उही लाइन p->draw() दुई पटक चल्न लागेको छ। कहाँ पुग्छ हेर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: p is a Shape pointer. Its declared type never changes — only what it points at.
items.ne: p एउटा Shape पोइन्टर हो। यसको घोषित प्रकार बदलिँदैन — केवल यसले देखाउने वस्तु बदलिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: p = &c — the pointer now holds the address of a Circle object.
items.ne: p = &c — अब पोइन्टरसँग Circle अब्जेक्टको ठेगाना छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: p->draw() runs. Because draw() is virtual, C++ looks at the OBJECT and calls Circle::draw().
items.ne: p->draw() चल्यो। draw() virtual भएकाले C++ ले अब्जेक्ट हेरेर Circle::draw() बोलायो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: p = &s — the SAME pointer, now pointing at a Square.
items.ne: p = &s — उही पोइन्टर, अब Square तिर देखाइरहेको।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The identical line p->draw() now calls Square::draw(). The line did not change — the object did.
items.ne: उही लाइन p->draw() ले अब Square::draw() बोलायो। लाइन बदलिएन — अब्जेक्ट बदलियो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: This only happens because draw() is virtual. Without it, C++ would decide from the pointer type at compile time.
items.ne: यो draw() virtual भएकाले मात्र हुन्छ। नभए C++ ले पोइन्टरको प्रकार हेरेर कम्पाइल गर्दै निर्णय गर्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Overloading, overriding, or neither?
items.ne: Overloading, overriding, कि दुवै होइन?

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Three checks, in order. Are the functions in ONE class or in a base and a derived class? Are the parameter lists the same or different? And if they are the same, is the base function virtual? Only the last one decides run-time behaviour.
items.ne: तीन जाँच, क्रमैसँग। फङ्सनहरू एउटै क्लासमा छन् कि base र derived मा? प्यारामिटर सूची उही छ कि फरक? र उही भए base को फङ्सन virtual छ? run-time व्यवहार अन्तिमले मात्र तय गर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.ref: polykind · option "Neither — the base version runs"
items.en: Neither — the base version runs
items.ne: दुवै होइन — base कै संस्करण चल्छ

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: One class, one name, two different parameter lists — one argument against two. There is no inheritance here at all, and the compiler can pick the right function from the call itself, so this is compile-time polymorphism.
items.ne: एउटै क्लास, एउटै नाम, दुई फरक प्यारामिटर सूची — एक र दुई। यहाँ inheritance नै छैन, र compiler ले call आफैंबाट सही फङ्सन छान्न सक्छ, त्यसैले यो compile-time polymorphism हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Base and derived, the same name and the same empty parameter list, and the base function is virtual. The call goes through a base pointer, so the decision waits until the program runs and Circle::draw is what executes.
items.ne: Base र derived, उही नाम र उही खाली प्यारामिटर सूची, र base को फङ्सन virtual छ। Call base pointer मार्फत जाने भएकाले निर्णय प्रोग्राम चल्दासम्म कुर्छ र Circle::draw चल्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: It looks like the case above with one word removed, and that word is the whole mechanism. Without virtual the compiler decides from the POINTER type, which is Shape, so Shape::draw runs even though the object is a Circle. This is function hiding, not overriding.
items.ne: यो माथिको केसबाट एउटा शब्द हटाएको जस्तै देखिन्छ, र त्यो शब्द नै पूरै प्रविधि हो। virtual नभए compiler ले POINTER को प्रकार — अर्थात् Shape — बाट निर्णय गर्छ, त्यसैले वस्तु Circle भए पनि Shape::draw चल्छ। यो function hiding हो, overriding होइन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The parameter lists are identical and only the return type differs, which C++ does not accept — the compiler cannot tell from a call which one you meant. This will not compile, so it is not overloading, and with no derived class it cannot be overriding either.
items.ne: प्यारामिटर सूची ठ्याक्कै उही छ, फरक रिटर्न टाइपमा मात्र — C++ ले यो स्वीकार गर्दैन, किनभने call हेरेर compiler ले कुन चाहिएको भन्न सक्दैन। यो compile हुँदैन, त्यसैले overloading होइन, र derived क्लास नै नभएकाले overriding पनि होइन।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Dog::speak replaces Animal::speak with the same signature, so it is overriding and the derived version runs. Note that it runs here because the object type is known exactly, not because of virtual — virtual only changes what happens through a base pointer or reference.
items.ne: Dog::speak ले उही हस्ताक्षरसहित Animal::speak लाई प्रतिस्थापन गर्छ, त्यसैले यो overriding हो र derived कै संस्करण चल्छ। तर यहाँ चल्नुको कारण virtual होइन, वस्तुको प्रकार ठ्याक्कै थाहा हुनु हो — virtual ले base pointer वा reference मार्फत मात्र फरक पार्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Three functions, one name, parameter TYPES different each time. Overloading does not require a different number of parameters — a different type, or even a different order, is enough for the compiler to tell them apart.
items.ne: तीन फङ्सन, एउटै नाम, हरेक पटक प्यारामिटरको प्रकार फरक। Overloading लाई प्यारामिटरको सङ्ख्या फरक हुनु जरुरी छैन — प्रकार फरक, वा क्रम मात्र फरक भए पनि compiler ले छुट्याउन सक्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Learn this whole tree — the branches, the other names, and what achieves each.
items.ne: यो पूरा रूख कण्ठ पार्नुहोस् — हाँगा, अर्को नाम, र कसले हासिल गर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: The compiler matches the call against each version's parameter list and picks the one that fits — all before the program runs.
items.ne: कम्पाइलरले कललाई हरेक संस्करणको प्यारामिटरसँग मिलाएर सही एउटा छान्छ — प्रोग्राम चल्नु अघि नै।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: virtual makes C++ look at the real object.
items.ne: उही पोइन्टर, उही कल — तर दुई फरक जवाफ, किनकि virtual

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Same person — different behaviour in different places. The name did not change; the situation decided the behaviour. That is polymorphism.
items.ne: उदाहरण — एउटै मान्छे, धेरै भूमिका। एउटै मान्छे घरमा छोरा, स्कुलमा विद्यार्थी, पसलमा ग्राहक र अस्पतालमा बिरामी हुन्छ। व्यक्ति उही, ठाउँ अनुसार व्यवहार फरक। नाम फेरिएन, अवस्थाले व्यवहार तय गर्‍यो — यही polymorphism हो।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Definition — learn this wording The word polymorphism comes from Greek: poly means many and morph means forms. So polymorphism literally means "many forms". In C++, polymorphism is the ability of the same function name or the same operator to behave differently in different situations, depending on the object or on the arguments used.
items.ne: परिभाषा — यही शब्द कण्ठ पार्नुहोस् Polymorphism ग्रीक शब्दबाट बनेको हो: poly = धेरै, morph = रूप। अर्थात् "धेरै रूप"। C++ मा एउटै फङ्सनको नाम वा एउटै अपरेटर ले फरक अवस्थामा फरक व्यवहार गर्ने क्षमतालाई polymorphism भनिन्छ — कुन अब्जेक्ट वा कस्तो आर्गुमेन्ट प्रयोग भयो, त्यसमा भर पर्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Function overloading Function overloading means writing two or more functions with the same name in the same class, but with different parameter lists. The parameter lists must differ in the number of parameters, the type of parameters, or their order. Important: a difference in the return type alone is NOT enough. Two functions with the same name and same parameters but different return types cause a compiler error.
items.ne: फङ्सन ओभरलोडिङ Function overloading भनेको उही क्लास भित्र उही नाम तर फरक प्यारामिटर भएका दुई वा बढी फङ्सन लेख्नु हो। प्यारामिटर संख्या, प्रकार, वा क्रम मा फरक हुनुपर्छ। महत्त्वपूर्ण: return type मात्र फरक भएर पुग्दैन। नाम र प्यारामिटर उही तर return type फरक भए कम्पाइलर error दिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Operator overloading Operator overloading means giving an additional meaning to an existing C++ operator so that it also works with objects of your own class. For example + normally adds numbers. By overloading it, you can make c1 + c2 add two Complex number objects. The syntax uses the keyword operator followed by the symbol.
items.ne: अपरेटर ओभरलोडिङ Operator overloading भनेको भइरहेको C++ अपरेटरलाई थप अर्थ दिनु हो, ताकि यो तपाईंकै क्लासका अब्जेक्टसँग पनि काम गरोस्। जस्तै + ले सामान्यतया संख्या जोड्छ। ओभरलोड गरेपछि c1 + c2 ले दुई Complex अब्जेक्ट जोड्न सक्छ। Syntax मा operator कीवर्ड पछि चिन्ह लेखिन्छ।

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: Function overriding Function overriding means the derived class defines a function with exactly the same name, the same return type and the same parameters as a function already present in its base class. The derived version replaces the base version for objects of the derived class. Overriding requires inheritance — it is impossible without a base and a derived class. If the base function is marked virtual and you call it through a base class pointer, C++ calls the derived version at run time. That is run-time polymorphism. Without virtual, the base version is called instead.
items.ne: फङ्सन ओभरराइडिङ Function overriding भनेको derived क्लासमा base क्लासकै फङ्सन जस्तै उही नाम, उही return type र उही प्यारामिटर भएको फङ्सन लेख्नु हो। derived अब्जेक्टका लागि derived कै संस्करणले base को संस्करणलाई प्रतिस्थापन गर्छ। Overriding का लागि inheritance अनिवार्य छ। base फङ्सनमा virtual लेखिएको छ र base पोइन्टर बाट बोलाइयो भने C++ ले चल्दै गर्दा derived संस्करण बोलाउँछ — यही run-time polymorphism हो। virtual नलेखे base कै संस्करण चल्छ।

items.en: Advantages of polymorphism One interface, many implementations — easier to read, write and remember. Code reusability and shorter programs. Flexibility — new derived classes can be added without changing existing code. Supports dynamic binding and cleaner program design. Reduces the number of different function names a programmer must remember.
items.ne: पोलिमर्फिज्मका फाइदा एउटै इन्टरफेस, धेरै काम — पढ्न, लेख्न र सम्झन सजिलो। कोड पुनः प्रयोग र छोटो प्रोग्राम। लचकता — पुरानो कोड नछोई नयाँ derived क्लास थप्न सकिन्छ। Dynamic binding सम्भव बनाउँछ। फरक–फरक नाम सम्झिरहनु पर्दैन।

What you will learn: to apply the table above to code you have not seen. The paper prints a class and asks which kind of polymorphism it is — and two of these six cases are neither, which is where the mark goes. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: माथिको तालिकालाई नदेखेको कोडमा लागू गर्न। परीक्षामा क्लास छापेर कुन किसिमको polymorphism हो सोधिन्छ — र यी छ केसमध्ये दुई "दुवै होइन" हुन्, अंक त्यहीँ जान्छ। How to use this Work the three checks in the order the lead gives them. Cases 3 and 4 are the two that are neither, and they fail for completely different reasons: case 3 compiles and quietly runs the wrong function, case 4 does not compile at all. Read both reasons — a question that shows you code without virtual is testing case 3 on purpose. लिडमा दिइएका तीन जाँच क्रमैसँग गर्नुहोस्। एक क्लास कि दुई? एउटै क्लास भए overloading मात्र हुन सक्छ। प्यारामिटर उही कि फरक? फरक भए overloading; उही भए पुनर्परिभाषा हेर्दै छ। त्यसपछि मात्र virtual खोज्नुहोस्। केस ३ र ४ दुवै होइन, तर कारण बेग्लै छ: केस ३ compile हुन्छ र चुपचाप गलत फङ्सन चलाउँछ, केस ४ compile नै हुँदैन।

The derived version replaces the base version for objects of the derived class. Overriding requires inheritance — it is impossible without a base and a derived class. If the base function is marked virtual and you call it through a base class pointer, C++ calls the derived version at run time. That is run-time polymorphism. Without virtual, the base version is called instead. फङ्सन ओभरराइडिङ Function overriding भनेको derived क्लासमा base क्लासकै फङ्सन जस्तै उही नाम, उही return type र उही प्यारामिटर भएको फङ्सन लेख्नु हो। derived अब्जेक्टका लागि derived कै संस्करणले base को संस्करणलाई प्रतिस्थापन गर्छ। Overriding का लागि inheritance अनिवार्य छ। base फङ्सनमा virtual लेखिएको छ र base पोइन्टर बाट बोलाइयो भने C++ ले चल्दै गर्दा derived संस्करण बोलाउँछ — यही run-time polymorphism हो। virtual नलेखे base कै संस्करण चल्छ। {{dia:dispatch}} The same pointer and the same call give two different answers, because virtual makes C++ look at the real object. उही पोइन्टर, उही कल — तर दुई फरक जवाफ, किनकि virtual ले C++ लाई वास्तविक अब्जेक्ट हेर्न लगाउँछ। Example 3 With and without virtual — the exam's favourite trick class Base { public: void show() { cout << "Base show" << endl; } // NOT virtual }; class Derived : public Base { public: void show() { cout << "Derived show" << endl; } }; int main() { Base *p; Derived d; p = &d; p->show(); // a Base pointer, holding a Derived object return 0; } A Base pointer is holding a Derived object, and show() is not virtual. Commit to one line of output. Most people answer with the type of the object; without virtual, C++ answers with the type of the pointer. Base pointer ले Derived object समातेको छ, र show() virtual छैन। एउटै लाइन output भन्नुहोस्। धेरैले object को प्रकार भन्छन्; virtual नभए C++ ले pointer को प्रकार भन्छ। Output without virtual Base show Now add one word — virtual void show() in Base — and the very same program prints Derived show instead. One keyword changes the whole output. That is exactly what the examiner is testing. अब Base मा एउटा शब्द थप्नुहोस् — virtual void show() — र उही प्रोग्रामले Derived show छाप्छ। एउटा कीवर्डले पूरै आउटपुट फेर्छ। परीक्षकले जाँच्ने ठ्याक्कै यही हो। Common mistake Thinking overriding works through the object as well as the pointer. If you write Derived d; d.show(); the derived version runs whether or not the function is virtual — because the object's type is known exactly. virtual only matters when you call through a base class pointer or reference. Derived d; d.show(); लेख्दा virtual भए पनि नभए पनि derived कै संस्करण चल्छ — किनकि अब्जेक्टको प्रकार ठ्याक्कै थाहा हुन्छ। virtual को महत्त्व base पोइन्टर बाट बोलाउँदा मात्र देखिन्छ। virtual matters only through a pointer or reference. Through the object, the type is already known. virtual ले pointer वा reference मार्फत मात्र फरक पार्छ। वस्तु मार्फत त प्रकार पहिले नै थाहा हुन्छ। ▶ Experiment — Which function actually runs? Decide first, then check. This is the single most-tested idea in the unit, and the one students most often get backwards. Predict first
items.ne: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् Shape has a virtual void show(). Circle overrides it. You write Shape *p = &c; where c is a Circle, then call p->show(). Which one runs? Shape::show() Circle::show() Both, in order Compiler error Because show() is virtual, C++ waits until the program is running and looks at the object, not at the pointer's type. The object is a Circle, so Circle::show() runs. Delete the word virtual and the answer flips to Shape::show() — that is the whole idea in one line. show() virtual भएकाले C++ ले प्रोग्राम चल्दै गर्दा पोइन्टरको प्रकार होइन, अब्जेक्ट हेर्छ। अब्जेक्ट Circle भएकाले Circle::show() चल्छ। virtual हटाए उत्तर Shape::show() मा पल्टिन्छ — पूरै कुरा यही एक लाइनमा छ। Interactive experiment
items.ne: · अन्तरक्रियात्मक प्रयोग

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · अन्तरक्रियात्मक प्रयोग Compile-time choice vs run-time choice What you will learn: when C++ decides which function to call. Overloading is settled while compiling; a virtual call is settled while running. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: C++ ले कुन फङ्सन बोलाउने भन्ने कहिले निर्णय गर्छ — overloading कम्पाइल गर्दा, virtual चल्दै गर्दा। Try each call area(5) area(4, 6) p = &s; p->show() p = &c; p->show() Reset Why did this happen? Overloading — the compiler counts the arguments and picks the matching version before the program ever runs. Compile-time. Virtual override — the computer looks at the object the pointer actually points to, while the program is running. Run-time. Same call, different output. Overloading: कम्पाइलरले आर्गुमेन्ट गनेर प्रोग्राम चल्नु अघि नै छान्छ — compile-time। Virtual override: पोइन्टरले देखाएको वास्तविक अब्जेक्ट हेरेर चल्दै गर्दा छान्छ — run-time। उही कल, फरक आउटपुट। Overloading vs Overriding — the key table BasisFunction OverloadingFunction Overriding MeaningSame function name with different parameters in the same class.Same function name with the same parameters, redefined in a derived class. InheritanceNot required.Required — there must be a base and a derived class. ParametersMust be different — in number, type or order.Must be exactly the same. Return typeMay be same or different (return type alone is not enough).Must be the same. BindingEarly / static binding.Late / dynamic binding when virtual is used. TypeCompile-time polymorphism.Run-time polymorphism. virtual keywordNot used.virtual is used in the base class. PurposeTo give one name to several similar jobs.To give the child a different version of the parent's function. छोटो सार Overloading = उही क्लासमा उही नाम तर फरक प्यारामिटर; inheritance चाहिँदैन; compile-time। Overriding = derived क्लासमा उही नाम र उही प्यारामिटर; inheritance चाहिन्छ; virtual राखे run-time। Practise the judgement
items.ne: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Read the code and name it: overloading, overriding, or neither? What you will learn: to apply the table above to code you have not seen. The paper prints a class and asks which kind of polymorphism it is — and two of these six cases are neither, which is where the mark goes. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: माथिको तालिकालाई नदेखेको कोडमा लागू गर्न। परीक्षामा क्लास छापेर कुन किसिमको polymorphism हो सोधिन्छ — र यी छ केसमध्ये दुई "दुवै होइन" हुन्, अंक त्यहीँ जान्छ। How to use this Work the three checks in the order the lead gives them. One class or two? One class means it can only be overloading. Same parameters or different? Different means overloading; the same means you are looking at a redefinition. Only then look for virtual. Cases 3 and 4 are the two that are neither, and they fail for completely different reasons: case 3 compiles and quietly runs the wrong function, case 4 does not compile at all. Read both reasons — a question that shows you code without virtual is testing case 3 on purpose. लिडमा दिइएका तीन जाँच क्रमैसँग गर्नुहोस्। एक क्लास कि दुई? एउटै क्लास भए overloading मात्र हुन सक्छ। प्यारामिटर उही कि फरक? फरक भए overloading; उही भए पुनर्परिभाषा हेर्दै छ। त्यसपछि मात्र virtual खोज्नुहोस्। केस ३ र ४ दुवै होइन, तर कारण बेग्लै छ: केस ३ compile हुन्छ र चुपचाप गलत फङ्सन चलाउँछ, केस ४ compile नै हुँदैन। Advantages of polymorphism One interface, many implementations — easier to read, write and remember. Code reusability and shorter programs. Flexibility — new derived classes can be added without changing existing code. Supports dynamic binding and cleaner program design. Reduces the number of different function names a programmer must remember. पोलिमर्फिज्मका फाइदा एउटै इन्टरफेस, धेरै काम — पढ्न, लेख्न र सम्झन सजिलो। कोड पुनः प्रयोग र छोटो प्रोग्राम। लचकता — पुरानो कोड नछोई नयाँ derived क्लास थप्न सकिन्छ। Dynamic binding सम्भव बनाउँछ। फरक–फरक नाम सम्झिरहनु पर्दैन। Exam focus — questions asked from this unit SEE exam connection
items.ne: · परीक्षा जोड

items.subject: grade10/oop-cpp
items.en: · परीक्षा जोड Overloading versus overriding, and compile-time versus run-time, are the highest-frequency questions in the whole subject. Overloading र Overriding, अनि Compile-time र Run-time — यी पूरै विषयकै सबैभन्दा बढी सोधिने प्रश्न हुन्। Q1 · Define polymorphism. Explain its types with examples. [6 marks] Show the answer Polymorphism comes from the Greek words poly (many) and morph (forms), so it means many forms. In C++ it is the ability of the same function name or operator to behave differently in different situations. Compile-time (static) polymorphism — the compiler decides which function to call while compiling, by checking the arguments. It is achieved by function overloading and operator overloading. Example: three area() functions with different parameters. Run-time (dynamic) polymorphism — the decision is made while the program runs, based on the object the base pointer points to. It is achieved by function overriding with virtual functions. Example: Base *p = &derivedObj; p->show(); परिभाषा + दुवै प्रकार + एक–एक उदाहरण। चित्र (रूख) कोरे झन् राम्रो। Q2 · Differentiate between function overloading and function overriding. [5 marks] Show the answer Write a table with at least five rows: meaning (same class, different parameters vs derived class, same parameters); inheritance (not required vs required); parameters (must differ vs must be identical); binding (early/static vs late/dynamic); type (compile-time vs run-time); and the virtual keyword (not used vs used in the base class). कम्तीमा पाँच हरफको तालिका लेख्नुहोस्। Q3 · What is a virtual function? Why is it needed? [3 marks] Show the answer A virtual function is a member function declared in the base class using the keyword virtual and redefined (overridden) in a derived class. It is needed so that when the function is called through a base class pointer, C++ decides at run time which version to run by looking at the actual object being pointed to, instead of the pointer's type. Without virtual the base class version would always be called, and run-time polymorphism would be impossible. परिभाषा + किन चाहिन्छ (base पोइन्टरबाट derived संस्करण चलाउन) — दुवै लेख्नुहोस्। Q4 · Write a program to demonstrate run-time polymorphism. [5 marks] Show the answer Write a base class Shape with virtual void draw(), two derived classes Circle and Square that each override draw(), and a main() that declares Shape *p; then points it first at a Circle object and then at a Square object, calling p->draw(); each time. The output will be "Drawing a Circle" then "Drawing a Square" — the same call giving two different results. That is the full program traced step by step in the Trace a Program section. Trace a Program सेक्सनको Program 3 नै यसको पूरा उत्तर हो — त्यहीँ लाइन–लाइन हेर्नुहोस्। Key points to revise

items.en: The difference is scope. A program is a single ordered set of instructions for one task. Software is the whole package — one or more programs, the data files they need, and the documentation. Every program is software, but software is normally many programs: a browser is one, an operating system is hundreds.
items.ne: फरक दायराको हो। Program एउटै कामका लागि क्रमबद्ध निर्देशनको एउटा समूह हो। Software चाहिँ पूरै प्याकेज — एक वा धेरै program, तिनलाई चाहिने data फाइल, र documentation। हरेक program software हो, तर software प्रायः धेरै program हुन्छ: browser एउटा हो, operating system सयौं।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Low level means close to the hardware, and only two categories qualify: machine language and assembly language. C, Java and Python are all high level. C is sometimes called a middle level language because it can reach memory addresses directly, but it is still translated by a compiler and it is still written in English-like words.
items.ne: Low level को अर्थ hardware सँग नजिक हुनु हो, र दुई श्रेणी मात्र यसमा पर्छन्: machine language र assembly language। C, Java र Python सबै high level हुन्। C लाई कहिलेकाहीं middle level भनिन्छ किनभने यसले मेमोरीको ठेगानासम्म सिधै पुग्न सक्छ, तर यो पनि compiler ले अनुवाद गर्छ र अङ्ग्रेजीजस्ता शब्दमै लेखिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: C is compiled, not interpreted. The compiler reads the whole file before anything runs, so a grammar mistake anywhere means no executable file is created and nothing executes. Option A describes an interpreter, which runs line by line and therefore does stop part way. This is the practical difference between the two translators.
items.ne: C compile हुने भाषा हो, interpret हुने होइन। Compiler ले केही चल्नुअघि पूरै फाइल पढ्छ, त्यसैले जहाँसुकैको व्याकरण गल्तीले executable फाइल बन्दैन र केही चल्दैन। विकल्प (क) ले interpreter को वर्णन गर्छ, जसले एक–एक लाइन चलाउँछ र त्यसैले बीचमै रोकिन्छ। दुई अनुवादकबीचको व्यावहारिक फरक यही हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Printing sends something out of the program to the person, so it is output, and input and output share the same slanted parallelogram. The rectangle is for processing — a calculation or an assignment that happens inside the program where nobody sees it. Drawing a rectangle here is one of the commonest ways marks are lost on a flowchart question.
items.ne: छाप्नु भनेको प्रोग्रामबाट मान्छेसम्म केही पठाउनु हो, त्यसैले यो output हो, र input अनि output दुवैलाई उही छड्के parallelogram प्रयोग हुन्छ। Rectangle चाहिँ processing का लागि हो — प्रोग्रामभित्रै हुने गणना वा assignment, जुन कसैले देख्दैन। यहाँ rectangle कोर्नु flowchart को प्रश्नमा अंक गुमाउने सबैभन्दा सामान्य तरिकामध्ये एक हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Finiteness says an algorithm must end after a limited number of steps. This one has an input and it certainly has output, and every step is clear enough to carry out, so those three properties hold. What it never does is stop, and a procedure that never stops has not solved the problem. Missing the Stop box in a flowchart is the drawn version of the same mistake.
items.ne: Finiteness ले algorithm सीमित चरणपछि सकिनै पर्छ भन्छ। यसमा input छ र output पक्कै छ, र हरेक चरण गर्न पुग्ने गरी स्पष्ट छ — त्यसैले ती तीन गुण पूरा भए। नहुने कुरा रोकिनु हो, र कहिल्यै नरोकिने विधिले समस्या समाधान गरेको हुँदैन। Flowchart मा Stop बाकस छुटाउनु यही गल्तीको कोरिएको रूप हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: The test is the ratio between data and calculation. Here there is a very large amount of data and the arithmetic is addition, so it is a business application, and what it needs is storage, retrieval, sorting and readable output. A scientific application is the opposite shape: a small amount of data and an enormous amount of calculation, which is why option A names floating-point speed for the wrong kind of job.
items.ne: जाँच data र गणनाको अनुपात हो। यहाँ data धेरै छ र गणना भनेको जोड मात्र, त्यसैले यो व्यावसायिक प्रयोग हो, र यसलाई भण्डारण, खोजी, क्रम मिलाउने र पढ्न मिल्ने output चाहिन्छ। वैज्ञानिक प्रयोगको आकार उल्टो हुन्छ: थोरै data र ठूलो गणना — त्यसैले विकल्प (क) ले गलत किसिमको कामलाई floating-point गति तोकेको छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Portability in C belongs to the source, not to the executable. The .exe is machine code built for one processor and one operating system, so copying it to a different kind of machine gives a file that cannot run. The .c file is ordinary text: compile it again on the far side and the same program is available there. This is why "C is portable" and "my .exe will not run on Linux" are both true at once.
items.ne: C मा portability source को गुण हो, executable को होइन। .exe एउटा प्रोसेसर र एउटा operating system का लागि बनेको मेसिन कोड हो, त्यसैले फरक किसिमको मेसिनमा सार्दा नचल्ने फाइल मात्र पुग्छ। .c फाइल सामान्य पाठ हो: त्यहाँ पुगेर फेरि compile गरे उही प्रोग्राम त्यहाँ पनि चल्छ। त्यसैले "C portable छ" र "मेरो .exe Linux मा चल्दैन" दुवै एकैचोटि सत्य हुन्छन्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Which category of programming language?
items.ne: प्रोग्रामिङ भाषाको कुन श्रेणी?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Each case describes how the instructions are written. Decide whether it is machine level, assembly level or high level. The test is who can read it without help: the processor, a person with a manual, or anybody.
items.ne: हरेक केसमा निर्देशन कसरी लेखिएको छ भनिएको छ। यो machine level, assembly level कि high level हो छुट्याउनुहोस्। जाँच यही हो: सहायताविना कसले पढ्न सक्छ — प्रोसेसरले, म्यानुअल भएको मान्छेले, कि जोसुकैले?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Which flowchart symbol does this step need?
items.ne: यो चरणलाई कुन flowchart चिन्ह चाहिन्छ?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Each case is one step of a flowchart. Choose the shape you would draw for it. The question to ask is not what the step says but what KIND of thing it is: a boundary, a crossing, a calculation or a question.
items.ne: हरेक केस flowchart को एउटा चरण हो। त्यसका लागि कुन आकार कोर्ने छान्नुहोस्। सोध्नुपर्ने प्रश्न चरणले के भन्यो होइन, यो कुन किसिमको कुरा हो भन्ने हो: सिमाना, पार गर्ने, गणना, कि प्रश्न?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Only 0s and 1s, which is the one form the processor reads directly with no translation at all. It is also the only level that is different on every make of processor, and the reason nobody writes it by hand today.
items.ne: केवल ० र १, जुन प्रोसेसरले कुनै अनुवादविनै सिधै पढ्ने एकमात्र रूप हो। हरेक बनोटको प्रोसेसरमा फरक हुने तह पनि यही हो, र आजकल कसैले हातले नलेख्ने कारण त्यही।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Short word-like codes such as MOV and ADD stand one-for-one for machine instructions. It is readable by a person who knows the processor, and it still needs an assembler before it can run.
items.ne: MOV र ADD जस्ता छोटा सङ्केत एक–एक गरी मेसिन निर्देशनका ठाउँमा आउँछन्। प्रोसेसर जान्ने मान्छेले पढ्न सक्छ, र चल्नुअघि assembler चाहिन्छ नै।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: English-like words and ordinary arithmetic, with nothing in it that names a register or an address. That is what high level means: written for the person, then translated by a compiler for the machine.
items.ne: अङ्ग्रेजीजस्ता शब्द र सामान्य गणित, र यसमा कुनै register वा ठेगानाको नाम छैन। High level को अर्थ यही हो: मान्छेका लागि लेखिने, अनि compiler ले मेसिनका लागि अनुवाद गर्ने।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Portability is the property high level languages have and the other two do not. Machine and assembly code are tied to one processor family, so the same file could not be moved between two different machines.
items.ne: एउटै source दुई ठाउँमा चल्नु — portability — high level भाषाको गुण हो, अरू दुईको होइन। Machine र assembly कोड एउटै प्रोसेसर परिवारसँग बाँधिन्छ, त्यसैले उही फाइल सार्न मिल्दैन।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Registers appear by name in assembly and nowhere else that a Grade 9 student meets. Machine level has registers too but no names at all, and a high level language hides registers completely behind variables.
items.ne: Register को नाम assembly मा मात्र देखिन्छ। Machine level मा register त छन् तर नाम नै हुँदैन, र high level भाषाले register लाई variable पछाडि पूरै लुकाउँछ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Anything that crosses the boundary between the program and the person is input or output, and both use the parallelogram. Reading from a keyboard and printing to a screen are drawn with the same shape.
items.ne: प्रोग्राम र मान्छेबीचको सिमाना नाघ्ने जुनसुकै कुरा input वा output हो, र दुवैलाई parallelogram नै। Keyboard बाट पढ्नु र पर्दामा छाप्नु एउटै आकारले कोरिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A calculation or an assignment changes a value inside the program and nobody outside sees it happen. That is processing, and processing is the rectangle — the commonest box in any flowchart.
items.ne: गणना वा assignment ले प्रोग्रामभित्रको मान बदल्छ र बाहिर कसैले देख्दैन। त्यो processing हो, र processing भनेको rectangle — कुनै पनि flowchart मा सबैभन्दा धेरै आउने बाकस।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A question with a yes and a no is a decision, drawn as a diamond. It is the only symbol with two arrows leaving it, and leaving one of those two branches unlabelled is where marks are usually lost.
items.ne: हो र होइन भएको प्रश्न decision हो, र त्यो diamond ले कोरिन्छ। दुई तीर बाहिर जाने एकमात्र चिन्ह यही हो, र ती दुई शाखामध्ये एउटामा नाम नलेख्दा प्रायः अंक जान्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Start and Stop are terminals and both are ovals. Every flowchart needs one start, and a chart whose path can finish without reaching a stop is incomplete however correct the middle is.
items.ne: Start र Stop दुवै terminal हुन् र दुवै oval। हरेक flowchart मा एउटा start चाहिन्छ, र बीचको भाग जतिसुकै ठिक भए पनि stop नपुगी सकिने chart अपूरो हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Display is output, so it takes the same parallelogram as the read step did. Students who draw a rectangle here have confused what the program computes with what the person is shown.
items.ne: Display भनेको output हो, त्यसैले read कै जस्तो parallelogram नै। यहाँ rectangle कोर्ने विद्यार्थीले प्रोग्रामले गणना गरेको कुरा र मान्छेलाई देखाइएको कुरा मिसाएका हुन्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.1 Program, programmer, programming language, software — प्रोग्राम, प्रोग्रामर, प्रोग्रामिङ भाषा, सफ्टवेयर
items.en: Why the four words need each other: the programmer writes the source in a programming language, a translator turns it into something the machine runs, and the result shipped to a user is software. Note where each kind of error appears.
items.ne: चारै शब्द किन एकअर्कालाई चाहिन्छन्: प्रोग्रामरले प्रोग्रामिङ भाषामा source लेख्छ, अनुवादकले त्यसलाई मेसिनले चलाउन मिल्ने बनाउँछ, र प्रयोगकर्तासम्म पुग्ने नतिजा software हो। कुन किसिमको त्रुटि कहाँ देखिन्छ, ध्यान दिनुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.4 Program design tools — algorithm and flowchart — प्रोग्राम डिजाइनका साधन — algorithm र flowchart
items.en: The six symbols. In an examination the shapes are marked as well as the logic, so a correct method drawn with the wrong boxes still loses marks.
items.ne: छ वटा चिन्ह। परीक्षामा तर्कसँगै आकारको पनि अंक हुन्छ, त्यसैले सही विधि गलत बाकसमा कोरे पनि अंक जान्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Write an algorithm for a small problem and draw its flowchart with the correct symbols.
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा: program, programmer, programming language र software को परिभाषा दिन र program अनि software को फरक भन्न, प्रोग्रामिङ भाषाका तीन श्रेणी नाम लिई हरेकलाई कसले पढ्न सक्छ भन्न, high-level प्रोग्राम चल्नुअघि किन अनुवाद गर्नुपर्छ बुझाउन, वैज्ञानिक र व्यावसायिक प्रयोगका उदाहरण दिन, र सानो समस्याको algorithm लेखेर सही चिन्हसहित flowchart कोर्न सक्नुहुनेछ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.1 Program, programmer, programming language, software — प्रोग्राम, प्रोग्रामर, प्रोग्रामिङ भाषा, सफ्टवेयर
items.en: The difference that carries the mark. "Program and software are the same thing" is marked wrong. A program is one set of instructions for one job. Software is the package: the programs, the files they need, and the manual. If a question asks you to differentiate them, the word to reach for is scope — a program is a part, software is the whole.
items.ne: अंक बोक्ने फरक यही हो। "Program र software एउटै हो" भन्नु गलत मानिन्छ। Program एउटा कामका लागि एउटा निर्देशन समूह हो। Software चाहिँ पूरा प्याकेज हो: प्रोग्राम, तिनलाई चाहिने फाइल, र म्यानुअल। फरक सोधिए दायरा शब्द सम्झनुहोस् — program भाग हो, software सिङ्गो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.2 Categories of programming language — प्रोग्रामिङ भाषाका श्रेणी
items.en: Beyond the topic list, and needed from Unit 2 onwards. The curriculum's topic 1.2 names only the categories. The three translators are not on the list and you will meet all three in this subject, so learn them here: an assembler turns assembly into machine code; a compiler reads a whole high level program and produces an executable file before anything runs; an interpreter reads and runs one line at a time, so the program stops at the first bad line rather than refusing to start. C uses a compiler.
items.ne: विषयसूचीभन्दा बाहिर, तर युनिट २ देखि चाहिने। पाठ्यक्रमको विषय १.२ ले श्रेणी मात्र नाम लिन्छ। तीन अनुवादक सूचीमा छैनन् तर यस विषयमा तीनै भेटिन्छन्, त्यसैले यहीँ सिक्नुहोस्: assembler ले assembly लाई मेसिन कोड बनाउँछ; compiler ले पूरै high level प्रोग्राम पढेर चल्नुअघि नै executable फाइल बनाउँछ; interpreter ले एक–एक लाइन पढेर चलाउँछ, त्यसैले प्रोग्राम सुरु नै नहुने होइन, पहिलो गलत लाइनमा पुगेर रोकिन्छ। C ले compiler प्रयोग गर्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.2 Categories of programming language — प्रोग्रामिङ भाषाका श्रेणी
items.en: Option B is tempting and still wrong: an interpreted program travels as source too, and it needs the interpreter installed on the other machine before it runs. Nothing is portable without something being installed on the far side.
items.ne: Source portable हो, executable होइन। Portability को अर्थ उही .c फाइल हरेक मेसिनमा compile गर्दा उस्तै व्यवहार गर्छ भन्ने हो। .exe चाहिँ एउटा प्रोसेसर र एउटा operating system कै मेसिन कोड हो, त्यसैले त्यसलाई सार्नु गलत फाइल सार्नु हो। माथिको चित्रको व्यावहारिक अर्थ यही हो: compiler को बायाँ भएको सबै सर्छ, दायाँ भएको सर्दैन। विकल्प (ख) लोभलाग्दो छ तर गलत: interpret हुने प्रोग्राम पनि source कै रूपमा सर्छ, र अर्को मेसिनमा interpreter install भएपछि मात्र चल्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.4 Program design tools — algorithm and flowchart — प्रोग्राम डिजाइनका साधन — algorithm र flowchart
items.en: Write the steps out before opening this. Count how many arrows must leave your decision box, and check that every path reaches a Stop.
items.ne: खोल्नुअघि चरणहरू लेख्नुहोस्। Decision बाकसबाट कति तीर बाहिर जानुपर्छ गन्नुहोस्, र हरेक बाटो Stop सम्म पुग्छ कि पुग्दैन जाँच्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.4 Program design tools — algorithm and flowchart — प्रोग्राम डिजाइनका साधन — algorithm र flowchart
items.en: Three things are being marked here and only one of them is the comparison. Both branches are labelled yes and no; both branches end at the same Stop; and the printing boxes are parallelograms, not rectangles, because printing crosses the boundary to the person. Note also that the algorithm never says what happens when a and b are equal — it prints "b is larger", which is wrong. A complete answer would use three branches or say "a is not larger".
items.ne: यहाँ तीन कुराको अंक छ, र तीमध्ये एउटा मात्र तुलना हो। दुवै शाखामा yes र no लेखिएको छ; दुवै शाखा उही Stop मा पुग्छन्; र छाप्ने बाकस rectangle होइन parallelogram हुन्, किनभने छाप्नु मान्छेसम्मको सिमाना नाघ्नु हो। अर्को कुरा — a र b बराबर भए के हुन्छ algorithm ले भनेकै छैन; त्यसले "b is larger" छाप्छ, जुन गलत हो। पूरा उत्तरमा तीन शाखा हुन्थ्यो, वा "a is not larger" लेखिन्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.4 Program design tools — algorithm and flowchart — प्रोग्राम डिजाइनका साधन — algorithm र flowchart
items.en: Two variables are needed, not one. Decide what each holds and what its value must be before the repetition starts.
items.ne: एउटा होइन, दुई variable चाहिन्छ। हरेकले के राख्छ र दोहोरिन सुरु हुनुअघि त्यसको मान के हुनुपर्छ, निर्णय गर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.4 Program design tools — algorithm and flowchart — प्रोग्राम डिजाइनका साधन — algorithm र flowchart
items.en: Step 2 is where this goes wrong in real answers. If sum is not set to 0 first, step 4 adds to an unknown value; if i is not set to 1, the count starts nowhere. The loop ends because step 5 changes the thing step 3 tests — remove step 5 and the algorithm fails finiteness and runs forever.
items.ne: वास्तविक उत्तरमा चरण २ कै कारण बिग्रन्छ। sum लाई पहिले ० नराखे चरण ४ ले अज्ञात मानमा जोड्छ; i लाई १ नराखे गन्ती कतैबाट सुरु हुँदैन। Loop सकिनुको कारण चरण ५ ले चरण ३ ले जाँच्ने कुरै बदल्छ — चरण ५ हटाए algorithm finiteness मा असफल हुन्छ र सधैं चलिरहन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.4 Program design tools — algorithm and flowchart — प्रोग्राम डिजाइनका साधन — algorithm र flowchart
items.en: Forgetting to initialise before a loop. sum = 0 before the repetition begins, every time.
items.ne: Program र software एउटै भन्नु: program एउटा निर्देशन समूह, software चाहिँ program + data + documentation। Assembly लाई machine language भन्नु: assembly मा mnemonic हुन्छन् र assembler चाहिन्छ; machine language binary हो र केही चाहिँदैन। Read वा Print लाई rectangle कोर्नु: दुवै input/output हुन्, parallelogram। Decision का शाखामा नाम नलेख्नु: नाम नभएका दुई तीरले कुन बाटो कुन हो भन्दैनन्, र अंक नाम कै हो। Stop नभएको algorithm लेख्नु: finiteness पाँच गुणमध्ये एक हो। Loop अघि initialise बिर्सनु: दोहोरिन सुरु हुनुअघि sum = 0, सधैं।

It is the unit with the least C in it and the most definitions, so the questions are predictable: define the four terms; differentiate two of them; list the categories of language; and — the one worth the most — write an algorithm and draw a flowchart for a small problem. Practise drawing flowcharts on paper, because that is where they will be marked.

items.ne: Program भनेको निश्चित क्रममा लेखिएका निर्देशनको समूह हो, जसले कम्प्युटरलाई एउटा निश्चित काम कसरी गर्ने भन्छ। Software भनेको प्रोग्रामहरू, तिनले प्रयोग गर्ने data र तिनलाई बुझाउने documentation को समूह हो। फरक: program एउटा वस्तु हो; software पूरै प्याकेज। हरेक program software हो, तर software प्रायः धेरै program मिलेर बन्छ।

items.en: Machine and assembly together are called low level languages.
items.ne: १. Machine level — ० र १ मात्र; प्रोसेसरले सिधै चलाउँछ; छिटो, लेख्न गाह्रो, हरेक प्रोसेसरमा फरक। उदाहरण 10110000 01100001। २. Assembly level — MOV, ADD जस्ता mnemonic, मेसिन निर्देशनसँग एक–एक मिल्ने; assembler चाहिन्छ; प्रोसेसरसँग बाँधिएको। उदाहरण MOV AL, 61h। ३. High level — अङ्ग्रेजीजस्ता शब्द; पढ्न सजिलो, मेसिनबीच portable; compiler वा interpreter चाहिन्छ। उदाहरण C, C++, Java। Machine र assembly लाई सँगै low level भनिन्छ।

items.ne: Algorithm: चरण १ Start; चरण २ a, b, c पढ्नुहोस्; चरण ३ sum = a + b + c; चरण ४ avg = sum / 3; चरण ५ sum र avg छाप्नुहोस्; चरण ६ Stop। Flowchart: oval (Start) → parallelogram (Read a, b, c) → rectangle (sum) → rectangle (avg) → parallelogram (Print) → oval (Stop), तलतिरका तीरले जोडिएको। यस समस्यामा कुनै decision छैन, त्यसैले diamond र शाखा छैनन्। अंक सही चिन्ह सही क्रममा राखेको र चरण ३ अनि ४ लाई एउटै बाकसमा नमिसाएको हो — हरेक गणना आफ्नै process चरण हो।

items.ne: Program = एउटै कामका लागि क्रमबद्ध निर्देशन; software = program + data + documentation। तीन श्रेणी: machine (binary, अनुवाद नचाहिने), assembly (mnemonic, assembler), high level (अङ्ग्रेजीजस्तो, compiler वा interpreter)। Machine र assembly low level; C high level, जसलाई middle level पनि भनिन्छ। Source portable हुन्छ, compile भएको executable हुँदैन। वैज्ञानिक काम = थोरै data मा धेरै गणना; व्यावसायिक काम = धेरै data मा थोरै गणना। Algorithm finite, definite र effective हुनुपर्छ, र output दिनैपर्छ। Flowchart चिन्ह: oval terminal, parallelogram input/output, rectangle process, diamond decision, circle connector, तीर flow।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.1 Program, programmer, programming language, software — प्रोग्राम, प्रोग्रामर, प्रोग्रामिङ भाषा, सफ्टवेयर
items.en: Four words the examination asks for separately A program is a set of instructions, written in order, that tells a computer how to do one particular job. Two things are doing work in that sentence: instructions, and in order. The same four instructions in a different order are a different program, and usually a wrong one. A programmer is the person who writes it. Not the person who uses it, and not the person who installs it — the one who decides what the steps are and writes them down. A programming language is the notation the programmer writes in. It exists because the two sides cannot meet: a computer cannot read Nepali or English, and a person cannot comfortably write binary. The language is a meeting point with rules strict enough that a machine can translate it mechanically. Software is the wider word. It is the collection of programs, the data they work on, and the documentation that says how to use them. One program is software, but software is usually many programs — a browser is one program; an operating system is hundreds.
items.ne: परीक्षाले छुट्टाछुट्टै सोध्ने चार शब्द Program भनेको क्रमैसँग लेखिएका निर्देशनको समूह हो, जसले कम्प्युटरलाई कुनै एउटा काम कसरी गर्ने भन्छ। यो वाक्यमा दुई कुराले काम गरिरहेका छन्: निर्देशन, र क्रम। उही चार निर्देशन फरक क्रममा राखे फरक प्रोग्राम हुन्छ, र प्रायः गलत हुन्छ। Programmer भनेको त्यो लेख्ने मान्छे हो। प्रयोग गर्ने होइन, install गर्ने पनि होइन — चरण के–के हुन् भनेर निर्णय गरेर लेख्ने। Programming language भनेको प्रोग्रामरले लेख्ने लिपि हो। यो त्यसैले चाहिन्छ कि दुवै पक्ष आपसमा भेट्न सक्दैनन्: कम्प्युटरले नेपाली वा अङ्ग्रेजी पढ्न सक्दैन, र मान्छेले सजिलै binary लेख्न सक्दैन। भाषा बीचको भेटघाट हो, र यसका नियम मेसिनले यान्त्रिक रूपमै अनुवाद गर्न सक्ने गरी कडा हुन्छन्। Software फराकिलो शब्द हो। यो प्रोग्रामहरूको समूह, तिनले काम गर्ने data, र कसरी चलाउने भन्ने documentation मिलेर बन्छ। एउटा प्रोग्राम पनि software हो, तर software प्रायः धेरै प्रोग्राम हुन्छ — browser एउटा प्रोग्राम हो; operating system सयौं।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.2 Categories of programming language — प्रोग्रामिङ भाषाका श्रेणी
items.en: Three levels, and the question that sorts them Languages are classified by how close they are to the machine. The question that decides the category is: who can read this without help? Machine level language — 0s and 1s only. The processor reads it directly, with no translation of any kind. It is the fastest to run and almost impossible to write by hand, and it is different on every make of processor. Example: 10110000 01100001. Assembly level language — short codes called mnemonics that stand one-for-one for machine instructions: MOV, ADD, JMP. A person who knows the processor can read it. It needs an assembler to become machine code, and it is still tied to one processor. High level language — English-like words and ordinary arithmetic: C, C++, Java, Python. Anybody who has learnt the language can read it, the same source file works on different machines, and it needs a compiler or an interpreter. Machine and assembly together are called low level languages, because they are close to the hardware and far from the person. C is a high level language, though it is often called a middle level language as well, because it can reach down to memory addresses in a way that most high level languages cannot. That ability is Unit 7.
items.ne: तीन तह, र छुट्याउने प्रश्न भाषाको वर्गीकरण मेसिनसँग कति नजिक छ भन्ने आधारमा हुन्छ। श्रेणी निर्णय गर्ने प्रश्न यही हो: सहायताविना यो कसले पढ्न सक्छ? Machine level language — ० र १ मात्र। प्रोसेसरले कुनै अनुवादविनै सिधै पढ्छ। चल्न सबैभन्दा छिटो, हातले लेख्न झन्डै असम्भव, र हरेक बनोटको प्रोसेसरमा फरक। उदाहरण: 10110000 01100001। Assembly level language — mnemonic भनिने छोटा सङ्केत, जो एक–एक गरी मेसिन निर्देशनका ठाउँमा आउँछन्: MOV, ADD, JMP। प्रोसेसर जान्ने मान्छेले पढ्न सक्छ। मेसिन कोड बन्न assembler चाहिन्छ, र यो पनि एउटै प्रोसेसरसँग बाँधिएको हुन्छ। High level language — अङ्ग्रेजीजस्ता शब्द र सामान्य गणित: C, C++, Java, Python। भाषा सिकेको जोसुकैले पढ्न सक्छ, उही source फरक मेसिनमा चल्छ, र compiler वा interpreter चाहिन्छ। Machine र assembly लाई सँगै low level भाषा भनिन्छ, किनभने ती hardware सँग नजिक र मान्छेसँग टाढा छन्। C high level भाषा हो, तर यसलाई middle level पनि भनिन्छ — किनभने यसले धेरै high level भाषाले नसक्ने गरी मेमोरीको ठेगानासम्म पुग्न सक्छ। त्यो क्षमता युनिट ७ मा आउँछ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.3 Applications — scientific and business — प्रयोग — वैज्ञानिक र व्यावसायिक
items.en: Two kinds of job, and what each demands The syllabus names two application areas, and they are named together because they pull the machine in opposite directions. Scientific applications do a large amount of calculation on a small amount of data. Weather forecasting for the Kathmandu valley, earthquake modelling, satellite image processing, the engineering calculations behind a bridge. What they need is arithmetic speed and accuracy — many decimal places, many operations per second, and floating-point work that does not drift. Business applications do a small amount of calculation on a large amount of data. A bank's daily transactions, a school's result processing, payroll for a factory, the stock ledger of a shop. The arithmetic is addition and percentages; what they need is storage, sorting, searching and well-formatted reports — and absolute reliability, because an error here is somebody's salary. C is used for both, and it is used far more for a third kind the syllabus does not name: system programming. Operating systems, compilers and device drivers are written in C because of the memory control Unit 7 introduces.
items.ne: दुई किसिमका काम, र हरेकले माग्ने कुरा पाठ्यक्रमले दुई प्रयोग क्षेत्र नाम लिन्छ, र सँगै नाम लिनुको कारण यिनले मेसिनलाई उल्टो दिशामा तान्छन् भन्ने हो। वैज्ञानिक प्रयोग ले थोरै data मा धेरै गणना गर्छ। काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको मौसम पूर्वानुमान, भूकम्पको मोडेल, उपग्रह तस्बिरको प्रशोधन, पुल बनाउने इन्जिनियरिङ गणना। यिनलाई गणनाको गति र शुद्धता चाहिन्छ — धेरै दशमलव, प्रति सेकेन्ड धेरै क्रिया, र नबग्ने floating-point काम। व्यावसायिक प्रयोग ले धेरै data मा थोरै गणना गर्छ। बैंकको दैनिक कारोबार, विद्यालयको नतिजा, कारखानाको तलब, पसलको मौज्दात खाता। गणना भनेको जोड र प्रतिशत मात्र; यिनलाई भण्डारण, क्रम मिलाउने, खोज्ने र राम्ररी ढाँचा मिलेको प्रतिवेदन चाहिन्छ — र पूर्ण भरपर्दोपन, किनभने यहाँको त्रुटि कसैको तलब हो। C दुवैमा चल्छ, र पाठ्यक्रमले नाम नलिएको तेस्रो किसिममा झन् बढी: system programming। Operating system, compiler र device driver C मै लेखिन्छन्, किनभने युनिट ७ ले देखाउने मेमोरी नियन्त्रण यसमा छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 1.4 Program design tools — algorithm and flowchart — प्रोग्राम डिजाइनका साधन — algorithm र flowchart
items.en: The planning you do before any code An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step procedure for solving a problem, written in ordinary language. It is not C, and it does not have to be: its job is to get the method right while mistakes are still cheap to fix. Five properties are expected in an answer, and each one is a way an algorithm can be wrong: Finiteness — it must end after a limited number of steps. A procedure that never stops has not solved anything. Definiteness — every step must mean exactly one thing. "Add some numbers" is not a step. Input — zero or more values supplied at the start. Output — at least one result. An algorithm that produces nothing has no purpose. Effectiveness — every step must be simple enough to actually be carried out with paper and pencil. A flowchart is the same method drawn as a picture, using standard symbols joined by arrows. It shows the path through the steps, which is exactly what a list of sentences hides: a decision with two branches is one line of text and two visible arrows.
items.ne: कोड लेख्नुअघिको योजना Algorithm भनेको समस्या समाधान गर्ने सीमित, चरणबद्ध विधि हो, सामान्य भाषामा लेखिएको। यो C होइन, र हुनु पनि पर्दैन: गल्ती सच्याउन सस्तै हुँदा विधि ठिक बनाउनु यसको काम हो। उत्तरमा पाँच गुण खोजिन्छ, र हरेक गुण algorithm बिग्रने एउटा तरिका पनि हो: Finiteness — सीमित चरणपछि सकिनै पर्छ। कहिल्यै नरोकिने विधिले केही समाधान गरेको हुँदैन। Definiteness — हरेक चरणको ठ्याक्कै एउटै अर्थ हुनुपर्छ। "केही सङ्ख्या जोड्नुहोस्" चरण होइन। Input — सुरुमा शून्य वा बढी मान दिइन्छ। Output — कम्तीमा एउटा नतिजा। केही नदिने algorithm को प्रयोजन हुँदैन। Effectiveness — हरेक चरण कागज–कलमले साँच्चै गर्न सकिने गरी सरल हुनुपर्छ। Flowchart भनेको त्यही विधि चित्रमा कोरेको हो — मानक चिन्हहरू तीरले जोडेर। यसले चरणहरूबीचको बाटो देखाउँछ, जुन वाक्यहरूको सूचीले लुकाउँछ: दुई शाखा भएको decision पाठमा एक लाइन हो, चित्रमा दुई देखिने तीर।

The deciding question is always who can read it unaided — the processor, a person with a manual, or anybody who learnt the language. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: नाम होइन, नमुना हेरेर भाषा छुट्याउन। निर्णय गर्ने प्रश्न सधैं यही हो — सहायताविना कसले पढ्न सक्छ: प्रोसेसरले, म्यानुअल भएको मान्छेले, कि भाषा सिकेको जोसुकैले? How to use this Read the sample before the options. If you can see register names, it is assembly; if you can see only digits, it is machine; if you can read it as a sentence, it is high level. विकल्पभन्दा पहिले नमुना पढ्नुहोस्। Register का नाम देखिए assembly; अङ्क मात्र देखिए machine; वाक्यजस्तै पढ्न सकिए high level। Predict first

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् A program written in C is compiled on a Windows computer and the resulting .exe file is copied to a Linux computer. It refuses to run. Was the programmer wrong to call C portable? C मा लेखिएको प्रोग्राम Windows कम्प्युटरमा compile गरेर बनेको .exe फाइल Linux कम्प्युटरमा सारियो। त्यो चल्न मानेन। त्यसो भए C लाई portable भन्नु गलत थियो? Yes — C is not portable after all Yes — only interpreted languages are portable No — the SOURCE is portable; the compiled file never was The source is portable, not the executable. Portability means the same .c file can be compiled on each machine and will behave the same way. The .exe is machine code for one processor and one operating system, so copying it across is copying the wrong file. This is the practical meaning of the diagram above. Everything to the left of the compiler travels; everything to the right of it does not. Option B is tempting and still wrong: an interpreted program travels as source too, and it needs the interpreter installed on the other machine before it runs. Nothing is portable without something being installed on the far side. Source portable हो, executable होइन। Portability को अर्थ उही .c फाइल हरेक मेसिनमा compile गर्दा उस्तै व्यवहार गर्छ भन्ने हो। .exe चाहिँ एउटा प्रोसेसर र एउटा operating system कै मेसिन कोड हो, त्यसैले त्यसलाई सार्नु गलत फाइल सार्नु हो। माथिको चित्रको व्यावहारिक अर्थ यही हो: compiler को बायाँ भएको सबै सर्छ, दायाँ भएको सर्दैन। विकल्प (ख) लोभलाग्दो छ तर गलत: interpret हुने प्रोग्राम पनि source कै रूपमा सर्छ, र अर्को मेसिनमा interpreter install भएपछि मात्र चल्छ। 1.3 Applications — scientific and business

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Which flowchart symbol does this step need? What you will learn: to pick the shape from the kind of step rather than from the words in it. Input and output share one symbol; calculation has its own; a question has two arrows out. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: शब्द होइन, चरणको किसिम हेरेर आकार छान्न। Input र output को एउटै चिन्ह हुन्छ; गणनाको आफ्नै; प्रश्नबाट दुई तीर बाहिर जान्छन्। How to use this Ask one question per case: does anything leave or enter the program here? If yes it is a parallelogram. If it is a question with a yes and a no, it is a diamond. Otherwise it is almost always a rectangle. हरेक केसमा एउटा प्रश्न सोध्नुहोस्: यहाँ प्रोग्रामबाट केही बाहिर जान्छ वा भित्र आउँछ? भए parallelogram। हो–होइन भएको प्रश्न भए diamond। नत्र झन्डै सधैं rectangle। Mistakes that cost marks here Saying a program and software are the same. A program is one set of instructions; software is programs plus data plus documentation. Calling assembly language "machine language". Assembly uses mnemonics and needs an assembler. Machine language is binary and needs nothing. Drawing a rectangle for Read or Print. Both are input/output and both take the parallelogram. Leaving a decision branch unlabelled. A diamond with two unmarked arrows does not say which path is which, and the marks are for the labels. Writing an algorithm with no Stop. Finiteness is one of the five properties, and it is the one tested by leaving it out. Forgetting to initialise before a loop. sum = 0 before the repetition begins, every time. Program र software एउटै भन्नु: program एउटा निर्देशन समूह, software चाहिँ program + data + documentation। Assembly लाई machine language भन्नु: assembly मा mnemonic हुन्छन् र assembler चाहिन्छ; machine language binary हो र केही चाहिँदैन। Read वा Print लाई rectangle कोर्नु: दुवै input/output हुन्, parallelogram। Decision का शाखामा नाम नलेख्नु: नाम नभएका दुई तीरले कुन बाटो कुन हो भन्दैनन्, र अंक नाम कै हो। Stop नभएको algorithm लेख्नु: finiteness पाँच गुणमध्ये एक हो। Loop अघि initialise बिर्सनु: दोहोरिन सुरु हुनुअघि sum = 0, सधैं। Memory hook — Oval starts, slanted talks, box works, diamond asks. Four shapes, four jobs. सम्झने तरिका — Oval सुरु, छड्के बोल्छ, बाकस काम गर्छ, diamond सोध्छ। Practical work — this unit's other 2 hours

"float" is a keyword, so the compiler could not tell which meaning you intended. "_total2" begins with an underscore, contains only letters, digits and underscores, and is not a keyword, so it is valid.

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: C was developed by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Laboratories in 1972, and UNIX was rewritten in it. That origin explains the language: an operating system needs direct access to memory and almost no overhead, which is why C has pointers and why it stays fast. Bjarne Stroustrup developed C++ from C, which is a different language and a later one.
items.ne: C लाई Dennis Ritchie ले Bell Laboratories मा १९७२ मा विकास गरे, र UNIX त्यसैमा फेरि लेखियो। त्यही उत्पत्तिले भाषा बुझाउँछ: operating system लाई मेमोरीमा सिधै पहुँच र झन्डै शून्य थप भार चाहिन्छ — त्यसैले C मा pointer छन् र यो छिटो रहन्छ। Bjarne Stroustrup ले C बाट C++ बनाए, जुन फरक र पछिको भाषा हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: An escape sequence is a backslash and a letter that together stand for one character that cannot be typed directly. \n is the newline character: two characters in the source file, one invisible character in the output. \t is the tab, which is why option D is wrong. Without \n, two printf calls run their text together on the same line.
items.ne: Escape sequence भनेको backslash र एउटा अक्षर मिलेर सिधै टाइप गर्न नमिल्ने एउटा अक्षर जनाउने कुरा हो। \n newline अक्षर हो: source फाइलमा दुई अक्षर, output मा एउटा नदेखिने अक्षर। Tab चाहिँ \t हो, त्यसैले विकल्प (घ) गलत छ। \n नभए दुई printf को पाठ उही लाइनमा जोडिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: The semicolon is a statement terminator, so it belongs after every statement — a declaration, an assignment, a return. #include is not a statement at all: it is a preprocessor directive, handled before compiling begins, and it ends at the end of the line. A function heading and a closing brace are the other two places where no semicolon belongs.
items.ne: Semicolon statement terminator हो, त्यसैले हरेक statement पछि आउँछ — घोषणा, assignment, return। #include statement नै होइन: यो preprocessor directive हो, compile सुरु हुनुअघि नै चल्छ, र लाइनकै अन्त्यमा सकिन्छ। Function को शीर्षक र बन्द गर्ने brace अरू दुई ठाउँ हुन् जहाँ semicolon चाहिँदैन।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Single quotes make a character constant, which occupies exactly one byte and is printed with %c. Double quotes make a string constant, which is an array of characters ending in the invisible null character \0 — so even a one-letter string takes two bytes and is printed with %s. This is the difference that becomes the whole of Unit 5.
items.ne: एकल उद्धरणले character constant बनाउँछ, जुन ठ्याक्कै एक byte ओगट्छ र %c ले छापिन्छ। दोहोरो उद्धरणले string constant बनाउँछ, जुन नदेखिने null अक्षर \0 ले सकिने character को array हो — त्यसैले एक अक्षरको string ले पनि दुई byte लिन्छ र %s ले छापिन्छ। यही फरक युनिट ५ को पूरै कुरा बन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Arguments in C are passed by value, so a function receives copies. printf only needs to look at the value, and a copy is enough. scanf has to change n, and it cannot change a copy — it needs the address, which is what & supplies. This is call by reference meeting you in Unit 2, four units before it is named.
items.ne: C मा argument value बाट पठाइन्छन्, त्यसैले function ले प्रतिलिपि पाउँछ। printf लाई मान हेर्नु मात्र भएकाले प्रतिलिपि पुग्छ। scanf ले n बदल्नुपर्छ, र प्रतिलिपि बदल्न सक्दैन — ठेगाना चाहिन्छ, र & ले त्यही दिन्छ। नाम लिनुभन्दा चार युनिट अघि नै युनिट २ मा भेटिने call by reference यही हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: * and % have the same precedence, which is higher than +, and they associate left to right. So 4 * 2 is worked out first giving 8, then 8 % 3 gives the remainder 2, then 10 + 2 gives 12. Reading the line left to right like a sentence would give 14 * 2 = 28, then 28 % 3 = 1, which is option B and is how this question is usually got wrong.
items.ne: * र % को precedence उस्तै छ, + भन्दा माथि, र यी बायाँबाट दायाँ जान्छन्। त्यसैले पहिले 4 * 2 = 8, अनि 8 % 3 को शेष 2, अनि 10 + 2 = 12। वाक्यजस्तै बायाँबाट दायाँ पढे 14 * 2 = 28, अनि 28 % 3 = 1 आउँथ्यो — त्यो विकल्प (ख) हो र यो प्रश्न प्रायः त्यसरी नै बिग्रन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: 7 and 2 are both integers, so the division is integer division and the remainder is discarded before anything is stored: the result is 3, not 3.5 and not rounded to 4. Storing 3 in a float gives 3.0, and that is what prints. The variable being a float does not help, because the division finished before the float was involved. Writing 7.0 / 2 or (float) 7 / 2 gives 3.5.
items.ne: 7 र 2 दुवै integer भएकाले भाग integer division हो र केही भण्डारण हुनुअघि नै शेष फालिन्छ: नतिजा 3 हो — 3.5 पनि होइन, round गरेर 4 पनि होइन। 3 लाई float मा राख्दा 3.0 हुन्छ र त्यही छापिन्छ। Variable float हुनुले सहयोग गर्दैन, किनभने float बीचमा आउनुअघि नै भाग सकियो। 7.0 / 2 वा (float) 7 / 2 लेखे 3.5 आउँछ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: i++ is the POST-increment: the old value of i is used in the expression first, and only then is i increased. So j receives 5 and i becomes 6. Writing j = ++i instead would increase i first and give j the new value, making both 6. On a line of its own, i++ and ++i do exactly the same thing, which is why the difference only shows up when the value is being used.
items.ne: i++ POST-increment हो: पहिले expression मा i को पुरानो मान प्रयोग हुन्छ, अनि मात्र i बढ्छ। त्यसैले j ले 5 पाउँछ र i 6 हुन्छ। बरु j = ++i लेखे पहिले i बढेर j ले नयाँ मान पाउँथ्यो र दुवै 6 हुन्थे। एक्लै लाइनमा i++ र ++i ले ठ्याक्कै उही काम गर्छन् — त्यसैले फरक मान प्रयोग हुँदा मात्र देखिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Which format specifier does this need?
items.ne: यसलाई कुन format specifier चाहिन्छ?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: printf and scanf do not inspect the variable — they believe the specifier. Choose the one that matches the type. Getting this wrong does not usually stop the program: it prints something, and the something is wrong.
items.ne: printf र scanf ले variable जाँच्दैनन् — specifier लाई नै पत्याउँछन्। प्रकारसँग मिल्ने छान्नुहोस्। यो गलत हुँदा प्रायः प्रोग्राम रोकिँदैन: केही छाप्छ, र त्यो केही गलत हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Which family does this operator belong to?
items.ne: यो operator कुन परिवारको हो?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: The syllabus names five families and the examination asks you to classify, not just to use. Look at what the operator PRODUCES: a number, a true-or-false, a stored value, or a changed bit pattern.
items.ne: पाठ्यक्रमले पाँच परिवारको नाम लिन्छ र परीक्षाले प्रयोग मात्र होइन वर्गीकरण सोध्छ। Operator ले के निकाल्छ हेर्नुहोस्: सङ्ख्या, सत्य–असत्य, भण्डारण भएको मान, कि बदलिएको bit बनोट?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: An int is printed with %d, where the d stands for decimal integer. This is the specifier used more often than all the others together, and it is the one to reach for whenever a whole number is being shown.
items.ne: int लाई %d ले छापिन्छ, जहाँ d को अर्थ decimal integer हो। अरू सबै मिलेर जतिभन्दा पनि यही बढी प्रयोग हुन्छ, र पूर्ण सङ्ख्या देखाउँदा सधैं यही सम्झनुपर्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A float needs %f, and by default it prints six digits after the point — 5.400000, not 5.4. Writing %.2f asks for two, which is how a neat answer is produced in an examination program.
items.ne: float लाई %f चाहिन्छ, र पूर्वनिर्धारित रूपमा दशमलवपछि छ अङ्क छाप्छ — 5.400000, 5.4 होइन। %.2f लेखे दुई अङ्क आउँछ, र परीक्षाको प्रोग्राममा सफा उत्तर यसरी निकालिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A single character variable takes %c. Using %d here would print 65 instead of A, because that is the code number stored for the letter, and the program would still compile without any complaint.
items.ne: एउटै अक्षरको variable लाई %c। यहाँ %d प्रयोग गरे A का साटो 65 छाप्छ, किनभने अक्षरका लागि भण्डारण गरिएको सङ्ख्या त्यही हो — र प्रोग्राम कुनै गुनासोविना compile पनि हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A string is a character array and takes %s, which keeps printing until it meets the null character. %c would print only the first letter, because it expects one character and not an array.
items.ne: String character array हो र यसलाई %s चाहिन्छ, जसले null अक्षर नभेटेसम्म छापिरहन्छ। %c ले पहिलो अक्षर मात्र छाप्थ्यो, किनभने त्यसले array होइन एउटै अक्षर खोज्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: scanf uses the same specifiers as printf, so reading an integer is %d. The difference is the ampersand on the variable: scanf needs the address of n, because it has to put the value somewhere.
items.ne: scanf ले printf कै specifier प्रयोग गर्छ, त्यसैले पूर्णाङ्क पढ्न %d। फरक variable अगाडिको ampersand हो: scanf लाई n को ठेगाना चाहिन्छ, किनभने मान कतै राख्नुपर्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: The modulus operator gives the remainder after division, which is a number, so it is arithmetic. It works only on integers in C, and it is the standard way a program decides whether a number is even.
items.ne: Modulus ले भाग गरेपछिको शेष दिन्छ, र त्यो सङ्ख्या हो — त्यसैले arithmetic। C मा यो पूर्णाङ्कमा मात्र चल्छ, र सङ्ख्या जोर छ कि छैन भन्ने निर्णय प्रोग्रामले यसैले गर्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A comparison answers a question with true or false rather than producing a value, which makes it relational. The doubled equals sign is the one that compares; a single one would assign and change a.
items.ne: तुलना गर्दा मान होइन सत्य वा असत्य निस्कन्छ, त्यसैले यो relational हो। दोहोरो बराबर चिन्हले तुलना गर्छ; एउटै भए assign भएर a नै बदलिन्थ्यो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: The double ampersand joins two conditions that are each already true or false, which is what a logical operator does. The two comparisons inside it are relational; the operator combining them is not.
items.ne: दोहोरो ampersand ले सत्य–असत्य भइसकेका दुई सर्त जोड्छ, र logical operator ले गर्ने काम त्यही हो। भित्रका दुई तुलना relational हुन्; तिनलाई जोड्ने operator चाहिँ होइन।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A single ampersand works on each bit of the number separately rather than on the number as a whole. Here it keeps only the last bit, which is a quick way of testing whether x is odd.
items.ne: एउटै ampersand ले सङ्ख्यालाई सिङ्गो नभई हरेक bit लाई छुट्टाछुट्टै हेर्छ। यहाँ यसले अन्तिम bit मात्र राख्छ, र x बिजोर छ कि छैन जाँच्ने छिटो तरिका त्यही हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A compound assignment stores a value into the variable on the left, and that storing is what makes it assignment. It is shorthand for total = total + marks and does exactly the same thing.
items.ne: Compound assignment ले बायाँको variable मा मान राख्छ, र त्यही राख्ने कामले यसलाई assignment बनाउँछ। यो total = total + marks कै छोटो रूप हो र ठ्याक्कै उही काम गर्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Classify any C operator into one of the five families and work out what an expression evaluates to.
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा: सही header, main() र return सहितको पूरा C प्रोग्राम लेख्न, प्रोग्रामका भाग — preprocessor directive, header file, token, comment, identifier, escape sequence — नाम लिन, मान्य identifier का नियम र keyword किन identifier हुन सक्दैन भन्न, मानका लागि data type र त्यसलाई छाप्ने format specifier छान्न, scanf ले मान पढ्न र ampersand किन चाहिन्छ भन्न, अनि जुनसुकै C operator लाई पाँच परिवारमध्ये एकमा राखेर expression को मान निकाल्न सक्नुहुनेछ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 2.3 Variables and keywords — Variable र keyword
items.en: Legal or not? Check the four rules in order. 2marks starts with a digit — illegal. total marks has a space — illegal. float is a keyword — illegal. roll-no contains a hyphen, which C reads as minus — illegal. _total, total2, Total_Marks and a are all legal. A legal name can still be a bad one: a tells a reader nothing.
items.ne: मान्य हो कि होइन? चारै नियम क्रमैसँग जाँच्नुहोस्। 2marks अङ्कबाट सुरु — अमान्य। total marks मा खाली ठाउँ — अमान्य। float keyword — अमान्य। roll-no मा hyphen छ, जसलाई C ले घटाउ पढ्छ — अमान्य। _total, total2, Total_Marks र a सबै मान्य। मान्य नाम पनि नराम्रो हुन सक्छ: a ले पाठकलाई केही भन्दैन।
