items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A union is DECLARED exactly like a structure — only the keyword differs. That similarity is why the two are confused and why the examination asks you to differentiate them.
items.ne: Union को घोषणा structure कै जस्तो हुन्छ — keyword मात्र फरक। त्यही मिल्दोपनले दुईलाई अलमल्याउँछ, र परीक्षाले फरक सोध्नुको कारण पनि त्यही हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: b is created. A structure with these members would reserve space for BOTH; a union reserves one block, big enough for the largest member, and that is the whole saving.
items.ne: b बन्यो। यी member भएको structure ले दुवैका लागि ठाउँ छुट्याउँथ्यो; union ले सबैभन्दा ठूलो member अट्ने एउटै block छुट्याउँछ, र पूरै बचत त्यही हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Writing 65 into b.n fills the shared block. b.c is now reading the same bytes as a character, and 65 is the code for the letter A — nobody asked for that, it simply follows.
items.ne: b.n मा 65 लेख्दा साझा block भरिन्छ। b.c ले अब उही byte लाई अक्षरका रूपमा पढ्छ, र 65 भनेको A अक्षरको सङ्केत हो — कसैले मागेको होइन, आफैं हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Reading back the member that was last written gives the expected answer. A union is perfectly reliable as long as you read the member you wrote.
items.ne: अन्तिम पटक लेखिएकै member पढ्दा अपेक्षित उत्तर आउँछ। लेखेकै member पढ्ने हो भने union पूरै भरपर्दो हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Now X is written into b.c. X has the code 88, and it goes into the SAME block — so b.n has just been changed by a line that never mentioned n.
items.ne: अब b.c मा X लेखियो। X को सङ्केत 88 हो, र त्यो उही block मा जान्छ — त्यसैले n को नाम नै नलिएको लाइनले b.n बदलिदियो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: b.c is read and gives X, as expected.
items.ne: b.c पढ्दा अपेक्षाअनुसार X आउँछ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: And b.n is now 88, not 65. The first value is gone. In a STRUCTURE both members would still hold their own values, and that single difference is the answer to the standard comparison question.
items.ne: अनि b.n अब 88 छ, 65 होइन। पहिलो मान गयो। STRUCTURE मा दुवै member का आफ्नै मान रहन्थे, र मानक तुलनात्मक प्रश्नको उत्तर त्यही एउटा फरक हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Write the scanf lines before opening this. One of the three members takes no ampersand — decide which, and why. खोल्नुअघि scanf का लाइन लेख्नुहोस्। तीनमध्ये एउटा member लाई ampersand चाहिँदैन — कुन र किन, निर्णय गर्नुहोस्। Working #include <stdio.h> struct Student /* 1. the blueprint — no memory used yet */ { char name[20]; int roll; float percent; }; /* the semicolon here is compulsory */ int main() { struct Student s1; /* 2. NOW memory is reserved */ printf("Name : "); scanf("%s", s1.name); /* no & — an array name is an address */ printf("Roll : "); scanf("%d", &s1.roll); /* & — roll is an ordinary int */ printf("Percent: "); scanf("%f", &s1.percent); printf("\n%s has roll %d and scored %.2f%%", s1.name, s1.roll, s1.percent); return 0; } Output (if the user types Sita, 15 and 82.5) Name : Sita Roll : 15 Percent: 82.5 Sita has roll 15 and scored 82.50% Three things are being marked. The semicolon after the closing brace. The word struct in front of Student s1. And the dot operator: s1.roll means "the roll member of the variable s1", and the dot joins a variable to a member — never a type to a member, because Student.roll names no memory. Note also %% at the end: a single % would be read as the start of a specifier. तीन कुराको अंक छ। बन्द brace पछिको semicolon। Student s1 अगाडिको struct शब्द। अनि dot operator: s1.roll को अर्थ "s1 variable को roll member" हो, र dot ले variable लाई member सँग जोड्छ — प्रकारलाई कहिल्यै होइन, किनभने Student.roll ले कुनै मेमोरी जनाउँदैन। अन्त्यको %% पनि हेर्नुहोस्: एउटै % लाई specifier को सुरु पढिन्थ्यो। 6.4 Introduction to union

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Step through it
items.ne: · चरणबद्ध हेर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: · चरणबद्ध हेर्नुहोस् Writing one member changes the other What you will learn: that a line naming only b.c changes what b.n reads back. Watch the shared-memory row: it has one value, and both members are simply two ways of reading it. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: b.c को मात्र नाम लिने लाइनले b.n ले पढ्ने कुरा बदल्छ। साझा मेमोरीको पङ्क्ति हेर्नुहोस्: त्यहाँ एउटै मान छ, र दुवै member त्यसलाई पढ्ने दुई तरिका मात्र हुन्। How to use this Before the last step, predict what b.n will print. Almost everybody says 65, because that is what was put there — and no line since has mentioned n. अन्तिम चरणअघि b.n ले के छाप्छ अनुमान गर्नुहोस्। झन्डै सबैले ६५ भन्छन्, किनभने त्यहाँ राखिएको त्यही थियो — र त्यसपछि कुनै लाइनले n को नाम लिएकै छैन। 6.5 and 6.6 — declaring and accessing Both work exactly as they do for a structure, and that is the point worth stating plainly: union Box b; declares the variable, and b.n reaches a member with the same dot operator. Nothing in the syntax distinguishes a union from a structure anywhere in a program — not the declaration, not the variable, not the access. The only difference is what the memory does, which is why the diagram above is the whole topic. One practical rule follows from it: read back the member you wrote last. Writing b.n and then reading b.c is not an error the compiler will stop, and the value you get is the same bytes interpreted as a different type. ६.५ र ६.६ — घोषणा र पहुँच दुवै structure मा जस्तै ठ्याक्कै उसरी नै चल्छन्, र स्पष्ट भन्नुपर्ने कुरा त्यही हो: union Box b; ले variable घोषणा गर्छ, र b.n ले उही dot operator ले member मा पुग्छ। प्रोग्रामको कुनै ठाउँमा syntax ले union लाई structure बाट छुट्याउँदैन — न घोषणाले, न variable ले, न पहुँचले। फरक मेमोरीले के गर्छ भन्नेमा मात्र छ, र त्यसैले माथिको चित्र नै पूरै विषय हो। यसबाट एउटा व्यावहारिक नियम निस्कन्छ: अन्तिम पटक लेखेकै member पढ्नुहोस्। b.n लेखेर b.c पढ्नु compiler ले रोक्ने त्रुटि होइन, र आउने मान उही byte लाई फरक प्रकारका रूपमा पढेको नतिजा हो। Practise the judgement
items.ne: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Structure or union? What you will learn: to choose between them from what the program needs, which is the form the examination question takes. The deciding question is whether more than one member must hold a value at the same time. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: प्रोग्रामलाई के चाहिन्छ हेरेर दुईमध्ये छान्न — परीक्षाको प्रश्न यही रूपमा आउँछ। निर्णय गर्ने प्रश्न यही हो: एकैचोटि एकभन्दा बढी member सँग मान हुनुपर्छ कि पर्दैन? How to use this Two clues give a union away every time: a size equal to the largest member rather than the total, and a member going strange after a different member was written. दुई सुराकले union सधैं चिनाउँछन्: आकार जोड नभई सबैभन्दा ठूलो member बराबर हुनु, र अर्को member लेखेपछि एउटा member अनौठो हुनु। Predict first
items.ne: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् For { int n; char c; float f; } with int 4 bytes, char 1 and float 4, what is sizeof for the structure and for the union? int ४ byte, char १ र float ४ हुँदा { int n; char c; float f; } को structure र union को sizeof कति हुन्छ? Structure 4, union 9 Structure at least 9, union 4 Both 9 The structure is at least 9 and the union is 4. A structure gives every member its own memory, so its size is the total: 4 + 1 + 4 = 9. A union gives them one shared block, so its size is the largest member: 4. "At least" 9 rather than exactly 9, and this is worth knowing. Compilers insert unused bytes called padding so that each member starts at an address its type likes, so a real machine will often report 12 rather than 9. The rule is the total; the measurement may be larger. Saying "the sum of the members" is the expected examination answer, and measuring it yourself with sizeof in the practical is how you meet padding. Option A is the two answers swapped, which is the usual way this is got wrong. Structure कम्तीमा ९, union ४। Structure ले हरेक member लाई आफ्नै मेमोरी दिन्छ, त्यसैले आकार जोड हुन्छ: 4 + 1 + 4 = 9। Union ले एउटै साझा block दिन्छ, त्यसैले आकार सबैभन्दा ठूलो member बराबर — ४। ठ्याक्कै ९ नभई "कम्तीमा" ९ भनिनुको कारण पनि जान्नु राम्रो: हरेक member लाई उसको प्रकारले मन पराउने ठेगानाबाट सुरु गराउन compiler ले padding भनिने प्रयोगविहीन byte थप्छ, त्यसैले वास्तविक मेसिनले प्रायः ९ होइन १२ भन्छ। नियम जोड हो; नाप ठूलो हुन सक्छ। परीक्षाले खोज्ने उत्तर "member को जोड" हो, र padding सँग भेट प्रयोगात्मक कक्षामा sizeof आफैं नापेर हुन्छ। विकल्प (क) मा दुई उत्तर साटिएका छन्, र यो प्रायः त्यसरी नै बिग्रन्छ। Example 2 Five students in one array of structures Question: hold the records of five students and print them all. This is what the structure was for. Decide how s[i].roll is read before opening this. Which part is the index and which part is the member? खोल्नुअघि s[i].roll कसरी पढिन्छ निर्णय गर्नुहोस्। कुन भाग index हो र कुन भाग member? Working #include <stdio.h> struct Student { char name[20]; int roll; }; int main() { struct Student s[5]; /* FIVE complete records */ int i; for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) { printf("Student %d name and roll: ", i + 1); scanf("%s %d", s[i].name, &s[i].roll); } for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) printf("%d - %s\n", s[i].roll, s[i].name); return 0; } s[i].roll reads left to right: take element i of the array, then take its roll member. The index comes first because the array is of structures, not a structure of arrays. Note the two scanf arguments: s[i].name is a char array and takes no ampersand, &s[i].roll is an int and does — the same rule as always, applied inside a structure. Without the structure, five students would need two separate arrays kept in step with each other by hand. s[i].roll बायाँबाट दायाँ पढिन्छ: array को i औं element लिने, अनि त्यसको roll member। Index पहिले आउँछ, किनभने यो structure हरूको array हो, array हरूको structure होइन। scanf का दुई argument हेर्नुहोस्: s[i].name char array हो र ampersand लिँदैन, &s[i].roll int हो र लिन्छ — उही पुरानो नियम, structure भित्र लागू भएको। Structure नभए पाँच विद्यार्थीका लागि दुई छुट्टाछुट्टै array हातैले मिलाएर राख्नुपर्थ्यो। Mistakes that cost marks here Forgetting the semicolon after the closing brace. A structure declaration is a statement; a function definition is not. Writing Student s1; without struct. In C the keyword is part of the type name. Using the dot on the type instead of a variable. Student.roll names no memory; s1.roll does. Saying a union's size is the total of its members. It is the size of the largest one. Expecting both union members to keep their values. Only the one written last is meaningful. Putting & before a char array member in scanf. s1.name is already an address; &s1.roll is not. बन्द brace पछि semicolon बिर्सनु: structure को घोषणा statement हो; function definition होइन। struct बिना Student s1; लेख्नु: C मा त्यो keyword प्रकारकै नामको भाग हो। Variable होइन प्रकारमा dot लगाउनु: Student.roll ले कुनै मेमोरी जनाउँदैन, s1.roll ले जनाउँछ। Union को आकार member को जोड भन्नु: त्यो सबैभन्दा ठूलो member को आकार हो। Union का दुवै member ले आफ्नो मान राख्छन् भन्ठान्नु: अन्तिम लेखिएको मात्र अर्थपूर्ण हुन्छ। scanf मा char array member अगाडि & राख्नु: s1.name आफैं ठेगाना हो; &s1.roll होइन। Memory hook — Structure: everyone gets a room. Union: everyone shares one room. Size is the total, or the largest. सम्झने तरिका — Structure: सबैलाई आ–आफ्नो कोठा। Union: सबैले एउटै कोठा बाँड्ने। आकार जोड, कि सबैभन्दा ठूलो। Practical work — this unit's other 7 hours
items.ne: — प्रयोगात्मक काम — यस युनिटका अरू ७ घण्टा

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 6.4 Introduction to union — Union को परिचय
items.en: What you will learn: that a line naming only b.c changes what b.n reads back. Watch the shared-memory row: it has one value, and both members are simply two ways of reading it.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: b.c को मात्र नाम लिने लाइनले b.n ले पढ्ने कुरा बदल्छ। साझा मेमोरीको पङ्क्ति हेर्नुहोस्: त्यहाँ एउटै मान छ, र दुवै member त्यसलाई पढ्ने दुई तरिका मात्र हुन्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 6.4 Introduction to union — Union को परिचय
items.en: What you will learn: to choose between them from what the program needs, which is the form the examination question takes. The deciding question is whether more than one member must hold a value at the same time.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: प्रोग्रामलाई के चाहिन्छ हेरेर दुईमध्ये छान्न — परीक्षाको प्रश्न यही रूपमा आउँछ। निर्णय गर्ने प्रश्न यही हो: एकैचोटि एकभन्दा बढी member सँग मान हुनुपर्छ कि पर्दैन?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A pointer is an ordinary variable in every respect — it has a type, a name and an address of its own — and what it holds is a location rather than a quantity. int *p; p = &n; leaves p holding where n lives, not what n contains. *p is how you reach the value from there, and the two must not be confused: p is an address and *p is the number at it.
items.ne: Pointer हरेक हिसाबले सामान्य variable नै हो — यसको प्रकार, नाम र आफ्नै ठेगाना हुन्छ — र यसले राख्ने कुरा परिमाण नभई स्थान हो। int *p; p = &n; पछि p सँग n कहाँ बस्छ भन्ने हुन्छ, n मा के छ भन्ने होइन। त्यहाँबाट मानसम्म पुग्ने तरिका *p हो, र यी दुई मिसाउनु हुँदैन: p ठेगाना हो र *p त्यहाँको सङ्ख्या।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: & is the address-of operator: written before a variable, it gives where that variable lives. * is the value-at, or dereference, operator: written before a pointer, it gives what is stored at the address the pointer holds. They work in opposite directions and undo each other, so *(&n) is simply n. Option A is the two definitions swapped, which is the usual way this is got wrong.
items.ne: & address-of operator हो: variable अगाडि लेख्दा त्यो variable कहाँ बस्छ भन्ने दिन्छ। * value-at वा dereference operator हो: pointer अगाडि लेख्दा pointer ले बोकेको ठेगानामा भएको कुरा दिन्छ। यी उल्टा दिशामा चल्छन् र एकअर्कालाई उल्ट्याउँछन्, त्यसैले *(&n) भनेको n नै हो। विकल्प (क) मा दुई परिभाषा साटिएका छन्, र यो प्रायः त्यसरी नै बिग्रन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Read *p = *p + 3 as "the value at p becomes the value at p plus three". The value at p is n, so this line is n = n + 3 written another way, and n becomes 10. A variable can be changed by a line that never names it, provided something holds its address — which is not a trick but exactly what scanf("%d", &n) has been doing since Unit 2. Printing p rather than n would show an address; one star is the whole difference.
items.ne: *p = *p + 3 लाई "p को ठेगानाको मान बराबर p को ठेगानाको मान जोड तीन" भनेर पढ्नुहोस्। P को ठेगानाको मान n हो, त्यसैले यो लाइन n = n + 3 कै अर्को लेखाइ हो र n १० हुन्छ। कसैसँग ठेगाना छ भने नाम नै नलिने लाइनले variable बदल्न सक्छ — यो जादू होइन, युनिट २ देखि scanf("%d", &n) ले गरिरहेकै काम हो। n होइन p छापेको भए ठेगाना देखिन्थ्यो; पूरै फरक एउटा star को हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: int *p; declares p as a pointer to an int — the star there is part of the type, not a dereference. p = &n; then stores n's address in it. Option C declares the pointer correctly and then puts a VALUE where an address belongs. Option A declares an ordinary int, and option D declares an ordinary int and then dereferences it, which is not something the compiler will accept.
items.ne: int *p; ले p लाई int को pointer घोषणा गर्छ — त्यहाँको star प्रकारको भाग हो, dereference होइन। अनि p = &n; ले यसमा n को ठेगाना राख्छ। विकल्प (ग) ले pointer त ठिकै घोषणा गर्छ तर ठेगाना चाहिने ठाउँमा मान राख्छ। विकल्प (क) ले सामान्य int घोषणा गर्छ, र (घ) ले सामान्य int घोषणा गरेर त्यसलाई dereference गर्छ, जुन compiler ले स्वीकार गर्दैन।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Call by reference is the advantage this subject has already relied on twice: the ampersand in every scanf since Unit 2, and the swap function in Unit 4. The other advantages are passing an array without copying it, allocating memory while the program runs, and building data structures such as linked lists. Option D is the opposite of the truth — C checks no bounds at all, which is part of the same bargain that makes pointers powerful.
items.ne: Call by reference यस विषयले पहिल्यै दुई पटक भर परेको फाइदा हो: युनिट २ देखि हरेक scanf को ampersand, र युनिट ४ को swap function। अरू फाइदा हुन् — प्रतिलिपि नबनाई array पठाउनु, प्रोग्राम चल्दै गर्दा मेमोरी छुट्याउनु, र linked list जस्ता data structure बनाउनु। विकल्प (घ) सत्यको ठिक उल्टो हो — C ले bound जाँच्दै जाँच्दैन, र pointer लाई शक्तिशाली बनाउने सम्झौताकै भाग त्यो हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Which pointer operator is needed here?
items.ne: यहाँ कुन pointer operator चाहिन्छ?

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Two operators, opposite directions. The ampersand takes an address out of a variable; the star takes a value out of an address. Decide which direction the line is travelling.
items.ne: दुई operator, उल्टा दिशा। Ampersand ले variable बाट ठेगाना निकाल्छ; star ले ठेगानाबाट मान निकाल्छ। लाइन कुन दिशामा गइरहेको छ, त्यही निर्णय गर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: & — address of
items.ne: & — ठेगाना लिने

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: * — value at
items.ne: * — ठेगानाको मान

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Neither
items.ne: दुवै होइन

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: A pointer stores an address, so the address of n has to be taken out of n before it can be stored. The ampersand is the only operator that produces an address, and this line is the standard way to aim a pointer.
items.ne: Pointer ले ठेगाना राख्छ, त्यसैले भण्डारण गर्नुअघि n बाट n को ठेगाना निकाल्नुपर्छ। ठेगाना निकाल्ने एकमात्र operator ampersand हो, र pointer लाई तेर्स्याउने मानक तरिका यही लाइन हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: The pointer holds an address, and printing the value stored there means following the pointer first. The star does that following, which is what dereferencing means and why it is read as value at.
items.ne: Pointer सँग ठेगाना छ, र त्यहाँको मान छाप्न पहिले pointer पछ्याउनुपर्छ। Star ले त्यही पछ्याउँछ — dereference को अर्थ त्यही हो, र यसलाई "ठेगानाको मान" भनेर पढिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: One element of an array is an ordinary int variable, so scanf still needs its address. The array name alone is already an address, but a single element written with brackets is not, and this trips students.
items.ne: Array को एउटा element सामान्य int variable जस्तै हो, त्यसैले scanf लाई यसको ठेगाना चाहिन्छ। Array को नाम मात्र भए ठेगाना हुन्छ, तर कोष्ठकसहितको एउटा element हुँदैन — यहीँ विद्यार्थी अल्झिन्छन्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: An array name already is the address of its first element, so writing an ampersand in front of it is unnecessary here. This is the one scanf in the subject that takes no ampersand, and it is asked about often.
items.ne: Array को नाम आफैंमा पहिलो element को ठेगाना हो, त्यसैले यहाँ अगाडि ampersand लेख्नु आवश्यक छैन। विषयभरिमा ampersand नचाहिने scanf यही हो, र यसबारे बारम्बार सोधिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Inside the function a holds an address, so the value living at that address is reached with the star. Writing t = a would copy the address into an int instead, and the swap would then exchange nothing.
items.ne: Function भित्र a सँग ठेगाना छ, त्यसैले त्यो ठेगानामा भएको मानसम्म star ले पुगिन्छ। t = a लेखे ठेगाना नै int मा सर्थ्यो, र swap ले केही साट्दैनथ्यो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.3 Referencing and dereferencing — Referencing र dereferencing
items.en: Two variables, each at its own address. The arrow is not stored anywhere — it is drawn from the value inside p to the location of n, which is exactly what a pointer is.
items.ne: दुई variable, हरेक आफ्नै ठेगानामा। तीर कतै भण्डारण हुँदैन — यो p भित्रको मान बाट n को स्थान सम्म कोरिएको हो, र pointer भनेकै त्यही हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: Give the advantages of pointers, and name the two places in this subject you have already relied on one.
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा: pointer भनेको के हो र यसले मानको ठाउँमा के राख्छ भन्न, pointer variable घोषणा गरेर कुनै variable तिर तेर्स्याउन, & र * चलाउन अनि हरेक कुन दिशामा काम गर्छ भन्न, pointer मार्फत variable बदल्ने प्रोग्राम पढेर output अनुमान गर्न, र pointer का फाइदा दिन अनि यसै विषयमा तपाईंले पहिल्यै दुई ठाउँमा pointer मा भर परिसक्नुभएको छ भन्ने देखाउन सक्नुहुनेछ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: The lightest unit on paper, and not a light unit. Four of the 64 theory hours and 2 of the 50 external marks — less than any other unit. Seven practical hours, though, and two topics you have already met: the & in every scanf since Unit 2, and the whole of call by reference in Unit 4. This unit names what you have been using.
items.ne: कागजमा सबैभन्दा हलुका, तर हलुका युनिट होइन। ६४ मध्ये चार घण्टा र ५० मध्ये २ अंक — अरू कुनै युनिटभन्दा कम। तर प्रयोगात्मक सात घण्टा छन्, र तपाईंले पहिल्यै भेटिसकेका दुई विषय पनि: युनिट २ देखि हरेक scanf मा आएको &, र युनिट ४ को पूरै call by reference। यस युनिटले तपाईंले चलाइरहेकै कुरालाई नाम दिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.3 Referencing and dereferencing — Referencing र dereferencing
items.en: Option C confuses p with *p. Printing p would show an address; printing n or *p shows 10. One star is the whole difference.
items.ne: १०। *p = *p + 3; लाई "p को ठेगानाको मान बराबर p को ठेगानाको मान जोड तीन" भनेर पढ्नुहोस्। P को ठेगानाको मान नै n हो, त्यसैले यो n = n + 3 कै अर्को लेखाइ हो। विकल्प (क) यस युनिटले हटाउन खोजेकै विश्वास हो: कसैसँग ठेगाना छ भने नाम नलिने लाइनले पनि variable बदल्न सक्छ। यो जादू होइन — युनिट २ देखि scanf("%d", &n) ले गरिरहेकै काम हो, र युनिट ४ को call by reference ले गर्ने पनि त्यही। विकल्प (ग) ले p र *p मिसाउँछ। p छापे ठेगाना देखिन्थ्यो; n वा *p छापे १०। पूरै फरक एउटा star को हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.4 Advantages of pointers — Pointer का फाइदा
items.en: Three of the four printf lines below are easy. Decide what &p prints and why it is different from p.
items.ne: तलका चार printf मध्ये तीन सजिलो छन्। &p ले के छाप्छ र p भन्दा किन फरक हुन्छ, निर्णय गर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.4 Advantages of pointers — Pointer का फाइदा
items.en: Lines 2 and 3 print the same number, which is the point: p's value is n's address. Line 5 prints a different one, because p is itself a variable living somewhere of its own. And the last two lines are the unit in miniature — a line that does not mention n changes n.
items.ne: दोस्रो र तेस्रो लाइनले उही सङ्ख्या छाप्छन्, र मुख्य कुरा त्यही हो: p को मान नै n को ठेगाना हो। पाँचौंले फरक छाप्छ, किनभने p आफैं कतै बस्ने variable हो। अन्तिम दुई लाइन पूरै युनिटको सानो रूप हुन् — n को नाम नलिने लाइनले n बदल्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.4 Advantages of pointers — Pointer का फाइदा
items.en: Three things in that output are not promised. The addresses change on every run. The shape of them belongs to the compiler's library: gcc on Linux writes an address as 0x7ffd1a2b3c4c, and MinGW gcc on Windows writes the same kind of address as 000000F7EBBFF74C — sixteen digits, upper case, no 0x. And whether p sits above or below n is the compiler's business: when this listing was run on Windows to check it, p turned out to be twelve bytes below n. What is promised is the relationship — lines 2 and 3 equal, line 5 different. The (void *) before each address is there because %p is defined to take a void *; most textbooks write printf("%p", &n) and most compilers accept it, but gcc -Wall will tell you about it.
items.ne: त्यो output का तीन कुराको वाचा छैन। ठेगाना हरेक पटक फेरिन्छ। त्यसको रूप compiler को library को कुरा हो: Linux को gcc ले 0x7ffd1a2b3c4c लेख्छ, Windows को MinGW gcc ले उही किसिमको ठेगानालाई 000000F7EBBFF74C लेख्छ — सोह्र अङ्क, ठूलो अक्षर, 0x छैन। र p, n भन्दा माथि बस्छ कि तल — त्यो compiler को कुरा हो: यो listing जाँच्न Windows मा चलाउँदा p, n भन्दा बाह्र byte तल निस्कियो। वाचा भएको कुरा सम्बन्ध हो — दोस्रो र तेस्रो लाइन बराबर, पाँचौं फरक। हरेक ठेगानाअघिको (void *) त्यहाँ छ किनभने %p ले void * लिने परिभाषा छ; धेरै पाठ्यपुस्तक printf("%p", &n) लेख्छन् र धेरै compiler ले मान्छन्, तर gcc -Wall ले यसबारे भनिदिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.4 Advantages of pointers — Pointer का फाइदा
items.en: Answer it in one sentence before opening this, using the word "address" twice.
items.ne: खोल्नुअघि "ठेगाना" शब्द दुई पटक प्रयोग गरेर एक वाक्यमा उत्तर दिनुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.4 Advantages of pointers — Pointer का फाइदा
items.en: Nothing in this program is new. The only thing that changed between Unit 2 and now is that you can say why — and that sentence is what a two-mark question on pointers is actually asking for.

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.3 Referencing and dereferencing — Referencing र dereferencing
items.en: One case needs neither operator. An array name is already an address, which is why scanf("%s", name) takes no ampersand while scanf("%d", &n) does.
items.ne: एउटा केसमा कुनै पनि operator चाहिँदैन। Array को नाम आफैं ठेगाना हो — त्यसैले scanf("%s", name) लाई ampersand चाहिँदैन र scanf("%d", &n) लाई चाहिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.1 Introduction to pointers — Pointer को परिचय
items.en: Every variable lives somewhere, and the address is a value When you declare int n = 25;, two facts come into existence: n holds 25, and n lives at some address in memory. You have been using the first fact since Unit 2. The second is this unit. A pointer is a variable that stores the address of another variable. It is an ordinary variable in every respect — it has a type, it has a name, it lives at an address of its own — and what it holds happens to be a location rather than a quantity. The address a program sees is not fixed. Run the same program twice and n may be at a different address each time. That is why a program never writes an address down and always asks for it with &, and why the number 1000 in the figure below is an illustration and not a fact.
items.ne: हरेक variable कतै बस्छ, र ठेगाना आफैंमा एउटा मान हो int n = 25; घोषणा गर्दा दुई तथ्य जन्मन्छन्: n सँग २५ छ, र n मेमोरीको कुनै ठेगानामा बस्छ। पहिलो तथ्य तपाईंले युनिट २ देखि चलाइरहनुभएको छ। दोस्रो यही युनिट हो। Pointer भनेको अर्को variable को ठेगाना राख्ने variable हो। यो हरेक हिसाबले सामान्य variable नै हो — यसको प्रकार छ, नाम छ, आफ्नै ठेगाना छ — र यसले राख्ने कुरा परिमाण नभई स्थान हो। प्रोग्रामले देख्ने ठेगाना स्थिर हुँदैन। उही प्रोग्राम दुई पटक चलाउँदा n हरेक पटक फरक ठेगानामा हुन सक्छ। त्यसैले प्रोग्रामले ठेगाना कहिल्यै लेखेर राख्दैन, सधैं & ले सोध्छ — र तलको चित्रमा देखिने १००० सङ्ख्या उदाहरण हो, तथ्य होइन।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.2 Declaring a pointer variable — Pointer variable को घोषणा
items.en: The star in the declaration is part of the type int *p; declares p as "a pointer to an int". The star here is not the dereference operator — it is part of the type, and it is the one place in C where the same symbol means two different things a line apart. The type matters. int *p; and float *q; both hold an address, and the type tells the compiler how to interpret the bytes found there and how far one step is. A pointer with the wrong type gives nonsense, not an error. A declared pointer points at nothing useful until it is given an address: int *p; — p exists and holds garbage. Dereferencing it now is a genuine crash waiting to happen. p = &n; — p now holds n's address. int *p = &n; — both on one line, which is the safer habit. Print an address with %p. Printing it with %d does not fail loudly — it prints a number — but on a 64-bit machine an address is 8 bytes and an int is 4, so the number you see is only part of the address. Checked on gcc: printf("%d", &n) compiled with no message at all and printed 830470604 for an address whose real value was 0x9B659FF94C. gcc -Wall does warn about it.
items.ne: घोषणामा आउने star प्रकारकै भाग हो int *p; ले p लाई "int को pointer" घोषणा गर्छ। यहाँको star dereference operator होइन — यो प्रकारकै भाग हो, र C मा उही चिन्हले एक लाइनको फरकमा दुई फरक अर्थ दिने ठाउँ यही एक हो। प्रकारले फरक पार्छ। int *p; र float *q; दुवैले ठेगाना राख्छन्, र प्रकारले compiler लाई त्यहाँका byte कसरी पढ्ने अनि एक पाइला कति टाढा हो भन्छ। गलत प्रकारको pointer ले त्रुटि होइन, बेकारको नतिजा दिन्छ। घोषणा गरिएको pointer लाई ठेगाना नदिएसम्म यो काम लाग्ने कतै देखाउँदैन: int *p; — p छ र यसमा garbage छ। अहिले dereference गर्नु भनेको crash निम्त्याउनु हो। p = &n; — अब p सँग n को ठेगाना छ। int *p = &n; — दुवै एउटै लाइनमा, र सुरक्षित बानी यही हो। ठेगाना छाप्न %p चलाउनुहोस्। %d ले ठाडै असफल हुँदैन — एउटा सङ्ख्या छाप्छ — तर ६४-bit मेसिनमा ठेगाना ८ byte को हुन्छ र int ४ byte को, त्यसैले देखिने सङ्ख्या ठेगानाको अंश मात्र हो। gcc मा जाँचिएको: printf("%d", &n) कुनै सन्देशविनै compile भयो र 0x9B659FF94C ठेगानाको ठाउँमा 830470604 छाप्यो। gcc -Wall ले यसबारे चेतावनी दिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.3 Referencing and dereferencing — Referencing र dereferencing
items.en: Two operators, opposite directions Referencing — the address-of operator & takes a variable and gives its address. &n is "where n lives". Dereferencing — the value-at operator * takes an address and gives what is stored there. *p is "the value at the address in p". They undo each other: *(&n) is simply n. Reading them as English helps more than memorising them — "address of n", "value at p". The star works in both directions. printf("%d", *p); reads a value out through the pointer; *p = 50; writes a value in through it, and n changes although the line never mentions n. That second use is the whole of call by reference, and the whole of why pointers are treated with care.
items.ne: दुई operator, उल्टा दिशा Referencing — address-of operator & ले variable लिएर त्यसको ठेगाना दिन्छ। &n भनेको "n कहाँ बस्छ" हो। Dereferencing — value-at operator * ले ठेगाना लिएर त्यहाँ भएको कुरा दिन्छ। *p भनेको "p मा भएको ठेगानाको मान" हो। यी एकअर्कालाई उल्ट्याउँछन्: *(&n) भनेको n नै हो। कण्ठ गर्नुभन्दा अङ्ग्रेजीमा पढ्दा बढी सजिलो हुन्छ — "address of n", "value at p"। Star दुवै दिशामा चल्छ। printf("%d", *p); ले pointer मार्फत मान निकाल्छ; *p = 50; ले त्यसैमार्फत मान भित्र राख्छ, र लाइनले n को नाम नलिई पनि n बदलिन्छ। दोस्रो प्रयोग नै पूरै call by reference हो, र pointer लाई होसियारीसाथ चलाउनुपर्ने कारण पनि त्यही।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.topic: 7.4 Advantages of pointers — Pointer का फाइदा
items.en: Four, and you have used two already A function can change the caller's variables. This is call by reference, and it is the only way a function can hand back more than one answer. You met it in Unit 4; this unit is the explanation of how it worked. Arrays are passed without copying. An array name is already an address, so sending an array of a thousand elements to a function costs one address rather than a thousand copies — and it is why sorting inside a function changes the caller's array. Memory can be asked for while the program runs — dynamic memory allocation, with malloc and free. It is how a program handles a list whose size nobody knew when it was written. Not on the Grade 9 syllabus; named here because it is the reason pointers matter in Grade 10 and beyond. Data structures become possible. A linked list, a tree and a graph are built out of items that hold the address of the next item. Without pointers there is no way to write one, which is where Grade 10 Unit 1 begins. The cost, stated honestly: a pointer that holds a wrong address will read or write somewhere it should not, and C will not stop it. Power and risk are the same property seen from two sides.
items.ne: चार, र तपाईंले दुई त चलाइसक्नुभयो Function ले बोलाउनेका variable बदल्न सक्छ। यही call by reference हो, र function ले एकभन्दा बढी उत्तर फर्काउने एकमात्र उपाय यही हो। युनिट ४ मा भेट्नुभयो; यो युनिट त्यो कसरी चल्यो भन्ने व्याख्या हो। Array प्रतिलिपि नबनाई पठाइन्छ। Array को नाम आफैं ठेगाना हो, त्यसैले हजार element को array function लाई पठाउँदा हजार प्रतिलिपि होइन एउटा ठेगाना मात्र लाग्छ — र function भित्र क्रम मिलाउँदा बोलाउनेकै array बदलिनुको कारण पनि त्यही। प्रोग्राम चल्दै गर्दा मेमोरी माग्न सकिन्छ — dynamic memory allocation, malloc र free सहित। लेख्ने बेला आकार कसैलाई थाहा नभएको सूची प्रोग्रामले यसैगरी सम्हाल्छ। कक्षा ९ को पाठ्यक्रममा छैन; कक्षा १० र त्यसपछि pointer किन महत्त्वपूर्ण हुन्छ भन्ने कारण भएकाले यहाँ नाम लिइएको हो। Data structure सम्भव हुन्छन्। Linked list, tree र graph अर्को वस्तुको ठेगाना राख्ने वस्तुहरूबाट बन्छन्। Pointer नभए यी लेख्ने उपायै हुँदैन, र कक्षा १० को युनिट १ त्यहींबाट सुरु हुन्छ। लागत, इमानदारीसाथ: गलत ठेगाना बोकेको pointer ले नपुग्नुपर्ने ठाउँमा पढ्छ वा लेख्छ, र C ले रोक्दैन। शक्ति र जोखिम एउटै गुणलाई दुई तिरबाट हेरेको हो।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: · चरणबद्ध हेर्नुहोस् A pointer holds an address, not a value What you will learn: that p and *p are two different things on the same line, and that writing through a pointer changes a variable the line never names. The last two steps are the ones that matter. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: एउटै लाइनमा p र *p दुई फरक कुरा हुन्, र pointer मार्फत लेख्दा लाइनले नाम नै नलिएको variable बदलिन्छ। महत्त्वपूर्ण चरण अन्तिम दुई हुन्। How to use this Read the four variable rows as two pairs: what n is and where n is, then what p holds and what is at that place. The last step changes n through the second pair alone. चारै पङ्क्तिलाई दुई जोडी बनाएर पढ्नुहोस्: n के हो र n कहाँ छ, अनि p सँग के छ र त्यो ठाउँमा के छ। अन्तिम चरणले दोस्रो जोडीबाटै n बदल्छ। Practise the judgement
items.ne: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: · निर्णय अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् Which pointer operator is needed here? What you will learn: to decide between & and * from the direction the line is travelling — taking an address out, or taking a value out of an address. तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: लाइन कुन दिशामा गइरहेको छ हेरेर & र * छुट्याउन — ठेगाना निकालेको, कि ठेगानाबाट मान निकालेको। How to use this One case needs neither operator. An array name is already an address, which is why scanf("%s", name) takes no ampersand while scanf("%d", &n) does. एउटा केसमा कुनै पनि operator चाहिँदैन। Array को नाम आफैं ठेगाना हो — त्यसैले scanf("%s", name) लाई ampersand चाहिँदैन र scanf("%d", &n) लाई चाहिन्छ। Predict first
items.ne: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस्

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en: · पहिले अनुमान गर्नुहोस् After int n = 7; int *p = &n; *p = *p + 3; what does printf("%d", n); print? int n = 7; int *p = &n; *p = *p + 3; पछि printf("%d", n); ले के छाप्छ? 7 — n was never assigned to 10 An address, because p was involved 10. Read *p = *p + 3; as "the value at p becomes the value at p plus three". The value at p is n, so this is n = n + 3 written another way. Option A is the belief this unit exists to remove: a variable can be changed by a line that does not name it, provided something holds its address. That is not a trick — it is exactly what scanf("%d", &n) has been doing since Unit 2, and what call by reference does in Unit 4. Option C confuses p with *p. Printing p would show an address; printing n or *p shows 10. One star is the whole difference. १०। *p = *p + 3; लाई "p को ठेगानाको मान बराबर p को ठेगानाको मान जोड तीन" भनेर पढ्नुहोस्। P को ठेगानाको मान नै n हो, त्यसैले यो n = n + 3 कै अर्को लेखाइ हो। विकल्प (क) यस युनिटले हटाउन खोजेकै विश्वास हो: कसैसँग ठेगाना छ भने नाम नलिने लाइनले पनि variable बदल्न सक्छ। यो जादू होइन — युनिट २ देखि scanf("%d", &n) ले गरिरहेकै काम हो, र युनिट ४ को call by reference ले गर्ने पनि त्यही। विकल्प (ग) ले p र *p मिसाउँछ। p छापे ठेगाना देखिन्थ्यो; n वा *p छापे १०। पूरै फरक एउटा star को हो। 7.4 Advantages of pointers
items.ne: — Pointer का फाइदा

items.subject: grade9/c-programming
items.en:
Three of the four printf lines below are easy. Decide what &p prints and why it is different from p. तलका चार printf मध्ये तीन सजिलो छन्। &p ले के छाप्छ र p भन्दा किन फरक हुन्छ, निर्णय गर्नुहोस्। Working #include <stdio.h> int main() { int n = 25; int *p; p = &n; /* p now holds the address of n */ printf("Value of n : %d
", n); printf("Address of n : %p
", (void *) &n); printf("Value in p : %p
", (void *) p); /* same as &n */ printf("Value at p (*p) : %d
", *p); /* same as n */ printf("Address of p : %p
", (void *) &p); /* p's OWN address */ *p = 50; /* write through the pointer */ printf("n is now : %d
", n); return 0; } Output — the addresses here are illustrative; read the note Value of n : 25 Address of n : 0x7ffd1a2b3c4c Value in p : 0x7ffd1a2b3c4c Value at p (*p) : 25 Address of p : 0x7ffd1a2b3c40 n is now : 50 Lines 2 and 3 print the same number, which is the point: p's value is n's address. Line 5 prints a different one, because p is itself a variable living somewhere of its own. And the last two lines are the unit in miniature — a line that does not mention n changes n. दोस्रो र तेस्रो लाइनले उही सङ्ख्या छाप्छन्, र मुख्य कुरा त्यही हो: p को मान नै n को ठेगाना हो। पाँचौंले फरक छाप्छ, किनभने p आफैं कतै बस्ने variable हो। अन्तिम दुई लाइन पूरै युनिटको सानो रूप हुन् — n को नाम नलिने लाइनले n बदल्छ। Three things in that output are not promised. The addresses change on every run. The shape of them belongs to the compiler's library: gcc on Linux writes an address as 0x7ffd1a2b3c4c, and MinGW gcc on Windows writes the same kind of address as 000000F7EBBFF74C — sixteen digits, upper case, no 0x. And whether p sits above or below n is the compiler's business: when this listing was run on Windows to check it, p turned out to be twelve bytes below n. What is promised is the relationship — lines 2 and 3 equal, line 5 different. The (void *) before each address is there because %p is defined to take a void *; most textbooks write printf("%p", &n) and most compilers accept it, but gcc -Wall will tell you about it. त्यो output का तीन कुराको वाचा छैन। ठेगाना हरेक पटक फेरिन्छ। त्यसको रूप compiler को library को कुरा हो: Linux को gcc ले 0x7ffd1a2b3c4c लेख्छ, Windows को MinGW gcc ले उही किसिमको ठेगानालाई 000000F7EBBFF74C लेख्छ — सोह्र अङ्क, ठूलो अक्षर, 0x छैन। र p, n भन्दा माथि बस्छ कि तल — त्यो compiler को कुरा हो: यो listing जाँच्न Windows मा चलाउँदा p, n भन्दा बाह्र byte तल निस्कियो। वाचा भएको कुरा सम्बन्ध हो — दोस्रो र तेस्रो लाइन बराबर, पाँचौं फरक। हरेक ठेगानाअघिको (void *) त्यहाँ छ किनभने %p ले void * लिने परिभाषा छ; धेरै पाठ्यपुस्तक printf("%p", &n) लेख्छन् र धेरै compiler ले मान्छन्, तर gcc -Wall ले यसबारे भनिदिन्छ। Example 2 The scanf you have been writing since Unit 2 Question: explain, using this unit's vocabulary, why scanf needs &n for an int and nothing for a char array. Answer it in one sentence before opening this, using the word "address" twice. खोल्नुअघि "ठेगाना" शब्द दुई पटक प्रयोग गरेर एक वाक्यमा उत्तर दिनुहोस्। Working #include <stdio.h> int main() { int n; char name[20]; scanf("%d", &n); /* & REQUIRED : n is an ordinary int */ scanf("%s", name); /* no & : the array name IS an */ /* address already */ printf("%d %s", n, name); return 0; } WHY scanf NEEDS AN ADDRESS AT ALL Arguments in C are passed BY VALUE, so a function receives copies. scanf has to change the caller's variable, and it cannot change a copy. It therefore takes the ADDRESS and writes through it — which is call by reference, and which is this unit. WHY THE ARRAY TAKES NO AMPERSAND An array name used on its own already IS the address of its first element. Writing &name is asking for the address of something that is one, which is not what scanf wants here. printf TAKES NEITHER printf only READS its arguments, so copies are enough and no address is needed. Nothing in this program is new. The only thing that changed between Unit 2 and now is that you can say why — and that sentence is what a two-mark question on pointers is actually asking for. यस प्रोग्राममा नयाँ केही छैन। युनिट २ देखि अहिलेसम्म बदलिएको एउटै कुरा हो — अब तपाईं किन भन्न सक्नुहुन्छ। Pointer बारे दुई अंकको प्रश्नले साँच्चै खोज्ने वाक्य त्यही हो। Mistakes that cost marks here Confusing p with *p. One is an address, the other is the value there. Thinking the star in int *p; dereferences. There it is part of the type; it only dereferences in a statement. Dereferencing a pointer that was never given an address. It holds garbage, and the program crashes. Writing p = n; instead of p = &n;. That stores a value where an address belongs. Putting & before an array name. The name is already the address of the first element. Quoting a specific address as a fact. It changes every run; say "the address of n", never "1000". p र *p मिसाउनु: एउटा ठेगाना, अर्को त्यहाँको मान। int *p; को star ले dereference गर्छ भन्ठान्नु: त्यहाँ त्यो प्रकारको भाग हो; dereference statement मा मात्र गर्छ। ठेगाना नदिइएको pointer dereference गर्नु: त्यसमा garbage हुन्छ र प्रोग्राम crash हुन्छ। p = &n; को ठाउँमा p = n; लेख्नु: ठेगाना चाहिने ठाउँमा मान राखिन्छ। Array को नाम अगाडि & राख्नु: नाम आफैं पहिलो element को ठेगाना हो। कुनै निश्चित ठेगानालाई तथ्य भन्नु: त्यो हरेक पटक बदलिन्छ; "n को ठेगाना" भन्नुहोस्, "१०००" कहिल्यै होइन। Memory hook — & asks "where?", * asks "what's there?" Address out, value out — opposite directions. सम्झने तरिका — & ले "कहाँ?" सोध्छ, * ले "त्यहाँ के छ?" ठेगाना बाहिर, मान बाहिर — उल्टा दिशा। Practical work — this unit's other 7 hours

items.en: What you will learn: that p and *p are two different things on the same line, and that writing through a pointer changes a variable the line never names. The last two steps are the ones that matter.
items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: एउटै लाइनमा p र *p दुई फरक कुरा हुन्, र pointer मार्फत लेख्दा लाइनले नाम नै नलिएको variable बदलिन्छ। महत्त्वपूर्ण चरण अन्तिम दुई हुन्।

items.subject: grade9/c-programming

items.ne: तपाईंले के सिक्नुहुन्छ: लाइन कुन दिशामा गइरहेको छ हेरेर & र * छुट्याउन — ठेगाना निकालेको, कि ठेगानाबाट मान निकालेको।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: A calculator is electronic, has a screen and does arithmetic, so none of those separates the two. What it cannot do is hold the whole list of steps — the program — and carry it out without a person pressing each key. That is why "stored instructions" is in the definition.
items.ne: क्यालकुलेटर पनि इलेक्ट्रोनिक छ, पर्दा छ र गणना गर्छ — त्यसैले ती कुनैले दुईलाई छुट्याउँदैनन्। उसले नसक्ने कुरा हो चरणहरूको पूरै सूची — प्रोग्राम — राखेर हरेक बटन मान्छेले नथिचिकनै चलाउनु। परिभाषामा "भण्डारण गरिएका निर्देशन" त्यसैले छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Data is the raw figures that mean little on their own. Information is what comes out after processing, in a form a person can use. The direction is always the same: data goes in, information comes out, and the processing in between is the computer's job.
items.ne: Data भनेको आफैंमा थोरै अर्थ राख्ने कच्चा अंक हो। Information भनेको प्रशोधनपछि निस्कने, मान्छेले काम लगाउन सक्ने रूप हो। दिशा सधैं उही: data भित्र, information बाहिर, र बीचको प्रशोधन कम्प्युटरको काम।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Accuracy means the machine does not make arithmetic mistakes, and here it did not — it averaged exactly what it was given. Garbage In, Garbage Out: correctness of the answer depends on the data you supply. Writing "the computer is not accurate" is the usual way marks are lost on this question.
items.ne: शुद्धताको अर्थ मेसिनले गणनामा गल्ती गर्दैन भन्ने हो, र यहाँ गरेन — दिइएकै कुराको ठ्याक्कै औसत निकाल्यो। Garbage In, Garbage Out: उत्तर सही हुनु तपाईंले दिएको data मा भर पर्छ। "कम्प्युटर शुद्ध छैन" लेख्नु नै यस प्रश्नमा अंक गुमाउने सामान्य तरिका हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: It measures a continuously changing quantity, which is analog, and then works in counted digits, which is digital. A machine doing both is hybrid. "Special purpose" is true of the pump but answers a different basis of classification — the question names data handling.
items.ne: यसले निरन्तर बदलिने परिमाण नाप्छ — त्यो analog — अनि गनिने अङ्कमा काम गर्छ — त्यो digital। दुवै गर्ने मेसिन hybrid हो। "Special purpose" पम्पका लागि सही भए पनि वर्गीकरणको अर्कै आधारको उत्तर हो; प्रश्नले डाटा ह्यान्डलिङ भनेको छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Five bases: size, data handling, purpose, model and brand. "By size" is about capacity — how much work the machine handles at once — which is why a supercomputer is in that class even though a mainframe may take up more room. Physical shape is the MODEL basis, not size.
items.ne: पाँच आधार: आकार, डाटा ह्यान्डलिङ, प्रयोजन, मोडेल र ब्रान्ड। "आकार अनुसार" भनेको क्षमता हो — मेसिनले एकैपटक कति काम थाम्छ — त्यसैले ठाउँ बढी ओगट्ने mainframe भए पनि supercomputer त्यही वर्गमा पर्छ। भौतिक आकार भनेको MODEL को आधार हो, size को होइन।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Built for one job and not reprogrammable is the definition of special purpose. It is also a microcomputer and a digital computer — every machine has an answer on all five bases at once, and the question tells you which basis it is asking about.
items.ne: एउटै कामका लागि बनेको र नयाँ प्रोग्राम हाल्न नमिल्ने — special purpose को परिभाषा यही हो। यो microcomputer र digital कम्प्युटर पनि हो; हरेक मेसिनसँग पाँचै आधारको उत्तर एकैचोटि हुन्छ, र प्रश्नले कुन आधार सोधेको हो भन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Diligence is the absence of boredom and tiredness: a computer does not lose concentration over a long run of repeated work, which a person would. Speed is about how fast, not how consistently.
items.ne: लगनशीलता भनेको दिक्क नलाग्नु र नथाक्नु हो: लामो दोहोरिने कामले कम्प्युटरको ध्यान भंग हुँदैन, जुन मान्छेको हुन्छ। गति भनेको कति छिटो भन्ने हो, कति एकनासले भन्ने होइन।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Input brings data in and output sends information out; neither keeps anything. Storage is the fourth stage of the definition, and it holds the stored program as well as the data — which is the feature that makes the machine a computer rather than a calculator.
items.ne: Input ले data भित्र ल्याउँछ, output ले information बाहिर पठाउँछ; दुवैले केही राख्दैनन्। Storage परिभाषाको चौथो चरण हो, र यसले data सँगै भण्डारण गरिएको प्रोग्राम पनि राख्छ — यही विशेषताले मेसिनलाई क्यालकुलेटर होइन कम्प्युटर बनाउँछ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Record keeping, test results and billing inside a hospital are all the health application area. The exam usually gives you a setting and asks for the field, or gives the field and asks for two uses — so learn each area with one Nepali example you could defend.
items.ne: अस्पतालभित्रको रेकर्ड राख्ने काम, जाँचको नतिजा र बिलिङ — सबै स्वास्थ्य प्रयोग क्षेत्रका हुन्। परीक्षाले प्रायः ठाउँ दिएर क्षेत्र सोध्छ, वा क्षेत्र दिएर दुई प्रयोग सोध्छ — त्यसैले हरेक क्षेत्रसँग एउटा नेपाली उदाहरण सम्झनुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Working all morning without tiring or losing care is diligence. Doing three unlike jobs on one machine is versatility. Speed and accuracy are true of the machine too, but nothing in this situation demonstrates them — the question asks which the situation SHOWS, not which the computer has.
items.ne: बिहानभरि नथाकी, ध्यान नघटाई काम गर्नु लगनशीलता हो। एउटै मेसिनमा तीन फरक काम गर्नु बहुउपयोगिता। गति र शुद्धता पनि मेसिनमा छन्, तर यो परिस्थितिले ती देखाउँदैन — प्रश्नले परिस्थितिले के देखाउँछ भनेको छ, कम्प्युटरसँग के छ भनेको होइन।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Accuracy is a claim about PROCESSING, not about the data. Given 950, the machine handled 950 correctly — which is exactly what accuracy means, and exactly why a wrong output does not disprove it. Option 3 is the tempting one: a program COULD be written to reject a mark above the full marks, but that is a check someone chose to add, not something a computer does because it is a computer. The characteristic being tested here is accuracy, and the principle is Garbage In, Garbage Out.
items.ne: शुद्धता भनेको प्रशोधन बारेको दाबी हो, data बारेको होइन। ९५० दिइएपछि मेसिनले ९५० लाई ठिकसँग चलायो — शुद्धताको अर्थ यही हो, र गलत आउटपुटले यसलाई गलत साबित नगर्ने कारण पनि यही। तेस्रो विकल्प लोभ्याउने छ: पूर्णाङ्कभन्दा बढी अंक अस्वीकार गर्ने प्रोग्राम लेख्न सकिन्छ, तर त्यो कसैले थपेको जाँच हो, कम्प्युटर भएकै कारण हुने कुरा होइन। यहाँ जाँचिएको विशेषता शुद्धता हो, र सिद्धान्त Garbage In, Garbage Out।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: "Working principle" is the data-handling basis, so the answer must be analog, digital or hybrid — which rules out microcomputer (size) and special purpose (purpose) however true they are of the machine. Between the two that remain, digital is the trap: the machine does produce digital output, but it also MEASURES a smoothly changing signal, and doing both is the definition of hybrid. The general lesson is to read which basis the question names before looking at the machine at all.
items.ne: "Working principle" भनेको डाटा ह्यान्डलिङको आधार हो, त्यसैले उत्तर analog, digital वा hybrid मध्ये हुनैपर्छ — यसले microcomputer (आकार) र special purpose (प्रयोजन) लाई हटाइदिन्छ, ती मेसिनका लागि जति नै सत्य भए पनि। बाँकी दुईमध्ये digital पासो हो: मेसिनले digital आउटपुट त दिन्छ, तर बिस्तारै बदलिने सङ्केत नाप्छ पनि, र दुवै गर्नु नै hybrid को परिभाषा हो। पाठ यो हो — मेसिन हेर्नुअघि प्रश्नले कुन आधार तोकेको छ पढ्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Data and information are not the same word. Data is raw and on its own means little: 72, 65, 88. Information is data that has been processed into something a person can use: "the class average is 75". The computer's whole job is turning the first into the second — which is why the definition names both.
items.ne: Data र information उस्तै शब्द होइनन्। Data कच्चा हुन्छ र आफैंमा थोरै अर्थ राख्छ: ७२, ६५, ८८। Information भनेको प्रशोधन भइसकेको, मान्छेले काम लगाउन सक्ने कुरा हो: "कक्षाको औसत ७५ छ"। कम्प्युटरको पूरै काम पहिलोलाई दोस्रो बनाउनु हो — त्यसैले परिभाषामा दुवैको नाम आउँछ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Saying a computer is "not accurate" when the output is wrong. If the input was wrong, that is GIGO. Accuracy describes the machine's arithmetic, not your typing.
items.ne: आउटपुट गलत हुँदा कम्प्युटर "शुद्ध छैन" भन्नु। इनपुट गलत थियो भने त्यो GIGO हो। शुद्धताले मेसिनको गणना जनाउँछ, तपाईंको टाइपिङ होइन।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Which basis of classification?
items.ne: कुन आधारको वर्गीकरण हो?

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Each case names a category, or describes a machine. Decide which of the five bases it answers. Ask what QUESTION the word is answering — how big, what signal, how many jobs, what shape, or who made it.
items.ne: हरेक केसमा कि एउटा वर्गको नाम छ, कि मेसिनको वर्णन। ती पाँच आधारमध्ये कुनको उत्तर हो छान्नुहोस्। त्यो शब्दले कुन प्रश्नको जवाफ दिँदै छ सोध्नुहोस् — कति ठूलो, कस्तो सङ्केत, कति काम, कस्तो आकार, कि कसले बनायो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Size
items.ne: आकार

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Data handling
items.ne: डाटा ह्यान्डलिङ

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Purpose
items.ne: प्रयोजन

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Model
items.ne: मोडेल

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Brand
items.ne: ब्रान्ड

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Supercomputer, mainframe, mini and micro all answer one question: how much work can it do at once. That is the size and power class — not the kind of signal, and not how many different jobs it was built for.
items.ne: Supercomputer, mainframe, mini र micro — चारैले एउटै प्रश्नको उत्तर दिन्छन्: एकैपटक कति काम गर्न सक्छ। यो आकार र क्षमताको वर्ग हो — सङ्केतको किसिम होइन, र कति फरक काम गर्न बनेको हो भन्ने पनि होइन।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Continuously changing means an ANALOG signal, and analog, digital and hybrid are the data-handling classes. The clue is always the signal: a measured quantity that slides smoothly is analog, counted 0s and 1s are digital.
items.ne: निरन्तर बदलिने भनेको ANALOG सङ्केत हो, र analog, digital, hybrid नै डाटा ह्यान्डलिङका वर्ग हुन्। सुराक सधैं सङ्केत नै हो: बिस्तारै सर्ने नापिने मान analog, गनिने ० र १ digital।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: One job only makes it special purpose; a machine you can load new programs onto is general purpose. It is also micro and digital — a computer sits in all five lists at once, and the question names which list it is asking about.
items.ne: एउटै काम गर्ने भएकाले special purpose; नयाँ प्रोग्राम हाल्न मिल्ने भए general purpose। यो micro र digital पनि हो — एउटै कम्प्युटर पाँचै सूचीमा एकैचोटि पर्छ, र प्रश्नले कुन सूची सोधेको हो त्यही नाम लिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Desktop, laptop and palmtop describe the physical form the machine is built in. A laptop is still a microcomputer, so answering size here would be true of the machine and still not answer the question that was asked.
items.ne: Desktop, laptop र palmtop ले मेसिन कस्तो भौतिक आकारमा बनेको छ भन्छन्। Laptop पनि microcomputer नै हो, त्यसैले यहाँ आकार भन्नु मेसिनका लागि सही भए पनि सोधिएको प्रश्नको उत्तर हुँदैन।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: IBM PC, IBM compatible and Apple say who built the machine or whose design it follows. Nothing about a brand tells you the size, the signal or the purpose, which is exactly why it is counted as a separate basis.
items.ne: IBM PC, IBM compatible र Apple ले मेसिन कसले बनायो वा कसको डिजाइन पछ्याउँछ भन्छन्। ब्रान्डले आकार, सङ्केत वा प्रयोजनबारे केही भन्दैन — त्यसैले यो छुट्टै आधार मानिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: It measures a continuous quantity and then works with counted digits, which is the definition of a HYBRID computer. Hybrid is the third data-handling class, and a question describing both kinds of signal in one machine is asking for it.
items.ne: यसले निरन्तर बग्ने परिमाण नाप्छ, अनि गनिने अङ्कसँग काम गर्छ — HYBRID कम्प्युटरको परिभाषा यही हो। Hybrid डाटा ह्यान्डलिङको तेस्रो वर्ग हो, र एउटै मेसिनमा दुवै किसिमको सङ्केत वर्णन गर्ने प्रश्नले यही खोज्दै छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Input → Process → Output, with storage underneath. "Define a computer with a block diagram" is a standard question, and this is the diagram it wants.
items.ne: Input → Process → Output, र मुनि storage। "ब्लक चित्रसहित कम्प्युटरको परिभाषा दिनुहोस्" भन्ने प्रश्न पटक–पटक आउँछ, र खोजिने चित्र यही हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Read the left column first. The exam names a basis and asks for its categories, or names a category and asks which basis it belongs to. The five bases are the curriculum's; the categories beside them are the usual textbook ones.
items.ne: पहिले बायाँ स्तम्भ पढ्नुहोस्। परीक्षाले कि आधार दिएर त्यसका वर्ग सोध्छ, कि वर्ग दिएर कुन आधारको हो सोध्छ। पाँच आधार पाठ्यक्रमका हुन्; छेउका वर्ग सामान्य पाठ्यपुस्तकका।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Place any computer you are shown into all five classifications at once.
items.ne: यो युनिट सकिँदा: कम्प्युटरलाई उसले डाटामाथि गर्ने कामबाट परिभाषित गर्न र त्यो चक्रका चार चरण नाम लिन, data र information को फरक उदाहरणसहित भन्न, कम्प्युटरका विशेषता भन्न र तीमध्ये कुन मेसिनको गुण हो (उत्तरको होइन) छुट्याउन, नेपालमा कम्प्युटरको प्रयोग कम्तीमा छ क्षेत्रमा देखाउन, वर्गीकरणका पाँच आधार र तिनका वर्ग नाम लिन, र देखाइएको जुनसुकै कम्प्युटरलाई पाँचै वर्गीकरणमा एकैपटक राख्न सक्नुहुनेछ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: No. It is electronic and it does process input into output, so it passes two parts of the test. What it cannot do is hold a list of instructions and follow them on its own — you press every key yourself. That is the line the definition draws, and it is why "stored instructions" is in it. A programmable scientific calculator sits much closer to the line, which is a fair thing to notice.
items.ne: होइन। यो इलेक्ट्रोनिक छ र इनपुटलाई आउटपुटमा बदल्छ पनि, त्यसैले जाँचका दुई भाग पास गर्छ। तर निर्देशनको सूची राखेर आफैं पछ्याउन सक्दैन — हरेक बटन तपाईं आफैं थिच्नुहुन्छ। परिभाषाले कोर्ने रेखा यही हो, र "भण्डारण गरिएका निर्देशन" त्यसैले राखिएको हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: GIGO — the one that costs marks. "Accuracy" means the machine does not make arithmetic mistakes. It does not mean the answer is right. If you type a student's marks as 850 instead of 85, the computer will average 850 perfectly and hand you a wrong result. Garbage In, Garbage Out. Accuracy is a property of the machine; correctness is a property of the data you gave it.
items.ne: GIGO — यहीँ अंक जान्छ। "शुद्धता" भनेको मेसिनले गणनामा गल्ती गर्दैन भन्ने हो। उत्तर नै सही हुन्छ भनेको होइन। विद्यार्थीको अंक ८५ का साटो ८५० टाइप गर्नुभयो भने कम्प्युटरले ८५० लाई ठ्याक्कै सही औसत निकालिदिन्छ, र गलत नतिजा दिन्छ। Garbage In, Garbage Out. शुद्धता मेसिनको गुण हो; सहीपन तपाईंले दिएको data को गुण हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Two characteristics are in play and the question separates them. Decide which one the two seconds demonstrates, and which one the wrong answers do not touch, before you open this.
items.ne: दुई विशेषता खेलमा छन् र प्रश्नले तिनलाई छुट्याउँछ। दुई सेकेन्डले कुन देखाउँछ, र गलत उत्तरले कुनलाई छुँदैन — खोल्नुअघि निर्णय गर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: The marks lost here are usually lost by writing "this shows the computer is not accurate". It is accurate — it averaged exactly what it was given. The example is GIGO, and naming GIGO is what earns the mark.
items.ne: यहाँ अंक प्रायः "यसले कम्प्युटर शुद्ध छैन भन्ने देखाउँछ" लेखेर जान्छ। ऊ शुद्ध छ — उसलाई दिइएकै कुराको ठ्याक्कै औसत निकाल्यो। यो उदाहरण GIGO हो, र GIGO नाम लिनुले नै अंक दिलाउँछ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: So the lists above are the standard textbook treatment, not quoted curriculum text. For size, data handling and purpose that distinction barely matters: every book and every paper uses the same categories. Model and brand are different. Books disagree about them, and IBM PC / IBM compatible / Apple is a convention from an older generation of computing that some teachers no longer use. Check these two against your own textbook and what your teacher writes on the board, and follow those if they differ from this page.
items.ne: पाठ्यक्रमले पाँच आधार मात्र नाम लिन्छ, त्यहीँ रोकिन्छ। विषय १.४ मा यसका ठ्याक्कै शब्द — "on the basis of size, on the data handling, on the purpose, on the model, on the brand" — र कुनै पनि आधारमुनि कुनै वर्ग लेखिएको छैन। त्यसैले माथिका सूची मानक पाठ्यपुस्तकको प्रचलन हुन्, पाठ्यक्रमकै उद्धरण होइनन्। आकार, डाटा ह्यान्डलिङ र प्रयोजनमा यो फरकले खासै अर्थ राख्दैन — सबै पुस्तक र सबै प्रश्नपत्रले उही वर्ग चलाउँछन्। मोडेल र ब्रान्ड भने फरक हुन्। पुस्तकहरूबीच मत बाझिन्छ, र IBM PC / IBM compatible / Apple पुरानो पुस्ताको प्रचलन हो, जुन कतिपय शिक्षकले अहिले चलाउनुहुन्न। यी दुईलाई आफ्नै पाठ्यपुस्तक र शिक्षकले बोर्डमा लेख्नुभएकोसँग मिलाएर हेर्नुहोस्, र फरक परे त्यही मान्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Case 3 is the one worth reading the reason for even if you get it right. The washing machine is also micro and also digital — more than one answer is true of the machine, and only one answers the question asked.
items.ne: केही थिच्नुअघि यो केसले कुन प्रश्नको उत्तर दिँदै छ भन्नुहोस्। कति काम? आकार। कस्तो सङ्केत? डाटा ह्यान्डलिङ। कति फरक काम? प्रयोजन। कस्तो आकार? मोडेल। कसले बनायो? ब्रान्ड। केस ३ को कारण सही भए पनि पढ्नुहोस्: वासिङ मेसिन micro पनि हो, digital पनि — मेसिनका लागि एकभन्दा बढी उत्तर सही हुन्छन्, तर सोधिएको प्रश्नको उत्तर एउटै हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Work down the five bases in order and answer each one separately. Write your five answers before opening this.
items.ne: पाँच आधार क्रमैसँग लिनुहोस् र हरेकको छुट्टै उत्तर दिनुहोस्। खोल्नुअघि आफ्ना पाँच उत्तर लेख्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: One machine, five answers, none of them competing. A question that gives you a machine and asks for "the classification" is asking for all five unless it names a basis.
items.ne: एउटै मेसिन, पाँच उत्तर, कुनै पनि एकअर्कासँग बाझिँदैनन्। मेसिन दिएर "वर्गीकरण" सोध्ने प्रश्नले आधार नतोकेसम्म पाँचै खोजेको हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Mixing the five bases into one list. "Supercomputer, digital, laptop" is not a classification — it is one answer from each of three different questions.
items.ne: पाँच आधारलाई एउटै सूचीमा मिसाउनु। "Supercomputer, digital, laptop" वर्गीकरण होइन — यी तीन फरक प्रश्नका एक–एक उत्तर हुन्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Calling a calculator a computer. It has no stored program; you press every key.
items.ne: क्यालकुलेटरलाई कम्प्युटर भन्नु। त्यसमा भण्डारण गरिएको प्रोग्राम छैन; हरेक बटन तपाईं थिच्नुहुन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Using "data" and "information" as the same word. Data goes in, information comes out; the processing in between is the difference.
items.ne: "Data" र "information" लाई उही शब्द ठान्नु। Data भित्र जान्छ, information बाहिर आउँछ; बीचको प्रशोधन नै फरक हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: These are the curriculum's own six for Unit 1, quoted from its practical list. The document calls them samples and says a teacher may set other work instead, as the student's need or the school's context requires — so treat this as what is expected of you unless your teacher says otherwise. The 10 hours are not a sample. They are the unit's practical allocation.
items.ne: यी युनिट १ का लागि पाठ्यक्रमकै छ वटा क्रियाकलाप हुन्, त्यसकै प्रयोगात्मक सूचीबाट लिइएका। पाठ्यक्रमले यिनलाई नमुना भनेको छ र विद्यार्थीको आवश्यकता वा विद्यालयको सन्दर्भअनुसार शिक्षकले अरू काम दिन सक्ने लेखेको छ — त्यसैले शिक्षकले अर्कै नभनेसम्म यही नै अपेक्षा हो भनी लिनुहोस्। १० घण्टा चाहिँ नमुना होइन — त्यो युनिटकै प्रयोगात्मक समय हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: You need: chart paper, markers, a ruler. Builds on: 1.1, the block diagram. Hand in: the chart, plus a photograph of it in your record file. Label input, process, output and storage — a chart that names the parts without naming the four stages is a picture, not a block diagram.
items.ne: चाहिन्छ: चार्ट पेपर, मार्कर, रुलर। आधार: १.१ को ब्लक चित्र। बुझाउने: चार्ट र त्यसको फोटो अभिलेख फाइलमा। input, process, output र storage नाम लेख्नुहोस् — चार चरण नलेखेको चार्ट ब्लक चित्र होइन, तस्बिर मात्र हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: You need: presentation software, or paper slides if no computer is free. Builds on: 1.2 and 1.3. Hand in: the file or the slides, and your speaking notes. For (b), use examples from Nepal — the ones in 1.3 are a starting list, not a limit.
items.ne: चाहिन्छ: प्रस्तुतीकरण सफ्टवेयर, वा कम्प्युटर खाली नभए कागजकै स्लाइड। आधार: १.२ र १.३। बुझाउने: फाइल वा स्लाइड, र बोल्ने नोट। (ख) का लागि नेपालकै उदाहरण लिनुहोस् — १.३ को सूची सुरुवात हो, सीमा होइन।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: You need: a prepared speech and a class audience — this one is organised by your teacher. Builds on: 1.3. Hand in: your written speech in your record file. Your own school is the strongest example you have.
items.ne: चाहिन्छ: तयार गरेको भाषण र कक्षाका श्रोता — यो शिक्षकले मिलाउनुहुन्छ। आधार: १.३। बुझाउने: लेखेको भाषण अभिलेख फाइलमा। सबैभन्दा बलियो उदाहरण तपाईंकै विद्यालय हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: You need: chart paper and markers. Builds on: 1.4 — working principle is the data handling basis: analog, digital, hybrid. Hand in: the chart. Give each type one real example; the fuel pump in the drill above is a hybrid one.
items.ne: चाहिन्छ: चार्ट पेपर, मार्कर। आधार: १.४ — working principle भनेको डाटा ह्यान्डलिङ को आधार हो: analog, digital, hybrid। बुझाउने: चार्ट। हरेक किसिमको एउटा वास्तविक उदाहरण दिनुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: You need: presentation software or paper slides. Builds on: 1.4. Hand in: the file and your notes. Weather forecasting at a Nepali met office is a supercomputer use worth naming; hospital and fuel-pump equipment are hybrid ones.
items.ne: चाहिन्छ: प्रस्तुतीकरण सफ्टवेयर वा कागजकै स्लाइड। आधार: १.४। बुझाउने: फाइल र नोट। नेपालको मौसम विभागको पूर्वानुमान supercomputer को उल्लेखनीय प्रयोग हो; अस्पताल र पेट्रोल पम्पका उपकरण hybrid।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: You need: presentation software or paper slides. Builds on: 1.4 — this covers all five bases between its three parts. Hand in: the file and your notes. Keep the three parts separate: merging the bases is the mistake the lesson warns about. The practical list writes mode in part (c) where the topic list for 1.4 writes model — the same basis, spelled two ways in the one document. Use model, and ask your teacher if an answer sheet says otherwise.
items.ne: चाहिन्छ: प्रस्तुतीकरण सफ्टवेयर वा कागजकै स्लाइड। आधार: १.४ — तीन भागले पाँचै आधार समेट्छन्। बुझाउने: फाइल र नोट। तीन भाग छुट्टै राख्नुहोस्; आधार मिसाउनु नै पाठले चेतावनी दिएको गल्ती हो। प्रयोगात्मक सूचीमा (ग) मा mode लेखिएको छ, तर १.४ को विषयसूचीमा model — एउटै आधार, एउटै कागजमा दुई हिज्जे। model नै प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: The curriculum adds two things worth knowing in advance. The practical examination is conducted in the presence of internal and external supervisors, and it assesses both the product and your skill in using equipment — so being able to explain your chart matters as much as the chart. And project work is assessed on the report and the presentation of it; when a project is presented by a group, every member submits their own short reflection on the report, so a group project is still individual work at the end.
items.ne: १८ प्रयोगात्मक अंकमध्ये ३ अंक अभिलेख का हुन्, काम गरेकै होइन। हरेक क्रियाकलापको अभिलेखमा हुनुपर्छ: क्रियाकलापको नम्बर र शीर्षक, मिति, के गर्नुभयो, के प्रयोग गर्नुभयो, के बनाउनुभयो (चार्ट भए फोटोसहित), र के सिक्नुभयो वा के बिग्रियो भन्ने एक–दुई वाक्य। सबै एउटै फाइलमा क्रम मिलाएर राख्नुहोस्। पाठ्यक्रमले थप्छ: प्रयोगात्मक परीक्षा आन्तरिक र बाह्य दुवै सुपरिवेक्षकको उपस्थितिमा हुन्छ, र त्यसले उत्पादनसँगै उपकरण चलाउने सीप पनि जाँच्छ — त्यसैले चार्ट बुझाउन सक्नु चार्ट बनाउनुजत्तिकै महत्त्वको छ। प्रोजेक्ट कामको मूल्याङ्कन रिपोर्ट र त्यसको प्रस्तुतीकरण मा हुन्छ; समूहमा प्रस्तुत गरेमा हरेक सदस्यले आफ्नै छोटो मनन् बुझाउनुपर्छ, त्यसैले समूहको प्रोजेक्ट पनि अन्ततः व्यक्तिगत काम हो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: Two. Find one wrong output you have actually seen — a bill, a result sheet, a mistyped name on a document. Decide whether the machine or the data was at fault, and write one sentence saying which and why. If it was the data, you have found a real GIGO example, and it will serve you better in the exam than the one in this lesson.
items.ne: पाठ्यक्रमको सूचीबाट होइन — माथिको सिद्धान्त हातमा टिक्छ कि टिक्दैन जाँच्ने छोटा अभ्यास। अंक छैन, शिक्षक चाहिँदैन। एक। बसेकै ठाउँबाट देखिने पाँच यन्त्र छान्नुहोस् — फोन, क्यालकुलेटर, टिभी, डिस्प्ले भएको फ्रिज, ल्यापटप। हरेकका लागि १.१ को परिभाषाअनुसार त्यसमा कम्प्युटर छ कि छैन भन्नुहोस्, र भए १.४ का पाँचै आधारमा राख्नुहोस्। जहाँ अलमल हुन्छ, त्यही फेरि पढ्ने ठाउँ हो। दुई। आफूले देखेको एउटा गलत आउटपुट सम्झनुहोस् — बिल, नतिजा, कागजमा बिग्रेको नाम। मेसिनको गल्ती थियो कि data को, एक वाक्यमा कारणसहित लेख्नुहोस्। Data को भए तपाईंले साँचो GIGO उदाहरण भेट्नुभयो।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: This unit carries 6 of the 50 external marks and 8 of the 64 theory hours. It is almost always asked as short definition questions and one classification question. The practical half of the unit — 10 hours of chart work and presentations — is assessed inside your school's internal 50 marks, not in the written paper.
items.ne: यो युनिटले बाह्य ५० मध्ये ६ अंक र ६४ सैद्धान्तिक घण्टामध्ये ८ घण्टा ओगट्छ। प्रायः छोटो परिभाषा प्रश्न र एउटा वर्गीकरण प्रश्नका रूपमा सोधिन्छ। युनिटको प्रयोगात्मक आधा भाग — चार्ट र प्रस्तुतीकरणका १० घण्टा — लिखित परीक्षामा होइन, विद्यालयभित्रको आन्तरिक ५० अंकमा मूल्याङ्कन हुन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Exam focus — what is asked from this unit
items.en: A computer accepts data, processes it by stored instructions, outputs information and stores both. The stored program is what a calculator lacks.

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: The definition, and why it is worded that way A computer is an electronic device that accepts data, processes it according to a set of stored instructions, produces information as output, and can store both for later use. Every part of that sentence is doing work. Electronic rules out an abacus. Stored instructions is the important one: a calculator also processes data, but you must press each key. A computer holds the whole list of steps — the program — inside itself and runs it without being told again at every step. The name is misleading. "Computer" means "one who computes", and calculation is only one of the things it does. It also stores, sorts, searches, compares, draws and communicates. Judge a machine by the four stages below, not by its name or its size.
items.ne: परिभाषा, र यसरी नै किन लेखिन्छ कम्प्युटर एउटा इलेक्ट्रोनिक उपकरण हो, जसले data लिन्छ, भण्डारण गरिएका निर्देशनअनुसार त्यसलाई प्रशोधन गर्छ, आउटपुटका रूपमा information दिन्छ, र दुवैलाई पछि प्रयोग गर्न राख्न सक्छ। यो वाक्यको हरेक भागको काम छ। इलेक्ट्रोनिक भनेपछि अबाकस बाहिरियो। सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण भण्डारण गरिएका निर्देशन हो: क्यालकुलेटरले पनि data प्रशोधन गर्छ, तर हरेक बटन तपाईंले थिच्नुपर्छ। कम्प्युटरले चरणहरूको पूरै सूची — अर्थात् प्रोग्राम — आफैंभित्र राख्छ र हरेक चरणमा फेरि नभनिकनै चलाउँछ। नाम भने अलमल्याउने खालको छ। "Computer" को अर्थ "गणना गर्ने" हो, तर गणना त उसले गर्ने धेरै काममध्ये एउटा मात्र हो। उसले राख्छ, क्रम मिलाउँछ, खोज्छ, तुलना गर्छ, कोर्छ र सञ्चार पनि गर्छ। मेसिनलाई नाम वा आकारले होइन, तलका चार चरणले जाँच्नुहोस्।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: What a computer is good at Speed — it works in millionths and billionths of a second. A task that would take a clerk a week can finish while you wait. Accuracy — it does not make mistakes in its own arithmetic. Diligence — it does not get bored or tired. The ten-thousandth calculation is done exactly as carefully as the first. Versatility — the same machine prints a bill, plays a song and checks spelling, because changing the program changes the job. Storage — it keeps very large amounts of data and finds any part of it again. Automation — once started, it carries out a whole job without a person at each step. Reliability — it gives the same answer to the same question every time.
items.ne: कम्प्युटर केमा राम्रो छ गति — ऊ सेकेन्डको दशलाख र अर्बौं भागमा काम गर्छ। कर्मचारीलाई हप्ता लाग्ने काम तपाईं पर्खिरहँदै सकिन्छ। शुद्धता — आफ्नै गणनामा ऊ गल्ती गर्दैन। लगनशीलता — ऊ दिक्क हुँदैन, थाक्दैन। दश हजारौं गणना पनि पहिलोजत्तिकै ध्यान दिएर हुन्छ। बहुउपयोगिता — उही मेसिनले बिल छाप्छ, गीत बजाउँछ र हिज्जे जाँच्छ, किनभने प्रोग्राम फेर्दा काम फेरिन्छ। भण्डारण — ऊ धेरै ठूलो मात्रामा data राख्छ र त्यसको जुनसुकै भाग फेरि भेट्टाउँछ। स्वचालन — एकपटक सुरु गरेपछि हरेक चरणमा मान्छे नचाहिने गरी पूरै काम सिध्याउँछ। भरपर्दोपन — उही प्रश्नको उत्तर उसले हरेक पटक उही दिन्छ।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Where computers are actually used in Nepal Education — school records and results, online classes, and the material you are reading now. Banking and money — accounts, ATMs, mobile banking, and the remittance that reaches a village from abroad in minutes rather than weeks. Government — citizenship and land records, the national ID, online passport applications, and tax filing. Health — patient records at a hospital or health post, laboratory machines, and telemedicine that lets a doctor in Kathmandu advise a health worker in a hill district. Communication — email, messaging and video calls. Transport and tourism — online bus and flight booking, and hotel systems. Weather and disaster warning — forecasting the monsoon and giving flood warning downstream, which in Nepal is a use that saves lives. Agriculture — market prices, weather advice and soil records reaching farmers by phone.
items.ne: नेपालमा कम्प्युटर साँच्चै कहाँ प्रयोग हुन्छ शिक्षा — विद्यालयको अभिलेख र नतिजा, अनलाइन कक्षा, र तपाईंले अहिले पढिरहेको यो सामग्री। बैंकिङ र पैसा — खाता, ATM, मोबाइल बैंकिङ, र विदेशबाट गाउँसम्म हप्तौंमा होइन मिनेटमै पुग्ने रेमिट्यान्स। सरकारी काम — नागरिकता र जग्गाको अभिलेख, राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र, अनलाइन राहदानी आवेदन, र कर दाखिला। स्वास्थ्य — अस्पताल र स्वास्थ्य चौकीमा बिरामीको अभिलेख, प्रयोगशालाका मेसिन, र काठमाडौंको डाक्टरले पहाडी जिल्लाको स्वास्थ्यकर्मीलाई सल्लाह दिन मिल्ने टेलिमेडिसिन। सञ्चार — इमेल, म्यासेज र भिडियो कल। यातायात र पर्यटन — अनलाइन बस र हवाई टिकट, होटेलका प्रणाली। मौसम र विपद् सूचना — मनसुनको पूर्वानुमान र तल्लो तटमा बाढीको चेतावनी — नेपालमा यो ज्यान बचाउने प्रयोग हो। कृषि — बजार भाउ, मौसमको सल्लाह र माटोको अभिलेख फोनबाटै किसानसम्म।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.en: Five questions, not one list Computers are classified on five different bases, and this is where the unit's marks usually are. The mistake to avoid is treating them as one long list. They are five separate questions, and every computer has an answer to all five at once. By size — supercomputer, mainframe, minicomputer, microcomputer. This asks how much work the machine can do at once. By data handling — analog, digital, hybrid. This asks what kind of signal it works with. Analog measures something that changes smoothly, like a voltage. Digital counts in 0s and 1s. Hybrid does both: a fuel pump measures flowing petrol and prints a digital bill. By purpose — general purpose (you can load new programs onto it) or special purpose (built for one job, like the computer in a washing machine). By model — the physical form: desktop, laptop, palmtop and similar. By brand — IBM PC, IBM compatible, Apple.
items.ne: पाँच प्रश्न, एउटै सूची होइन कम्प्युटरको वर्गीकरण पाँच फरक आधार मा हुन्छ, र यस युनिटका अंक प्रायः यहीँ हुन्छन्। बच्नुपर्ने गल्ती — यिनलाई एउटै लामो सूची ठान्नु। यी पाँच छुट्टाछुट्टै प्रश्न हुन्, र हरेक कम्प्युटरसँग पाँचैको उत्तर एकैचोटि हुन्छ। आकार अनुसार — supercomputer, mainframe, minicomputer, microcomputer। यसले मेसिनले एकैपटक कति काम गर्न सक्छ सोध्छ। डाटा ह्यान्डलिङ अनुसार — analog, digital, hybrid। यसले कस्तो सङ्केतसँग काम गर्छ सोध्छ। Analog ले बिस्तारै बदलिने कुरा नाप्छ, जस्तै भोल्टेज। Digital ले ० र १ मा गन्छ। Hybrid ले दुवै गर्छ: पेट्रोल पम्पले बग्ने पेट्रोल नाप्छ र digital बिल छाप्छ। प्रयोजन अनुसार — general purpose (नयाँ प्रोग्राम हाल्न मिल्ने) वा special purpose (एउटै कामका लागि बनेको, जस्तै वासिङ मेसिनभित्रको कम्प्युटर)। मोडेल अनुसार — भौतिक आकार: desktop, laptop, palmtop र यस्तै। ब्रान्ड अनुसार — IBM PC, IBM compatible, Apple।

items.subject: grade9/computer-fundamentals
items.topic: Practical work — this unit's other 10 hours
items.en: Why this section exists This unit is 18 hours, not 8. The 8 hours above are theory; the curriculum gives this unit 10 more hours of practical work, and lists six activities for them. Those activities are worth real marks. Of the 50 internal marks for this subject, 18 are practical work (15 for doing it, 3 for keeping records) and 12 are project work (10 for doing it, 2 for records). A further 5 are a viva in which you explain your own practical and project work. This website cannot do any of them for you. They are chart paper, presentations and a speech to your class. What it can do is tell you exactly what is required, what you need, and what to keep so that the marks are there when they are counted.
items.ne: यो खण्ड किन छ यो युनिट ८ होइन, १८ घण्टाको हो। माथिका ८ घण्टा सैद्धान्तिक हुन्; पाठ्यक्रमले यस युनिटलाई १० घण्टा प्रयोगात्मक काम दिएको छ, र त्यसका लागि छ वटा क्रियाकलाप तोकेको छ। ती क्रियाकलापका साँच्चिकै अंक छन्। यस विषयका ५० आन्तरिक अंकमध्ये १८ अंक प्रयोगात्मक काम (गर्नेको १५, अभिलेखको ३) र १२ अंक प्रोजेक्ट काम (गर्नेको १०, अभिलेखको २) हुन्। थप ५ अंक भाइभाका, जहाँ तपाईंले आफ्नै प्रयोगात्मक र प्रोजेक्ट काम बुझाउनुपर्छ। यी काम यो वेबसाइटले तपाईंका लागि गरिदिन सक्दैन। यी चार्ट पेपर, प्रस्तुतीकरण र कक्षामा बोल्ने काम हुन्। यसले गर्न सक्ने कुरा — के चाहिन्छ, के गर्नुपर्छ र के राख्नुपर्छ ठ्याक्कै बताउने, ताकि अंक गणना हुँदा ती तपाईंसँग होऊन्।
